0050ffd3-7d3a-4ffc-b0bb-b16ef879751c.title: Corduroy
0050ffd3-7d3a-4ffc-b0bb-b16ef879751c.summary: A teddy bear spends his days waiting in a store for someone to buy him

0093aca5-91cf-4198-835b-97ca2f657ae2.title: Sadie and the Snowman
0093aca5-91cf-4198-835b-97ca2f657ae2.summary: Join Sadie, a young girl who builds a snowman on a snowy winter day. As Sadie spends time with her snowman, she imagines all the adventures they'll have together. However, as the weather changes, Sadie faces a challenge that tests her creativity and determination.

01270a07-6ba6-5286-bd66-bb5e20eaa716.title: A Rover's Story
01270a07-6ba6-5286-bd66-bb5e20eaa716.summary: A Rover's Story is a 2022 middle-grade science-fiction novel by Jasmine Warga, with illustrations by Matt Rockefeller, published by Balzer + Bray. Resilience, called Res, is a Mars rover who begins to feel as the NASA engineers who build him talk to him, play him music and write his code. An Ohio sixth grader named Sophie, whose mother helped build him, names him and writes him letters as she grows up. Res travels to Jezero Crater on Mars with a drone friend, Fly, and a bossy satellite, Guardian, to search for signs of ancient life and for an older rover that has gone silent, and he disobeys orders to rescue Fly. Underneath, the book is about what it means to feel, to care about others when you are told feelings are useless, and to be changed by the people who made you. It was a New York Times bestseller and an ALA Notable Book.

018e0f83-3ea8-4919-adb4-e5593a5454f1.title: To the Lighthouse
018e0f83-3ea8-4919-adb4-e5593a5454f1.summary:
This story is divided into three parts. The first part, "The Window," introduces the Ramsay family and their guests at their summer home on the Isle of Skye in Scotland. The central figure is Mrs. Ramsay, a warm and nurturing matriarch, whose presence shapes the lives of those around her. The family plans a trip to the lighthouse, but it is postponed due to various obstacles.

In the second part, "Time Passes," the narrative shifts to a time of war, and the Ramsay family home is left empty and in disrepair. The passage of time is marked by the decay of the house and the landscape, as well as by the deaths and losses suffered by the characters.

The third part, "The Lighthouse," returns to the Ramsay family and their guests years later, as they finally embark on the long-awaited trip to the lighthouse. The journey becomes a metaphor for the characters' inner journeys, as they grapple with memories, regrets, and the passage of time.

01cd5e9f-c241-4b39-9a79-8962e72e98f4.title: Let It Go
01cd5e9f-c241-4b39-9a79-8962e72e98f4.summary: "Let It Go" is a song from Disney's 2013 computer-animated feature film Frozen, whose music and lyrics were composed by husband-and-wife songwriting team Robert Lopez and Kristen Anderson-Lopez. The song was performed in its original show-tune version in the film by American actress and singer Idina Menzel in her vocal role as Queen Elsa. It was later released as a single, being promoted to adult contemporary radio by Walt Disney Records in January 2014. Anderson-Lopez and Lopez also composed a simplified pop version which was performed by actress and singer Demi Lovato over the start of the film's closing credits. Disney's music division planned to release Lovato's version of the song before Menzel's, as they did not consider Menzel's version a traditional pop song. A music video was released separately for Lovato's version.

021e6048-6b8a-559d-9d33-961310a3270a.title: The Fault in Our Stars
021e6048-6b8a-559d-9d33-961310a3270a.summary: The Fault in Our Stars is a young adult novel by John Green, first published in January 2012 by Dutton. Sixteen-year-old Hazel Grace Lancaster has thyroid cancer that has spread to her lungs and cannot be cured. At a support group in Indianapolis she meets Augustus Waters, a seventeen-year-old in remission after losing a leg to cancer, and the two bond over books, above all Hazel's favorite novel, An Imperial Affliction, which ends abruptly. With help from a charity wish, they travel to Amsterdam to ask its reclusive author what happens next. Underneath, the book asks how to love and live well when time is short, and what a short life can mean. Kirkus praised its humor and sharp dialogue, it topped the New York Times children's chapter book list for seven weeks, and a film followed in 2014. The title comes from a line in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar.

02cd5835-63ba-5486-8021-fb6d1ec96972.title: A Little History of the World
02cd5835-63ba-5486-8021-fb6d1ec96972.year: 1936 (German original, Eine kurze Weltgeschichte fuer junge Leser; English Wikipedia says it appeared in 1936, German Wikipedia says 1935 - see dropped.md; first English edition 2005)
02cd5835-63ba-5486-8021-fb6d1ec96972.summary: A Little History of the World is a short history of humankind that E. H. Gombrich, later best known for The Story of Art, wrote in Vienna as a young man for young readers. In 40 short chapters it moves from the Stone Age and the first inventors through the ancient world, the founding of the great religions, the age of knights, revolutions and machines, to the world wars, and closes with Gombrich looking back on the part of history he lived through himself. It tells history as a story, so that readers can follow it without taking notes on names and dates. Underneath, it is about how people have lived together, fought and learned, and reviewers find tolerance, reason and humanity running through it. The Nazi regime banned it as too pacifistic. Yale University Press published the first English edition, translated by Caroline Mustill, in 2005; Kirkus gave it a star. Reviewers also note its Western point of view.

039a42e1-a9d4-4df8-a800-2e50e19ab17c.title: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer
039a42e1-a9d4-4df8-a800-2e50e19ab17c.summary:
The Adventures of Tom Sawyer is an 1876 novel by Mark Twain about a boy, Tom Sawyer, growing up along the Mississippi River. It is set in the 1840s in the town of St. Petersburg, which is based on Hannibal, Missouri, where Twain lived as a boy. In the novel, Sawyer has several adventures, often with his friend Huckleberry Finn. Originally a commercial failure, the book ended up being the best-selling of Twain's works during his lifetime.
Though overshadowed by its 1884 sequel, Adventures of Huckleberry Finn, the book is considered by many to be a masterpiece of American literature. It is alleged by Mark Twain to be one of the first novels to be written on a typewriter.

03c73983-5044-4442-bfb1-3b9f7ae74c17.title: Manhattan Project
03c73983-5044-4442-bfb1-3b9f7ae74c17.summary: "Manhattan Project" is a 1985 song by Canadian progressive rock band Rush, named after the WWII project that created the first atomic bomb. The song appeared on Rush's eleventh studio album Power Windows in 1985. "Manhattan Project" is the third track on the album and clocks in at 5:07. Despite not being released as a single, it did reach #10 on the U.S. Mainstream Rock Chart in January 1986.

045e4c93-7e3e-4884-83b1-e05ea39ae47d.title: Ten Little Bears: a counting rhyme
045e4c93-7e3e-4884-83b1-e05ea39ae47d.summary: Ten bear friends have different adventures as they play--until there is only one left

046a6e3a-0000-4205-9885-7d3ae6fe2348.title: The Berenstain Bears and Too Much Teasing
046a6e3a-0000-4205-9885-7d3ae6fe2348.summary: Brother Bear likes to tease his sister, but when he's the one who is taunted at school, he understands why Sister gets so mad.

04d7a0fe-84b6-4c1c-9111-f998bf9fd3e1.title: Kitten's First Full Moon
04d7a0fe-84b6-4c1c-9111-f998bf9fd3e1.summary: When Kitten mistakes the full moon for a bowl of milk, she ends up tired, wet, and hungry trying to reach it.

062c804a-ea93-453a-9eb8-cbbd97e8ce77.title: Today is Monday
062c804a-ea93-453a-9eb8-cbbd97e8ce77.summary: This book takes young readers on a journey through the days of the week. Each day, a different food is featured, starting with Monday's meal of bread and butter and ending with Sunday's feast of ice cream. The book follows a repetitive structure, with each day introducing a new food item and repeating the foods from previous days.

06da22b1-13e5-4b8e-a3fe-c04c6ff6c699.title: Forrest Gump
06da22b1-13e5-4b8e-a3fe-c04c6ff6c699.summary:
Forrest Gump (played by Tom Hanks) is a coming of age film. Even though he has physical and mental limitations, he lives his life to the fullest all while changing the lives of those around him. This film follows the title character "Forrest Gump" from the 1950's to the 1980's.
Forrest Gump was nominated for a 13 Academy Awards in 1995 and took home 6, including Best Picture.

06eb7fdb-a2a1-4d0e-89ed-678f8f189897.title: Working: People Talk About What They Do All Day and How They Feel About What They Do

089fd058-6740-5d06-bb56-d58474c06789.title: The Bacchae
089fd058-6740-5d06-bb56-d58474c06789.summary: The Bacchae is a tragedy by the Greek playwright Euripides, first performed in Athens in 405 BC, after his death, when it won first prize at the City Dionysia festival. The god Dionysus comes to Thebes disguised as a foreign holy man to avenge his mother's name and to make the city accept his worship. The young king, Pentheus, refuses to honor him, arrests the stranger and tries to stop the women of Thebes, who have left the city to celebrate the god's rites on a mountain. Dionysus tricks Pentheus into spying on them in disguise, and in a frenzy the women, led by his own mother Agave, kill him. When Agave comes back to her senses she realizes what she has done, and Dionysus exiles her and her father Cadmus. The play weighs reason against ecstasy, and revenge against respect for the gods. Donna Tartt's novel The Secret History is about students who pursue the rapture the play describes.

0aa19d58-6bb0-4068-8013-3a9681f14059.title: Starfield
0aa19d58-6bb0-4068-8013-3a9681f14059.summary: Explore the planets of the Milky Way and uncover the mysterious signals in the stars your way.

0aa54c4d-59c2-492e-96f7-b29e8a988e8b.title: Spongebob Squarepants: Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated
0aa54c4d-59c2-492e-96f7-b29e8a988e8b.summary: After Plankton loses control of his evil robots, it's up to Spongebob and the gang to take them down and save the day.

0c59e4e3-77d9-436c-8e90-70fcb20dda66.title: Fast Car
0c59e4e3-77d9-436c-8e90-70fcb20dda66.summary:
"Fast Car" by Tracy Chapman is a song that tells the story of a young woman's desire for a better life and her dreams of escaping her difficult circumstances. The song's lyrics follow the narrator as she reflects on her life and the struggles she faces, including poverty, family issues, and a lack of opportunities. The "fast car" represents the narrator's hope for a brighter future and her longing to leave her troubles behind.

Throughout the song, the narrator expresses her desire to escape her current situation and build a better life for herself and her partner. She dreams of driving away in a fast car, leaving her troubles behind and finding freedom and happiness elsewhere. However, as the song progresses, it becomes clear that the narrator's dreams may never be fully realized, as she remains trapped in her circumstances despite her aspirations.

Overall, "Fast Car" is a poignant and powerful song that explores themes of poverty, hope, and the struggle for a better life. Tracy Chapman's emotive vocals and the song's haunting melody combine to create a moving portrayal of the human experience.

0c7db4ba-0b93-41b6-8d08-87b1a5debd45.title: The Call of the Wild
0c7db4ba-0b93-41b6-8d08-87b1a5debd45.summary:
The story follows the journey of Buck, a large domestic dog living comfortably in California until he is stolen and sold into the harsh life of an Alaskan sled dog during the Klondike Gold Rush.

As Buck adapts to his new environment, he taps into his primal instincts and learns to survive in the harsh wilderness. Under the cruel treatment of his various owners, Buck discovers his inner strength and instinctual connection to his ancestors. He gradually becomes the leader of a wolf pack, embracing his wild nature.

Throughout the novel, Buck experiences the brutal realities of life in the wilderness, including encounters with other animals and humans. He forms deep bonds with some of his fellow sled dogs and learns to trust his instincts to navigate the challenges he faces.

0d6e0a1a-ccc8-55b0-98f1-f461c29a81c7.title: Perfectly Norman
0d6e0a1a-ccc8-55b0-98f1-f461c29a81c7.summary: Perfectly Norman is a picture book written and illustrated by Tom Percival, one of the Big Bright Feelings books, published by Bloomsbury in 2018. Norman thinks he is perfectly normal until the day he grows a pair of wings. He loves to fly, but he is afraid of how his parents will react, so he hides the wings under a big yellow coat. Hiding makes him miserable and he loses interest in things he used to love, such as bathtime, the park, swimming and birthday parties. His parents notice his sadness and gently encourage him to come out of hiding, and he finds the courage to take off the coat and fly. The pictures are mostly black and white with bright splashes of color, and the last spread is full of color and shows children flying together. Norman learns that there is no such thing as perfectly normal, only perfectly Norman. Kirkus lists it for ages 3 to 5.

0da61796-ccd8-4a2e-9be1-db224c9b8e72.title: The Iliad
0da61796-ccd8-4a2e-9be1-db224c9b8e72.summary:
This poem tells the story of the Trojan War, a legendary conflict between the Greeks and the Trojans. The poem focuses primarily on a few weeks during the final year of the war, centering on the wrath of Achilles, one of the Greek heroes, and its consequences.

The epic begins with Achilles withdrawing from the fighting after a dispute with Agamemnon, the Greek commander. Achilles' absence from the battlefield leads to a series of events that shape the course of the war. The Trojans, led by their prince Hector, gain the upper hand against the Greeks, resulting in devastating losses for both sides.

Throughout the poem, Homer explores themes of honor, glory, fate, and the human condition. The characters grapple with questions of mortality, heroism, and the consequences of their actions. The gods and goddesses of Mount Olympus intervene in the affairs of mortals, further complicating the conflict and shaping its outcome.

"The Iliad" culminates in a dramatic showdown between Achilles and Hector, the greatest warriors of their respective sides. Achilles, driven by vengeance for the death of his friend Patroclus, confronts Hector in single combat and ultimately kills him, bringing about the downfall of Troy.

0ebb6bb6-f6e5-48de-a973-6f91f999dfa0.title: I Go Blind
0ebb6bb6-f6e5-48de-a973-6f91f999dfa0.summary: The song "I Go Blind" by Hootie and the Blowfish is a song that captures the emotions of infatuation and longing. The lyrics express the feeling of being captivated by someone to the extent that the singer feels blinded by their presence.

0ed185f6-f630-4336-888b-d1723b2c84c4.title: American Prometheus
0ed185f6-f630-4336-888b-d1723b2c84c4.summary: American Prometheus: The Triumph and Tragedy of J. Robert Oppenheimer is a 2005 biography by Kai Bird and Martin J. Sherwin, the result of some twenty-five years of research. It follows Oppenheimer from a gifted, troubled youth to the leadership of the Los Alamos laboratory that built the first atomic bombs, and then to his public humiliation in 1954, when a government hearing stripped him of his security clearance. Underneath, it is the story of a scientist who made something he could not unmake and spent the rest of his life arguing about how it should be used. It won the 2006 Pulitzer Prize for Biography and was the basis for the 2023 film Oppenheimer.

1177c10e-7d6b-5cca-bc37-e20cf0b6cf9c.title: Homegoing
1177c10e-7d6b-5cca-bc37-e20cf0b6cf9c.summary: Homegoing is the first novel by Yaa Gyasi, published by Alfred A. Knopf in 2016. It begins in 18th-century Ghana with two half-sisters who never meet: Effia marries a British official and lives in Cape Coast Castle, while Esi is held in the dungeons beneath it and sold into slavery in America. Each chapter follows one descendant, alternating between the two family lines through eight generations, from the Gold Coast and the American South to Baltimore, Harlem and modern Ghana. Underneath, it asks how slavery and colonialism echo through a family, what heritage survives, and who gets to tell history. It deals with slavery, racism, violence, addiction and the death of children. It won the National Book Critics Circle's John Leonard Prize for a first book and the PEN/Hemingway Award.

11cd7296-82cf-5e45-a807-1e62c9af7b9c.title: Silly Jokes About Monsters
11cd7296-82cf-5e45-a807-1e62c9af7b9c.summary: Silly Jokes About Monsters is a joke book by Michael Dahl for beginning readers, one of the Silly Joke Books from Pebble, the early-reader imprint of Capstone. Its 24 pages pair funny photographs with short monster jokes, gathered under three headings: Funny Frights, Monster Munchies and Ghostly Giggles. The publisher says these are jokes to tell again and again, even if monsters scare you a little. The Library of Congress lists the book for ages 5 to 8 and grades 2 to 3. Underneath, it is about laughing at what frightens us and sharing a joke with someone else, which also makes it a light, low-pressure book for a new reader to try aloud with a friend or family member. Michael Dahl has written more than 200 books for children and young adults.

11d321f6-4687-476f-adf1-36923e5d7c71.title: How I Built This - Wikipedia: Jimmy Wales
11d321f6-4687-476f-adf1-36923e5d7c71.summary: In this episode of How I Built This, Guy Raz speaks with Jimmy Wales about launching Wikipedia in 2001. Wikipedia is one of most visited websites in the word.

128d610d-b181-5149-be41-2ec80cdc2108.title: The Reptile Room (Book the Second)
128d610d-b181-5149-be41-2ec80cdc2108.summary: The Reptile Room is the second book in Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events, written by Daniel Handler under that pen name and illustrated by Brett Helquist, published by HarperCollins in 1999. Having escaped Count Olaf, the three Baudelaire orphans, Violet, Klaus and baby Sunny, go to live with a kind relative, the herpetologist Dr. Montgomery Montgomery, called Uncle Monty, whose Reptile Room holds a collection of snakes. For a short time they are happy and given real jobs. Then a new assistant, Stephano, turns out to be Olaf in disguise, and the children must prove it to adults who will not listen. The book is dark comedy told by a gloomy narrator who keeps urging readers to put it down. Underneath, it is about grief, the people who see us clearly, and siblings solving a mystery together. Publishers Weekly praised its formal language and humor, and the audiobook read by Tim Curry won an AudioFile Earphones Award.

creators.name: Lemony Snicket
creators.role: author, the pen name of Daniel Handler

12fcabac-67db-5692-8e70-71aaf45e23ce.title: Cross-Training
12fcabac-67db-5692-8e70-71aaf45e23ce.summary: Cross-Training is a 64-page illustrated nonfiction book by Z. B. Hill for teen readers, published in 2014 by Mason Crest in its An Integrated Life of Fitness series. It explains cross-training as doing different sets of exercises that work different muscles. It describes how athletes use it so no muscle group is neglected and to push their bodies further, how people who are not athletes can use it to lose weight or stay in shape, and how to exercise safely. Underneath, the book is about keeping the body active in varied ways and building a lifelong habit of fitness. No professional review of this volume was found.

1394d08e-fbc3-450e-bd02-fc90ff805ea0.title: Up, Up, Down
1394d08e-fbc3-450e-bd02-fc90ff805ea0.summary: Anna loves to climb and ignores her mother's constant earning to "Be careful! Don't climb!," even after she falls down from scaling the refrigerator and the side of the house. One day, Anna manages to climb all the way up a palm tree, but the descent leaves her frantically hanging from a leaf. When her parents come to the rescue, the tables are quickly turned when her mother and father are the ones hanging from the tree instead!

13ec7bc5-ccc1-5dc0-a960-54db874ea283.title: A Tale for the Time Being
13ec7bc5-ccc1-5dc0-a960-54db874ea283.summary: A Tale for the Time Being is a 2013 novel by Ruth Ozeki, published by Viking. It tells two stories that meet across the Pacific. Nao, a sixteen-year-old in Tokyo, is bullied at school, and her family is struggling after her father lost his job in the United States. She keeps a diary, and she is thinking about ending her life. Before she does, she wants to record the life of her 104-year-old great-grandmother Jiko, a Zen Buddhist nun. Years later, on an island off the coast of British Columbia, a novelist named Ruth finds the diary in a Hello Kitty lunchbox that may have washed ashore after the 2011 tsunami, and she sets out to learn what became of Nao. Underneath, the book is about time and memory, feeling like a stranger in your family's country, and what keeps a person alive. It was shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize and won the Los Angeles Times Book Prize for Fiction.

14d18643-830d-4cd0-b9f4-579d14f6a984.title: Dazzle the Dinosaur
14d18643-830d-4cd0-b9f4-579d14f6a984.summary:
This is the story of a young dinosaur named Dazzle who feels lonely and wishes to have a friend. One day, he discovers a colorful stone that makes him feel happy and hopeful.

As Dazzle travels through the prehistoric landscape, he encounters various animals who are initially afraid of him because of his size and appearance. However, Dazzle's gentle and kind nature wins them over, and they become his friends.

Together, Dazzle and his new friends embark on a series of adventures, exploring the wonders of the world around them. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about friendship, acceptance, and the importance of being true to oneself.

16bb1c26-bcb2-4d88-a0d6-02edfa099334.title: The Time Machine
16bb1c26-bcb2-4d88-a0d6-02edfa099334.summary: The Time Machine is an 1895 dystopian post-apocalyptic science fiction novella by H. G. Wells about a Victorian scientist known as the Time Traveller who travels approximately 800,806 years into the future. The work is generally credited with the popularization of the concept of time travel by using a vehicle or device to travel purposely and selectively forward or backward through time. The term "time machine", coined by Wells, is now almost universally used to refer to such a vehicle or device.

16dac010-f0a3-43a6-9946-15d4bb6a2038.title: 109 East Palace: Robert Oppenheimer and the Secret City of Los Alamos
16dac010-f0a3-43a6-9946-15d4bb6a2038.summary: In 1943, J. Robert Oppenheimer, the brilliant, charismatic head of the Manhattan Project, recruited scientists to live as virtual prisoners of the U.S. government at Los Alamos, a barren mesa thirty-five miles outside Santa Fe, New Mexico. Thousands of men, women, and children spent the war years sequestered in this top-secret military facility. They lied to friends and family about where they were going and what they were doing, and then disappeared into the desert. Through the eyes of a young Santa Fe widow who was one of Oppenheimer’s first recruits, we see how, for all his flaws, he developed into an inspiring leader and motivated all those involved in the Los Alamos project to make a supreme effort and achieve the unthinkable. In 2006, it won the Spirit of the West Award for literary achievement in non-fiction.

179a7e98-3552-584d-83db-f6f31399b2da.title: Found
179a7e98-3552-584d-83db-f6f31399b2da.summary: Found is a short young adult thriller by Joseph Bruchac (Nulhegan Abenaki), published in January 2020 by 7th Generation in its PathFinders line. Nick, an Abenaki teenager who loves martial arts and rock climbing, is on a train to a Native outdoor school in Canada, where he will teach woodcraft. He opens the wrong compartment door, sees a murder, and is thrown off the train. Hunted through the Canadian wilderness, he hears his grandfather's voice and draws on the survival lessons and calm his Abenaki elders taught him, and he begins to see that the health of his people's homelands is at stake. Underneath, it is about inherited knowledge and keeping a clear head when afraid. Kirkus called it a fast, gripping read, and the publisher compares it to the story The Most Dangerous Game.

17b6d753-57b6-5445-b649-4c29bd6a2703.title: Principles of Business: Management
17b6d753-57b6-5445-b649-4c29bd6a2703.summary: Principles of Business: Management is a reference book edited by Richard L. Wilson and published in May 2017 by Salem Press with Grey House Publishing. It is the second volume of a six-volume Principles of Business series. Its 70 entries, arranged A to Z, explain the basics of running organizations in plain language, from leadership, teams and decision making to negotiation, crisis management, competitive strategy and starting a new business. Each entry opens with an abstract and key terms, then a short discussion with applications and issues, and ends with a further reading list. A glossary and an index close the volume. The publisher aims it at high school and undergraduate students, and also at job-seekers and people starting their own businesses.

1865570b-e3d3-5d1c-8485-082d72d604f9.title: The Goldfinch
1865570b-e3d3-5d1c-8485-082d72d604f9.summary: The Goldfinch is a novel by Donna Tartt, published by Little, Brown in 2013; it won the 2014 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction. Theo Decker is thirteen when a bomb goes off in a gallery at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York and kills his mother. A dying man gives Theo a ring and urges him to take a small Dutch painting, Carel Fabritius's The Goldfinch, and Theo carries it away and hides it for years. The novel follows him through the home of a wealthy school friend's family, his father's house in Las Vegas, where he befriends a boy named Boris, and an antiques shop in New York run by a man named Hobie, then on to Amsterdam. Along the way Theo struggles with grief, guilt and drugs, and the painting becomes the thing he cannot let go. Critics were divided, but Kirkus named it one of the best books of 2013.

1880d7fe-fd61-44c6-bf8c-fd4bbc41438d.title: Persona 5
1880d7fe-fd61-44c6-bf8c-fd4bbc41438d.summary: A group of high school students gain the power to enter the hearts of others and fight their dark desires, using their new abilities to try and right the wrongs of society from the shadows.

19ccb679-dafb-4ab0-b56b-b5b94fe28276.title: Journey to the Center of the Earth
19ccb679-dafb-4ab0-b56b-b5b94fe28276.summary: Journey to the Center of the Earth, also translated with the variant titles A Journey to the Centre of the Earth and A Journey into the Interior of the Earth, is a classic science fiction novel by Jules Verne. It was first published in French in 1864, then reissued in 1867 in a revised and expanded edition. Professor Otto Lidenbrock is the tale's central figure, an eccentric German scientist who believes there are volcanic tubes that reach to the very center of the earth. He, his nephew Axel, and their Icelandic guide Hans rappel into Iceland's celebrated inactive volcano Snæfellsjökull, then contend with many dangers, including cave-ins, subpolar tornadoes, an underground ocean, and living prehistoric creatures from the Mesozoic and Cenozoic eras. Eventually the three explorers are spewed back to the surface by an active volcano, Stromboli, located in southern Italy.

1a4a4924-0445-4cb6-a0f4-a649defed598.title: Law & Order: Special Victims Unit
1a4a4924-0445-4cb6-a0f4-a649defed598.summary: Law & Order: Special Victims Unit is an American police procedural crime drama television series created by Dick Wolf for NBC. The first spin-off of Law & Order, it stars Mariska Hargitay as Detective Olivia Benson, now the commanding officer of the Special Victims Unit after originally having been Stabler's partner in a fictionalized version of the New York City Police Department, and Christopher Meloni as Detective Elliot Stabler. Law & Order: Special Victims Unit follows the detectives of the Special Victims Unit as they investigate and prosecute sexually based crimes. Some of the episodes are loosely based on real crimes that have received media attention.

1b65ac91-a4a8-49c1-8a51-fb3cf8738fdc.title: A Place to Belong
1b65ac91-a4a8-49c1-8a51-fb3cf8738fdc.summary: Cynthia Kadohataillustrated by Julia KuoCaitlyn Dlouhy BooksAtheneum, 2019hardcover: 978-1481446648

1bd3af52-aae1-4205-b229-9544f47f8625.title: Goodnight Moon
1bd3af52-aae1-4205-b229-9544f47f8625.summary: The story follows a bedtime routine as a young rabbit says goodnight to various objects and characters in his room. The bunny says goodnight to everything from the moon to household items, eventually drifting off to sleep.

1c2aa369-70e6-48a9-863e-c84ce95e80c6.title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
1c2aa369-70e6-48a9-863e-c84ce95e80c6.summary:
This story follows four siblings—Peter, Susan, Edmund, and Lucy Pevensie—who are evacuated from London during World War II and sent to live with an old professor in the countryside.

While exploring the professor's mysterious mansion, Lucy stumbles upon a wardrobe that serves as a portal to the magical land of Narnia. She discovers that Narnia is under the rule of the evil White Witch, who has plunged the land into perpetual winter and holds it captive in her icy grasp.

Lucy's siblings are initially skeptical of her claims about Narnia, but soon they all find themselves transported to this enchanted realm. Together with Aslan, the wise and noble lion, and a host of fantastical creatures, the children embark on a perilous quest to overthrow the White Witch and restore peace and prosperity to Narnia.

As the Pevensie children navigate the wonders and dangers of Narnia, they encounter talking animals, mythical creatures, and magical beings, each playing a crucial role in the epic struggle between good and evil.

1d637287-5bd2-4bbe-a7f4-1be636d399f4.title: Oppenheimer
1d637287-5bd2-4bbe-a7f4-1be636d399f4.summary: Oppenheimer (2023) is an epic biographical film written and directed by Christopher Nolan for Universal Pictures, based on the biography American Prometheus by Kai Bird and Martin J. Sherwin. Cillian Murphy plays J. Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the Los Alamos laboratory that built the first atomic bombs during World War II. The film follows his studies, the race to build the bomb, and the 1954 security hearing that turned against him, as he wrestles with what his work has unleashed. It is about genius, responsibility and the cost of power. It won seven Academy Awards, including Best Picture.

1e161945-a4ed-4154-b429-d2ed5f2e32c4.title: Three Little Birds
1e161945-a4ed-4154-b429-d2ed5f2e32c4.summary: "Three Little Birds" is a popular song by Bob Marley and the Wailers and is a soothing and uplifting song with a simple yet powerful message of reassurance and positivity. The lyrics are often interpreted as a reminder to not worry about life's challenges because everything will be alright.

1e3ddd03-0680-50e6-b60a-7719943245de.title: Loserville
1e3ddd03-0680-50e6-b60a-7719943245de.summary: Loserville is a young adult novel by Peter Johnson, published in March 2009 by Front Street. It follows Lucas and four close friends over the summer after their sophomore year of high school: work, girlfriends, small rebellions and strained relationships with their parents. When the strict stepmother of Lucas's best friend Derek enters him in a reality television show called Loserville, hosted by a self-styled psychiatrist named Jesus, the friends' ordinary lives are squeezed into dramatic television. Underneath, the book is about friendship, troubled families and how edited television can distort the truth about real people. Kirkus found the premise interesting but the execution uneven; the story has a tragic turn.

1e99bb13-8797-559f-92f6-88d308884b38.title: Codebreaking Sisters: Our Secret War
1e99bb13-8797-559f-92f6-88d308884b38.summary: Codebreaking Sisters: Our Secret War is a Second World War memoir by Patricia and Jean Owtram, later known as Pat Davies and Jean Argles, published by Mirror Books in 2020 when the sisters were in their nineties. They grew up in a Lancashire family that sheltered Austrian Jewish refugees, and both girls learned German. In the war Patricia joined the Women's Royal Naval Service and listened in at coastal stations to German ship radio, work that fed Bletchley Park's attack on the Enigma ciphers. Jean, a crossword fan, became a code and cipher officer with the First Aid Nursing Yeomanry, serving the Special Operations Executive in London, Cairo and Italy. Both signed the Official Secrets Act and said nothing for decades. The sisters tell their stories in alternating chapters, a plain-spoken account of duty, secrecy and the quiet work of ordinary young women.

1ee641fe-0f63-4655-bb9b-e78e46256846.title: Music for a Sushi Restaurant
1ee641fe-0f63-4655-bb9b-e78e46256846.summary: The song is set in a sushi restaurant where the singer is on a date with the one that he sees as the "apple of his eye." There are many food metaphors to describe his love and attraction to her.

1f25f757-2a11-5f21-90f3-73ab522c31a5.title: Viola in Reel Life
1f25f757-2a11-5f21-90f3-73ab522c31a5.summary: Viola in Reel Life is a young adult novel by Adriana Trigiani, published by HarperTeen in 2009 and the first of her Viola books. Fourteen-year-old Viola Chesterton, a Brooklyn teenager who sees the world through her video camera, is sent to Prefect Academy, an all-girls boarding school in South Bend, Indiana, while her filmmaker parents spend a year in Afghanistan making a documentary. Leaving her best friend Andrew behind, she shares a room with three girls she expects to dislike. Over the year she makes friends, has a first romance, helps rescue the school's Founders Day play and enters a film contest. Underneath, it is about stepping out from behind the lens to take part in real life. Kirkus found the characters and plot predictable but a light read for teens who want romance; readers on Everand are mostly warmer. A sequel, Viola in the Spotlight, followed in 2011.

1f57bb48-c2a7-4de7-bae5-899294bdfe7f.title: Assassin's Creed
1f57bb48-c2a7-4de7-bae5-899294bdfe7f.summary: In the modern day, average bartender Desmond Miles uses advanced technology to experience the memories of his ancestor Altair, an Assassin of legend as he seeks to kill corrupt leaders in the time of the Crusades.

1fc5a0bd-7003-51ad-a458-c6b04b4414ed.title: Jazz
1fc5a0bd-7003-51ad-a458-c6b04b4414ed.summary: Jazz is a 1992 novel by Toni Morrison, the second book in her trilogy on African American history that began with Beloved. Most of it takes place in Harlem in 1926, and it opens after a shocking act: Joe Trace, a middle-aged door-to-door cosmetics salesman, has shot his teenage lover, Dorcas, and his wife Violet, a hairdresser, has attacked the girl's body at her funeral. A gossiping narrator who is never named tells the story, then the book moves back through the lives of Joe, Violet, Dorcas, her aunt Alice Manfred and others, to rural Virginia and the 19th-century South. Morrison built the book like jazz, with voices taking turns on the same themes, after three years of reading Harlem newspapers and records. Underneath, it is about love and loss, mothers and the lack of them, and what the past does to the people who carry it. It deals with murder, grief, racial violence and a mother's suicide.

1fe4ba98-f587-4cbb-a257-a8a184087064.title: Irreplaceable
1fe4ba98-f587-4cbb-a257-a8a184087064.summary: The song is about a woman who has discovered that her partner has been unfaithful. She tells him that he is easily replaceable and tells him to leave. The song’s lyrics make it clear that Beyoncé is not going to tolerate being treated poorly by a man, and that she’s fully capable of moving on without him. She is ending the relationship on her terms.

2024c63a-bfc0-492d-b54f-c69481ef1ab9.title: Click, Clack, Moo Christmas at the Farm

2024f327-903f-484f-b1a0-4b4f07c8fb50.title: Catch-22
2024f327-903f-484f-b1a0-4b4f07c8fb50.summary:
This story, set during World War II, follows the experiences of Captain John Yossarian, a U.S. Army Air Forces B-25 bombardier stationed on the island of Pianosa. 

As Yossarian navigates his way through the war, he encounters a host of eccentric characters, including his fellow soldiers, officers, and superiors. 

Throughout the novel, Yossarian grapples with the senseless violence and chaos of war while attempting to preserve his own sanity and survival. As he confronts the illogical rules and regulations of military life, he becomes increasingly disillusioned with the institutions and authority figures that govern his existence.

203a4704-40b6-4ae2-905c-4bd850f46575.title: Bear Snores On
203a4704-40b6-4ae2-905c-4bd850f46575.summary: On a cold winter night many animals gather to party in the cave of a sleeping bear, who then awakes and protests that he has missed the food and the fun.

22325eb3-c015-5494-982d-f5790a5ed07f.title: The Greatest
22325eb3-c015-5494-982d-f5790a5ed07f.summary: A 1977 American-British biographical drama about the boxer Muhammad Ali, who plays himself. Tom Gries directed it from a screenplay by Ring Lardner Jr., based on Ali's 1975 book The Greatest: My Own Story. It follows Cassius Clay from his light-heavyweight Olympic gold medal in Rome in 1960, through his conversion to Islam and new name, his refusal to be drafted for the Vietnam War, and his return to the ring, and it ends with his 1974 knockout of George Foreman in Zaire to win back the heavyweight title. The film is built largely from archival footage of Ali's real fights. Michael Masser wrote the score and the theme song, 'The Greatest Love of All,' which George Benson sang. Tom Gries died in January 1977, months before the release, and the film is dedicated to him. Critics were mixed: one called it a charming curio, another called it a whitewash.

223aa380-7ad9-42eb-b722-fd37db2548d9.title: 3AM
223aa380-7ad9-42eb-b722-fd37db2548d9.summary: "3AM" is the third single and the third track from American rock band Matchbox 20's debut album, Yourself or Someone Like You (1996). Written by Rob Thomas, Jay Stanley, John Leslie Goff, and Brian Yale, the song was inspired by Thomas dealing with his mother's cancer as a teenager. The song was officially serviced to US modern rock radio in October 1997 and was given a commercial release outside North America the following month.

230f9d9e-4af2-5d0c-bd40-75d63971f21c.title: The War That Saved My Life
230f9d9e-4af2-5d0c-bd40-75d63971f21c.summary: The War That Saved My Life is a historical novel by Kimberly Brubaker Bradley, published by Dial Books for Young Readers in 2015 and named a 2016 Newbery Honor Book. Ada, about ten, was born with a clubfoot, and her abusive mother keeps her hidden in a one-room London apartment, claiming she is mentally disabled. When children are evacuated from London at the start of World War II, Ada secretly follows her little brother Jamie onto the train. In Kent they are taken in by Susan Smith, a reluctant and grieving guardian. In the countryside Ada learns to walk with crutches, ride a pony, read and write, and slowly learns that she can be cared for. But the war and her mother's return threaten what she has built. The book deals with abuse, disability, loss and the chance to rebuild trust. Its sequel is The War I Finally Won.

2371555c-50c0-4bf5-96db-810ffd692aec.title: The Very Clumsy Click Beetle
2371555c-50c0-4bf5-96db-810ffd692aec.summary: In The Very Clumsy Click Beetle, a young click beetle is learning how to flip itself onto its feet after landing on its back. Despite repeated failures, the beetle doesn’t give up. Along the way, it encounters other animals who offer encouragement. The click beetle keeps trying until it finally succeeds in a triumphant flip, accompanied by a satisfying “click.”

23b2c7e3-c719-43b4-8da7-3ff8f35627ca.title: Beowulf
23b2c7e3-c719-43b4-8da7-3ff8f35627ca.summary:
Beowulf is an Old English epic poem in the tradition of Germanic heroic legend consisting of 3,182 alliterative lines. It is one of the most important and most often translated works of Old English literature. The date of composition is a matter of contention among scholars; the only certain dating is for the manuscript, which was produced between 975 and 1025 AD. Scholars call the anonymous author the "Beowulf poet". 
The story is set in pagan Scandinavia in the 5th and 6th centuries. Beowulf, a hero of the Geats, comes to the aid of Hrothgar, the king of the Danes, whose mead hall Heorot has been under attack by the monster Grendel for twelve years. After Beowulf slays him, Grendel's mother takes revenge and is in turn defeated. Victorious, Beowulf goes home to Geatland and becomes king of the Geats. Fifty years later, Beowulf defeats a dragon, but is mortally wounded in the battle. After his death, his attendants cremate his body and erect a barrow on a headland in his memory.

24eba5b1-5348-4093-bbde-c0a9cb4a1862.title: Undertale
24eba5b1-5348-4093-bbde-c0a9cb4a1862.summary: A lone human stumbles into the underground world of monsters, and now must find their way out all while meeting and contending with the inhabitants within.

2574bd62-e9a7-4bbd-a32c-5914448e1159.title: Brideshead Revisited
2574bd62-e9a7-4bbd-a32c-5914448e1159.summary:
This story follows the life of Charles Ryder, a young man of modest means who becomes enamored with the aristocratic Flyte family during his time at Oxford University in the 1920s. The story is narrated by Charles as he reflects on his past experiences and the transformative influence of his relationships with the Flytes.

At Oxford, Charles befriends Sebastian Flyte, an eccentric and charming aristocrat, and becomes deeply involved with Sebastian's family and their ancestral home, Brideshead Castle. Charles is drawn into the opulent world of the Flytes, marked by wealth, privilege, and tradition, and forms a close bond with Sebastian and his sister, Julia.

As Charles becomes increasingly entwined with the Flytes, he is exposed to their family dynamics, including the strained relationship between Sebastian and his devoutly Catholic mother, Lady Marchmain, and the conflict between their religious faith and personal desires.

The novel traces Charles' journey of self-discovery and moral awakening as he grapples with questions of love, faith, and identity against the backdrop of a changing society and the looming specter of World War II. Charles' relationships with Sebastian and Julia, as well as his complex feelings towards the aristocratic world of Brideshead, shape his understanding of himself and his place in the world.

25e0399e-9f68-42c4-b420-e7dbeab91e7f.title: Cyberpunk Red
25e0399e-9f68-42c4-b420-e7dbeab91e7f.summary: The Roleplaying Game of the Dark Future, play as a variety of roles in the Cyberpunk future of the 2050s, where morality is grey and status is more important than anything.

261d9966-a20c-45ce-a5d3-a64ecdf1d96b.title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
261d9966-a20c-45ce-a5d3-a64ecdf1d96b.summary: The land of Hyrule has been in chaos for almost one hundred years, and Link must rise to save it by defeating the evil Ganon.

26e49767-914c-5bc1-9baa-07e88e5f07a8.title: Greatest Love of All
26e49767-914c-5bc1-9baa-07e88e5f07a8.summary: A ballad recorded by Whitney Houston in December 1984 for her debut album, Whitney Houston (1985), and released as a single on March 18, 1986 by Arista Records. Michael Masser composed it and produced her recording; Linda Creed wrote the words. It is a cover: George Benson recorded the song, as 'The Greatest Love of All,' in 1977 for the Muhammad Ali film The Greatest. Houston said her version is about loving yourself despite your flaws, and a New York Times critic heard self-worth, spiritual devotion, Black pride and family loyalty in it. It spent three weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1986 and was nominated for the Grammy Award for Record of the Year. Creed wrote the lyrics while being treated for breast cancer and died in April 1986, weeks before the single reached the top.

27413899-5c1c-4878-bdd4-a953d5e9ca3c.title: Lord of the Flies
27413899-5c1c-4878-bdd4-a953d5e9ca3c.summary: Lord of the Flies is the 1954 debut novel of British author William Golding. The plot concerns a group of British boys who are stranded on an uninhabited island and their disastrous attempts to govern themselves. The novel's themes include morality, leadership, and the tension between civility and chaos.

282007ec-bf04-5cdc-9060-93c090c9441d.title: The Underground Railroad
282007ec-bf04-5cdc-9060-93c090c9441d.summary: The Underground Railroad is a novel by Colson Whitehead, published by Doubleday in 2016; it won the National Book Award and the 2017 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction. Cora is a young woman enslaved on a Georgia plantation, shunned by the others after her mother, Mabel, ran away without her. When a fellow enslaved man, Caesar, asks her to run with him, she agrees. In Whitehead's version the railroad is real, with tracks, tunnels and stations beneath the South, and each stop is a state with its own idea of freedom. A slave catcher named Ridgeway follows her through South Carolina, North Carolina, Tennessee and Indiana. It is historical fiction with invented elements, and it does not look away from the violence of slavery. The publisher's teacher's guide recommends it for grades 11 and 12 and carries a trigger warning for scenes of sexual and physical violence.

28b9ee43-a23f-44ac-8ab2-de6b5e698612.title: Enchanted (Taylor's Version)
28b9ee43-a23f-44ac-8ab2-de6b5e698612.summary: "Enchanted" is a song written and recorded by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift for her third studio album, Speak Now (2010). Produced by Swift and Nathan Chapman, the song is a power ballad combining pop, rock, and country. The production incorporates gentle acoustic guitars and crescendos after each refrain, leading to dynamic electric guitars, a steady drum beat, and a vocal harmony-layered coda. In the lyrics, a narrator is infatuated with someone after meeting them for the first time, and she worries about whether the initial feeling will be reciprocated.

292bbe2f-0d05-42d6-b037-5ecaface82a3.title: Escape to Play
292bbe2f-0d05-42d6-b037-5ecaface82a3.summary:
What could go wrong when three mischievous dogs slip out before dawn to explore the farm? Follow the pups as they make a mess in every new place they go.

Playful poetry and whimsical illustrations create an upbeat feeling as you move from page to page. Be sure to keep an eye out for some special paintings hanging on the farmhouse walls!

Escape to Play is a reminder to have fun with discovery. Art lovers and future art lovers will enjoy the backmatter section full of tidbits and questions. The backmatter section offers easy-to-read information about the art that was sprinkled throughout the book.

298b0e39-f9b4-5c72-a8fa-19645681f71c.title: Washington, D.C.
298b0e39-f9b4-5c72-a8fa-19645681f71c.summary: Washington, D.C. is a pictorial travel book in the American Traveler series, published in 1990 with photographs from The Image Bank. Google Books describes it as more than 90 color photographs with brief text presenting the sights of the capital in its diversity. Its text names the city's best-known places, among them the Capitol, the White House, the Washington Monument, the Lincoln and Jefferson Memorials, the Vietnam Veterans Memorial, the Smithsonian and Georgetown, and the people behind them such as Pierre L'Enfant, who planned the city. Underneath, it is a visitor's first look at a capital built as a planned city of monuments and museums. No reviews or awards were found.

2992e519-bef3-41ca-b7ea-c6cb927f37d9.title: Les Misérables
2992e519-bef3-41ca-b7ea-c6cb927f37d9.summary:
This story, set against the backdrop of 19th-century France, follows the lives of several characters, primarily focusing on Jean Valjean, a former convict who seeks redemption, and Inspector Javert, who pursues him relentlessly.

The story begins with Valjean's release from prison after serving 19 years for stealing a loaf of bread to feed his family. Despite his efforts to start afresh, he faces societal rejection and struggles to find his place in the world. Through acts of kindness and compassion, Valjean seeks redemption while evading capture by Javert, who sees the law as absolute and unyielding.

As Valjean assumes a new identity and becomes a successful businessman, he encounters Fantine, a destitute factory worker forced into prostitution to support her daughter Cosette. Valjean vows to care for Cosette after Fantine's death, leading to a life-changing journey of sacrifice and love.

Meanwhile, the novel follows the lives of other characters, including Marius Pontmercy, a young revolutionary, and Eponine, the daughter of the Thénardiers, unscrupulous innkeepers. Their paths intersect in the tumultuous backdrop of the June Rebellion of 1832, where they confront the harsh realities of poverty, injustice, and sacrifice.

29b3484c-ff2a-5706-bcd7-935b1ef42b37.title: A Dark Truth
29b3484c-ff2a-5706-bcd7-935b1ef42b37.summary: A short young-adult novel by Jeff Ross, published by Orca Book Publishers in 2016 in its Orca Soundings series, which the publisher describes as high-interest, low-reading-level fiction for teens. Riley and Dashawn have been friends since they were three and skateboard together. They bring a third skater, Natasha, to film clips for a sponsorship video near a new office development. When police arrive, the three scatter, and Dashawn never shows up at the meeting spot. The next day Riley learns the police beat him. The book is about friendship and race: Riley is shaken to find that not everyone lives in the same world he does.

2ade4d87-3f8a-50b1-a066-d64dbbcd0990.title: Project Hail Mary
2ade4d87-3f8a-50b1-a066-d64dbbcd0990.summary: Project Hail Mary is a science fiction novel by Andy Weir, published by Ballantine Books in 2021. Ryland Grace, a junior high science teacher with a doctorate in molecular biology, wakes aboard a starship with no memory of who he is or why he is there. The Sun is dimming because of a space-dwelling microbe, and the ship was sent, on a trip with no planned return, to learn why one nearby star is resisting the same infection. The rest of the crew has died along the way, so Grace must piece together his past and the mission on his own. Then he meets an alien engineer from another star that is under the same threat. Underneath, the book is about friendship across differences, working together, and choosing to give up your own safe way home. It reached The New York Times best-seller list, was a Hugo Award finalist, and became a 2026 film.

2b3b6983-6d51-4088-875b-3124bb16269d.title: How to Grow a Friend
2b3b6983-6d51-4088-875b-3124bb16269d.summary: A lovely metaphor teaches valuable lessons in how to treat others and make friendships blossom! Making a friend takes patience, care, and room to bloom—just like growing a flower. Soon your little gardeners will have their very own green thumbs for this most important of life skills.

2be3f880-c6aa-42e8-b216-4d2d86f8f6aa.title: We Could Be Heroes
2be3f880-c6aa-42e8-b216-4d2d86f8f6aa.summary: An extraordinary and emotional adventure about unlikely friends and the power of choosing who you want to be ... Jamie woke up in an empty apartment with no memory and only a few clues to his identity, but with the ability to read and erase other people's memories - a power he uses to hold up banks to buy coffee, cat food and books. Zoe is also searching for her past, and using her abilities of speed and strength ... to deliver fast food. And she'll occasionally put on a cool suit and beat up bad guys, if she feels like it. When the archrivals meet in a memory-loss support group, they realize the only way to reveal their hidden pasts might be through each other. As they uncover an ongoing threat, suddenly much more is at stake than their fragile friendship. With countless people at risk, Zoe and Jamie will have to recognize that sometimes being a hero starts with trusting someone else - and yourself.

2be7dc15-2805-4518-b2a2-bfced26c1ff0.title: All Star
2be7dc15-2805-4518-b2a2-bfced26c1ff0.summary: "All Star” can be considered a comforting anthem of courage and self-acceptance and a critique on how seriously society and people take themselves. It talks about breaking rules, living a pleasurable life, and embracing action. The chorus is a mantra of self-encouragement.

2cff0a42-e6bd-4ccb-9ba6-3e2c8994a367.title: Love and Luck
2cff0a42-e6bd-4ccb-9ba6-3e2c8994a367.summary:
"Love and Luck" by Jimmy Buffett is a laid-back, feel-good song that captures the essence of enjoying life with a positive attitude and a carefree spirit. The song is featured on his 1988 album Hot Water and embodies the tropical, easygoing vibe that Buffett is known for.

Themes:
Positivity: The song encourages embracing the good things in life, even amidst challenges. It reflects a philosophy of focusing on love, luck, and the simple pleasures rather than getting bogged down by negativity.
Carefree Lifestyle: True to Buffett’s signature style, "Love and Luck" promotes a laid-back approach to life, where having love and a bit of luck is all you need to be happy.
Resilience: There’s a subtle theme of resilience, suggesting that even when life throws curveballs, maintaining a positive outlook and appreciating what you have can help you get through.
Musical Style:
Tropical Rock: The song blends elements of country, rock, and Caribbean-inspired rhythms, creating a breezy, tropical feel.
Upbeat Melody: The melody is upbeat and cheerful, with a catchy chorus that makes it easy to sing along to. The instrumentation features steel drums, acoustic guitar, and a light rhythm section, contributing to its sunny, island vibe.
Lyrics:
The lyrics of "Love and Luck" talk about the ups and downs of life but emphasize that love and a bit of luck can make everything better. Buffett uses imagery of sunny skies, beaches, and good times to paint a picture of a life well-lived, even when things aren’t perfect.

Overall, "Love and Luck" is a quintessential Jimmy Buffett song that celebrates the joys of life, love, and the serendipity that often accompanies a positive outlook.

2e7b5096-5716-558c-b729-718823871071.title: The Book Thief
2e7b5096-5716-558c-b729-718823871071.summary: The Book Thief is a historical novel by Australian author Markus Zusak, first published in Australia in 2005 and in the United States by Knopf in 2006. Death narrates the story of Liesel Meminger, a girl who in January 1939 is sent to foster parents Hans and Rosa Hubermann on Himmel Street in the invented town of Molching, outside Munich. After taking her first book at her brother's grave, she learns to read with Hans's help and begins taking books from a Nazi bonfire and the mayor's wife's library. When the family hides a young Jewish man, Max Vandenburg, in their basement, the book turns on what words can do: wound, comfort, and save. Underneath, it is about small kindnesses inside a regime of hatred, and about grief. It was a 2007 Printz Honor Book and has sold more than 17 million copies.

2eee83a1-6699-5470-8e0a-e91a4ab61c9b.title: The Warmth of Other Suns
2eee83a1-6699-5470-8e0a-e91a4ab61c9b.summary: The Warmth of Other Suns: The Epic Story of America's Great Migration is a work of narrative history by Isabel Wilkerson, published by Random House in 2010. It tells the story of the Great Migration, the movement of almost six million Black Americans out of the South to cities in the North, Midwest and West between 1915 and 1970. Wilkerson spent about fifteen years on it and interviewed more than a thousand people. She follows three of them in depth: Ida Mae Gladney, who left a Mississippi sharecropping life for Chicago in 1937; George Starling, a Florida citrus worker who fled to Harlem after organizing his fellow workers; and Robert Pershing Foster, a Louisiana doctor who went to Los Angeles in 1953. The book won the National Book Critics Circle Award for nonfiction. It describes Jim Crow, lynching threats and housing discrimination, and some of the people it follows lose family closeness or peace of mind along the way.

2f6afee0-1bd4-4afb-bb5b-15e60ee911d3.title: Los Alamos National Laboratory/Bradbury Science Museum

2fb539f5-b74e-4359-9eab-5c250ad93d08.title: Pac-Man World: RePac
2fb539f5-b74e-4359-9eab-5c250ad93d08.summary: After his family is kidnapped, Pac-Man must go and fight the Ghosts to save them.

2ff3784d-0751-5faa-bd93-7fb13b40ad5d.title: Uji
2ff3784d-0751-5faa-bd93-7fb13b40ad5d.summary: Uji (有時), usually translated as Being-Time, is a 1240 essay by the Japanese Zen teacher Dōgen, written in early winter at a temple south of Kyoto. It is the twentieth fascicle of his Shōbōgenzō (Treasury of the True Dharma Eye). Starting from a saying of the Chinese monk Yaoshan, who describes himself as sometimes standing on a mountain peak and sometimes at the bottom of the sea, Dōgen argues that time and existence cannot be separated: all being is time, and every moment holds all things. He warns against thinking of time as something that only flies by, and writes that the pine and the bamboo are time, and so is the self. Early readers took it through the Buddhist idea of impermanence, and later ones have compared it with Heidegger's Being and Time. The essay gives the novel A Tale for the Time Being its title, per the approved note on that record.

3093fea7-2d98-4755-9362-6955769eed47.title: Smooth
3093fea7-2d98-4755-9362-6955769eed47.summary: "Smooth" is a passionate and sultry song that revolves around the theme of intense romantic attraction and desire. The lyrics convey the heat and chemistry between two people, describing the overwhelming emotions that come with a powerful connection. The singer expresses the irresistible allure of the person he desires and the magnetic pull of their relationship. Santana's signature guitar riffs complement Rob Thomas's soulful vocals, creating a musical synergy that captures the essence of the song's title. "Smooth" became a massive hit and won several awards, including multiple Grammy Awards, making it one of the iconic collaborations in the late 1990s music scene.

30a7c2d4-cb12-49ce-89d7-2a2fe2df0393.title: Call of Duty: World at War
30a7c2d4-cb12-49ce-89d7-2a2fe2df0393.summary: Call of Duty: World at War is a 2008 first-person shooter game developed by Treyarch and published by Activision. It is the fifth main installment of the Call of Duty series and is the fourth entry in the series to be set during World War II. The game was announced by Activision in June 2008 and was released in November 2008, for PlayStation 3, Windows, Xbox 360, and Wii. Other games under the World at War title were published for the Nintendo DS and PlayStation 2, featuring different storylines and missions.

30a83cd6-1587-4193-a48f-b9fe00050c53.title: The Secret Garden
30a83cd6-1587-4193-a48f-b9fe00050c53.summary: Ten-year-old Mary comes to live in a lonely house on the Yorkshire moors and discovers an invalid cousin and the mysteries of a locked garden.

313bf9bb-5eee-5279-8cd9-a22e674c327f.title: The One and Only Ivan
313bf9bb-5eee-5279-8cd9-a22e674c327f.summary: The One and Only Ivan is a novel by Katherine Applegate, with illustrations by Patricia Castelao, published by Harper in 2012; it won the 2013 Newbery Medal. Ivan is a silverback gorilla who has lived for decades in a glass-walled enclosure at the Exit 8 Big Top Mall and Video Arcade, a run-down circus-themed mall. He draws and paints, and his owner, Mack, sells the pictures. When a baby elephant named Ruby is bought for the mall and badly treated, Ivan keeps a promise he made to Stella, an old elephant who dies, and works to find Ruby a better life. To do it he must admit his home is a cage and face memories of the jungle he lost. Ivan tells the story himself in short, plain sentences. It was inspired by the real gorilla Ivan, who spent 27 years in a shopping center in Washington State before moving to Zoo Atlanta in 1994. It deals with captivity, loss and cruelty toward animals.

318469ce-b35a-5b56-abad-d27e472a3c84.title: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
318469ce-b35a-5b56-abad-d27e472a3c84.summary: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks is a work of nonfiction by the science journalist Rebecca Skloot, published by Crown in 2010. In 1951 Henrietta Lacks, a poor Black mother of five from Virginia, was treated for cervical cancer at Johns Hopkins Hospital in Baltimore, where tissue was taken from her without her knowledge. Her cells became HeLa, the first human cells to keep dividing in a laboratory, and went on to help with work such as the polio vaccine, while her family was not told for decades. Skloot spent about ten years on the story, and the book follows her partnership with Henrietta's daughter Deborah as they search for the woman behind the cells. Underneath, it is about consent, who owns a person's tissue, race and class in medicine, and a family's claim to its own story. It won the 2010 Wellcome Trust Book Prize and was made into an HBO film in 2017.

31bc3f9d-b1be-4030-9688-28c61f4d936a.title: Fat Man and Little Boy
31bc3f9d-b1be-4030-9688-28c61f4d936a.summary:
Fat Man and Little Boy is a 1989 American epic historical 
war drama film directed by Roland Joffé, who co-wrote the script with Bruce Robinson. The story follows the Manhattan Project, the secret Allied endeavor to develop the first nuclear weapons during World War II. The film is named after "Little Boy" and "Fat Man", the two bombs dropped on the Japanese cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, respectively. The film stars Paul Newman as Leslie Groves and Dwight Schultz as J. Robert Oppenheimer, with supporting roles filled by Bonnie Bedelia, John Cusack, Laura Dern, John C. McGinley and Natasha Richardson.

31ff19ca-8c5b-58df-9e24-8119fcc423d1.title: The Queen of Tupperware
31ff19ca-8c5b-58df-9e24-8119fcc423d1.summary: The Queen of Tupperware is a 49-minute episode of NPR's history podcast Throughline, released August 21, 2025, reported by NPR business correspondent Alina Selyukh and hosted by Rund Abdelfatah and Ramtin Arablouei. It tells the rise and fall of Brownie Wise, a divorced single mother in Detroit who began selling household products at home parties, then turned Earl Tupper's airtight plastic bowls into a national craze. By 1951 she was a vice president, and in 1954 she was the first woman on the cover of Business Week. A clash with Tupper, a stormy party that sent people to the hospital and her dismissal ended it, and the company then left her out of its own story. Underneath, the episode is about women's work in the 1950s, who gets recognition and who gets remembered. Historian Alison Clarke and biographer Bob Kealing are the guests. It mentions a violent marriage once, briefly.

32620915-e586-44de-9747-39def7d0b2b1.title: Push
32620915-e586-44de-9747-39def7d0b2b1.summary: "Push" is a song by American rock band Matchbox Twenty. It was released in 1997 as the second single from their debut album, Yourself or Someone Like You (1996). After landing "Long Day" on several rock radio stations paving the way, "Push" topped the US Modern Rock Tracks chart and became one of the band's signature songs.

330f5318-593c-4e37-9d36-aba3ed1a6ce5.title: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim
330f5318-593c-4e37-9d36-aba3ed1a6ce5.summary: Playing as the legendary Dragonborn, explore the region of Skyrim for adventure, thievery, deception, magic, and action to stop the return of the dragons and save Cyrodiil.

336d3ead-f4bf-564d-a071-b032f83309d1.title: The Internet and the Law: What Educators Need to Know
336d3ead-f4bf-564d-a071-b032f83309d1.summary: The Internet and the Law: What Educators Need to Know is a short handbook (about 110 pages) by Kathleen Conn, a lawyer and public school administrator, published by ASCD in 2002. Public schools were then bringing the Web, e-mail and other online tools into classrooms and offices, and the book sets out the legal questions that follow. Its chapters cover the foundations of school Internet law, freedom of expression, privacy, copyright (two chapters) and e-mail, with appendices on writing acceptable-use policies and on complying with the Children's Internet Protection Act. Underneath, it is about how teachers and school leaders can use the Internet while keeping students, staff and the school within the law. It was written in 2002, so later law is not covered. No review of it was found.

342e8344-a62b-4645-af60-545cb4a450e2.title: Cuphead
342e8344-a62b-4645-af60-545cb4a450e2.summary: Cuphead and his pal Mugman accidentally gamble their souls away to the devil, and must now go and collect all of his outstanding contracts to earn their souls back.

3501cd56-f216-49ff-b52a-c6c44d67db17.title: The Mill on the Floss
3501cd56-f216-49ff-b52a-c6c44d67db17.summary:
The story follows the lives of Tom and Maggie Tulliver, siblings growing up in the rural English countryside in the early 19th century. The Tulliver family lives at Dorlcote Mill, a family-owned mill on the banks of the Floss River.

The story explores the complex relationship between Tom and Maggie, who share a deep bond despite their differences in temperament and outlook. Tom is practical, rational, and adheres to societal conventions, while Maggie is imaginative, passionate, and rebellious.

As they navigate the challenges of adolescence and adulthood, Tom and Maggie encounter a series of trials and tribulations that test their loyalty to each other and their place within their family and community. Their lives are shaped by conflicts with their family members, particularly their father, Mr. Tulliver, and their aunt, Mrs. Glegg.

Maggie, in particular, struggles to reconcile her desires for independence and personal fulfillment with the expectations placed upon her by society and her family. Her romantic entanglements, particularly her love for Philip Wakem, the son of the Tullivers' sworn enemy, add further complexity to her journey.

352ff2ce-4c6e-4002-9940-1cfacb856507.title: The Power of Habit: Why We Do What We Do in Life and Business

36923bea-5311-5441-b461-4321851012cd.title: Holes
36923bea-5311-5441-b461-4321851012cd.summary: Holes is a novel by Louis Sachar, first published in 1998 by Farrar, Straus and Giroux. Stanley Yelnats, a teenager whose family blames a curse for its bad luck, is sent to Camp Green Lake, a juvenile correctional camp in the Texas desert, where each boy must dig a hole five feet wide and five feet deep every day. Woven through his story are the tale of a great-great-grandfather in Latvia and of Kate Barlow, a Texas schoolteacher turned outlaw. Underneath, the book is about friendship, fate and the way old wrongs reach into the present. It won the 1998 National Book Award for Young People's Literature and the 1999 Newbery Medal, and was made into a Disney film in 2003.

36ff37fa-90e2-46ac-bcb4-3246e0eebc38.title: Friends
36ff37fa-90e2-46ac-bcb4-3246e0eebc38.summary: Friends is an American television sitcom created by David Crane and Marta Kauffman, which aired on NBC from September 22, 1994, to May 6, 2004, lasting ten seasons. With an ensemble cast starring Jennifer Aniston, Courteney Cox, Lisa Kudrow, Matt LeBlanc, Matthew Perry and David Schwimmer, the show revolves around six friends in their 20s and early 30s who live in Manhattan, New York City. The original executive producers were Kevin S. Bright, Kauffman, and Crane.

3852b7c6-797d-48f4-a00e-0d6f3469be0f.title: Notre-Dame of Paris
3852b7c6-797d-48f4-a00e-0d6f3469be0f.summary: Notre-Dame of Paris, known in English as The Hunchback of Notre-Dame, is an 1831 novel by Victor Hugo, set in Paris in 1482. Quasimodo, the deaf bell-ringer of the cathedral, whose body makes others shun him, falls in love with Esmeralda, a Romani street dancer who shows him kindness. Both are destroyed by the obsession of Claude Frollo, the archdeacon who raised Quasimodo. Underneath, the novel is about how a society treats those it decides are outsiders, and about the cathedral itself, which Hugo wanted his readers to value and preserve. It remains one of the great Romantic novels and has been adapted many times for stage and screen.

386d25f7-2392-4a0e-b8e0-cbc070d39884.title: Brave New World
386d25f7-2392-4a0e-b8e0-cbc070d39884.summary:
In the World State, society is organized around principles of stability and uniformity. Citizens are engineered and conditioned from birth to fit into predetermined social roles. Human reproduction occurs through artificial means, and children are raised in government-run facilities where they are conditioned to accept their place in society.

The protagonist, Bernard Marx, feels disillusioned with the shallow and superficial nature of his society. He questions the lack of individuality and longs for genuine human connection. Bernard's curiosity leads him to explore forbidden areas of society, where he encounters ideas that challenge the status quo.

Bernard becomes acquainted with John the Savage, a man born outside of the World State's controlled environment. John's upbringing in a traditional society contrasts sharply with the sterile and mechanized world of the World State. His presence disrupts the carefully constructed order of the society, sparking curiosity and unrest among its citizens.

38eb6ab4-941b-482b-ab62-84e244ce8c23.title: Shake It Off (Taylor's Version)
38eb6ab4-941b-482b-ab62-84e244ce8c23.summary: "Shake It Off" is a song by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift and the lead single from her fifth studio album, 1989. She wrote the lyrics and composed the melody with its producers Max Martin and Shellback. Inspired by the media scrutiny on Swift's public image, the lyrics are about her indifference to detractors and their negative remarks. An uptempo dance-pop song, it features a looping drum beat, a saxophone line, and a handclap-based bridge. Big Machine Records released "Shake It Off" on August 19, 2014, to market 1989 as Swift's first pop album after her previous country-styled releases.

3a22fb38-bf89-45b1-ab06-64c071a9835c.title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
3a22fb38-bf89-45b1-ab06-64c071a9835c.summary: Manly Palmer Hall was a Canadian author, lecturer, astrologer and mystic. Over his 70-year career he gave thousands of lectures and published over 150 volumes, of which the best known is The Secret Teachings of All Ages (1928). In 1934 he founded the Philosophical Research Society in Los Angeles.

3b6c82b4-c46d-42a4-93e2-e2650d9169df.title: Diamond and Pearls
3b6c82b4-c46d-42a4-93e2-e2650d9169df.summary: "Diamonds and Pearls" paints a vivid picture of the singer's deep and passionate love for their partner. The lyrics convey the idea that material possessions like diamonds and pearls pale in comparison to the value of true love. Prince emphasizes that love is the most precious and enduring aspect of a relationship. The song suggests that despite external luxuries, the real wealth lies in the emotional connection and commitment between two people.

creators.name: Prince and The New Power Generation

3b710791-2d22-48a6-a076-08ee02eed439.title: Romeo and Juliet
3b710791-2d22-48a6-a076-08ee02eed439.summary:
The story is set in Verona, Italy, and revolves around two young lovers, Romeo Montague and Juliet Capulet, who belong to feuding families. The Montagues and Capulets have a long-standing feud that has caused tension and violence in the city.

Romeo attends a party at the Capulet household where he meets Juliet. Despite the enmity between their families, Romeo and Juliet fall deeply in love at first sight. They decide to get married secretly the next day.

The situation escalates as Tybalt, Juliet's cousin, challenges Romeo to a duel. Romeo tries to avoid the fight, but his friend Mercutio ends up fighting Tybalt and is killed. In a fit of rage, Romeo kills Tybalt and is subsequently banished from Verona.

To be with her love, Juliet devises a plan with Friar Laurence. She takes a potion that makes her appear dead, intending to awaken later and escape with Romeo. However, Romeo, unaware of the plan, believes Juliet is truly dead and rushes back to Verona.

Tragedy unfolds as Romeo finds Juliet seemingly lifeless. In despair, he takes his own life beside her. Juliet awakens to find Romeo dead and, devastated, takes her own life as well. The play concludes with the reconciliation of the feuding families, but it comes at the cost of the lives of their young heirs.

3d0c4dff-9aca-4826-b916-c9173f66a99b.title: The Master and Margarita
3d0c4dff-9aca-4826-b916-c9173f66a99b.summary:
This story intertwines multiple storylines set in Moscow during the 1930s. The primary plot revolves around the Devil, known as Woland, who visits Moscow with his retinue, including a talking cat named Behemoth. They cause chaos and expose the hypocrisy and corruption of Soviet society, targeting individuals who represent the oppressive regime.

Meanwhile, the Master, a disillusioned writer, and his lover Margarita struggle with personal and creative challenges. The Master has written a novel about Pontius Pilate, which serves as a commentary on the nature of good and evil. Margarita, desperate to reunite with the Master, makes a pact with Woland to become a witch and host a fantastical ball in his honor.

3deb0b2e-ffb0-4e5c-bf93-88c61194d934.title: To Someone from A Warm Climate (Uiscefhuaraithe)
3deb0b2e-ffb0-4e5c-bf93-88c61194d934.summary: "Someone from a Warm Climate" by Hozier is a poignant reflection on the emotional contrasts experienced in relationships and the environments we inhabit. The song captures the feeling of longing for a loved one, symbolized by the warmth and comfort of a tropical climate. It juxtaposes this warmth with the coldness or harshness of another place, possibly representing emotional distance or challenging phases in the relationship. Through vivid imagery and heartfelt lyrics, Hozier explores themes of love, separation, and the desire for connection despite the physical or emotional distances that might exist.

3e4288fe-dd35-48c2-97e3-948fcd5e4a6d.title: Get Out Of Bed
3e4288fe-dd35-48c2-97e3-948fcd5e4a6d.summary: Amy stays up very late watching TV and cannot be awakened for school. Everyone in the family tries to wake her using her/his own unique method. Finally the family decides to take Amy, bed and all, to school. There, Amy continues to sleep throughout the day in spite of all the activity going on around her. Amy's family carries her home in her bed, but she doesn't wake up until the next morning. When she goes to school, all of her classmates are fast asleep, and she is the only one awake.

3fd3689f-0216-45f3-974d-6491955a6e49.title: Mouse Paint
3fd3689f-0216-45f3-974d-6491955a6e49.summary: Three white mice find three jars of paint - red, blue, and yellow. They jump in and out, dance in the puddles, and discover some amazing things - things like green...and orange...and purple. Yet they never forget about the cat.

3fde0079-4cdf-42cb-a164-ea78f7f0eea8.title: Blurred Lines
3fde0079-4cdf-42cb-a164-ea78f7f0eea8.summary: "Blurred Lines" is a controversial song by Robin Thicke featuring T.I. and Pharrell Williams, released in 2013. The song generated significant attention, not only for its catchy and upbeat sound but also for the controversy surrounding its lyrics. The lyrics of "Blurred Lines" suggest a flirtatious interaction between a man and a woman, but the controversy arises from interpretations that the lyrics may convey a blurred line between consensual and non-consensual actions.

3ffd1756-d3ec-4e1f-ae9b-81637a6c9785.title: Arthur's New Puppy
3ffd1756-d3ec-4e1f-ae9b-81637a6c9785.summary: Arthur's new puppy causes problems when it tears the living room apart, wets on everything, and refuses to wear a leash.

403f0f83-5a9d-4a47-83a6-68bab4116ea8.title: The Go-Between
403f0f83-5a9d-4a47-83a6-68bab4116ea8.summary:
This story is set in England during the summer of 1900, revolving around a young boy named Leo Colston. Leo spends the summer at Brandham Hall, the estate of his wealthier school friend, Marcus Maudsley. As Leo becomes immersed in the lives of the Maudsley family, he unwittingly becomes a messenger or "go-between" for Marian, Marcus's older sister, and Ted Burgess, a tenant farmer.

Marian and Ted are engaged in a clandestine affair, which Leo discovers but doesn't fully understand due to his innocence. Leo's innocence and naivety serve as a lens through which the complexities of adult relationships and societal norms are explored.

As Leo becomes more entangled in the lives of Marian and Ted, he inadvertently becomes a pawn in a tragic love story marked by societal class differences and personal sacrifices. The consequences of his actions haunt Leo well into adulthood, as he reflects on the events of that fateful summer and the role he played in shaping the destinies of those around him.

408fd2d8-efa0-4dbb-a93d-a9395ca20682.title: The Whatifs
408fd2d8-efa0-4dbb-a93d-a9395ca20682.summary: Cora, always bothered by the Whatifs, grows much more anxious before her piano recital but a fellow performer helps her imagine what could go right, rather than wrong. Includes author's note about her own anxiety

4105928f-03ee-5664-bb5e-a775f6f359f2.title: The Crossover (TV series)
4105928f-03ee-5664-bb5e-a775f6f359f2.summary: The Crossover is an eight-episode drama released on Disney+ on April 5, 2023, adapted from Kwame Alexander's Newbery Medal-winning novel in verse. Created by Damani Johnson, with Alexander as an executive producer, it follows twin brothers Josh, nicknamed Filthy McNasty, and Jordan, called JB, basketball standouts who try to earn a place at a high school with a coach who sends players to the NBA. Josh narrates in poetry, with the grown Josh looking back in the voice of Daveed Diggs. Their father, Chuck, a former pro, coaches them and has a health scare; their mother, Crystal, works at their school and begins to pursue her own dreams. Underneath, it is about family, growing up, and what each brother wants for himself. It won the Children's and Family Emmy Award for Outstanding Young Teen Series.

412b5cea-fb61-4d88-bc9e-a36992c252e4.title: Spyro the Dragon
412b5cea-fb61-4d88-bc9e-a36992c252e4.summary: Spyro and his allies work together to save the land from a variety of ill-meaning foes and villains, often with wacky scenarios abound.

41b30b00-eb09-41d7-8dea-26e3a24e2fd1.title: Rise of the Planet of the Apes
41b30b00-eb09-41d7-8dea-26e3a24e2fd1.summary: A prequel to the 1968 film "Planet of the Apes", this film tells the story of how the apes became human-like intelligent because of scientific experiments to test drugs used on Alzheimer's patients and how these experiments begin an chain of events that will forever change the relationship between humans and apes.

41d58c79-960d-4b4a-83d2-8ee23b87b7a6.title: Treasure
41d58c79-960d-4b4a-83d2-8ee23b87b7a6.summary: "Treasure" by Bruno Mars is an upbeat and funky song that celebrates love and admiration for someone special. The song's lyrics express the narrator's feelings of infatuation and attraction, likening their love interest to a precious treasure that they want to cherish and protect. Throughout the song, Bruno Mars sings about wanting to give their love interest the world and expressing gratitude for their presence in their life. The catchy melody, retro-inspired production, and lively rhythm make "Treasure" a feel-good and infectious song that encourages listeners to dance and celebrate the joy of love.
