Overall, "Treasure" is a fun and uplifting anthem that captures the excitement and happiness of being in love

4211bc90-4118-5197-9aee-5e97d89af5a0.title: Sky Full of Elephants
4211bc90-4118-5197-9aee-5e97d89af5a0.summary: Sky Full of Elephants is the debut novel of Cebo Campbell, published by Simon & Schuster in 2024. It is set in a near-future United States where, in a single day, nearly every white American has died. A year later, Charlie Brunton, a Black professor of electric and solar power systems at Howard University who spent twenty years in prison for a crime he did not commit, gets a call from Sidney, the nineteen-year-old daughter he never knew. Raised to think of herself as white, Sidney is alone and traumatized, and she wants to find her mother's surviving relatives in Alabama. The two travel south together and reach Mobile, now the center of a Black society run by communal systems. Underneath, the book is an allegory about racial identity, inherited trauma, the truth about the past and healing, and about a father and daughter learning to trust each other. It deals with mass death, wrongful conviction and racism. Reviews are divided: Publishers Weekly gave it a star and Kirkus found it plodding.

4267889e-7d8c-4fe6-9f92-ecd7ef52b4e8.title: The Grapes of Wrath
4267889e-7d8c-4fe6-9f92-ecd7ef52b4e8.summary:
This story follows the journey of the Joad family, tenant farmers from Oklahoma, as they are forced to leave their land during the Dust Bowl era of the 1930s. The novel begins with Tom Joad's release from prison and his return home to find his family preparing to leave for California in search of work and a better life.

As the Joads travel westward in their dilapidated truck, they encounter hardship, prejudice, and exploitation along the way. They join thousands of other migrant workers in California's agricultural valleys, only to face exploitation by wealthy landowners and harsh working conditions.

Throughout the novel, Steinbeck portrays the resilience and dignity of the Joad family in the face of adversity. Despite their struggles, they cling to their sense of family and community, finding strength in their shared experiences and solidarity with other migrant workers.

42ad2939-ba82-471e-a52d-1b6234c63031.title: Dinosaur Valentine
42ad2939-ba82-471e-a52d-1b6234c63031.summary: This is the story of a young dinosaur named Digger who wants to make the perfect Valentine's Day card for his friend Stego. Throughout the book, Digger embarks on a charming adventure filled with creativity and friendship as he gathers materials and creates his special Valentine's Day surprise.

433f64cd-1030-420c-a783-8f12054df867.title: Mirrors
433f64cd-1030-420c-a783-8f12054df867.summary: "Mirrors" is a song by Justin Timberlake from his third studio album, "The 20/20 Experience," released in 2013. The song is notable for its length (over eight minutes) and its exploration of themes related to love and self-discovery. "Mirrors" serves as a reflection on love and the impact a significant other can have on an individual's life. The lyrics suggest that the person Timberlake is singing about is like a mirror, reflecting back his true self. The metaphor of a mirror is used to convey a deep emotional connection and a sense of completion. The song was met with positive reviews by critics upon release and received a Grammy Award nomination for Best Pop Solo Performance. Its music video won two MTV Video Music Awards, including Video of the Year.

4393ab57-95d1-4932-aa73-9df19d3b2db4.title: The Paper Bag Princess
4393ab57-95d1-4932-aa73-9df19d3b2db4.summary:
The story revolves around a princess named Elizabeth and a dragon who wreaks havoc in her kingdom. The traditional fairy tale narrative takes an unexpected turn when the dragon kidnaps Princess Elizabeth's betrothed, Prince Ronald, and destroys her castle.

Left with nothing but a paper bag to wear (as her clothes were burnt in the dragon's attack), Elizabeth embarks on a courageous journey to rescue Prince Ronald. Along the way, she cleverly outsmarts the dragon using her intelligence and resourcefulness. When she finally confronts Prince Ronald, he criticizes her disheveled appearance, expecting her to look more like a princess.

In a surprising twist, Elizabeth realizes that Prince Ronald is not worthy of her love and decides to live happily ever after on her own terms, without the need for a prince.

43a99514-3014-45b9-a4c4-b48a7036ad61.title: The Sun Also Rises
43a99514-3014-45b9-a4c4-b48a7036ad61.summary: The Sun Also Rises is the first novel by the American writer Ernest Hemingway. It portrays American and British expatriates who travel along the Camino de Santiago from Paris to the Festival of San Fermín in Pamplona and watch the running of the bulls and the bullfights. An early modernist novel, it received mixed reviews upon publication. Hemingway biographer Jeffrey Meyers writes that it is now "recognized as Hemingway's greatest work" and Hemingway scholar Linda Wagner-Martin calls it his most important novel. The novel was published in the United States in October 1926 by Scribner's. A year later, Jonathan Cape published the novel in London under the title Fiesta. It remains in print.

4456f4c9-e864-42d4-b937-2d7d0a57a6f5.title: Extra Yarn
4456f4c9-e864-42d4-b937-2d7d0a57a6f5.summary: Extra Yarn is a 2012 picture book written by Mac Barnett and illustrated by Jon Klassen. The book tells the story of a girl named Annabelle who knits for everyone in her town with a supply of yarn, until an archduke wants the yarn for himself. The book was a recipient of the 2013 Caldecott Honor for its illustrations. It received a starred review from Publishers Weekly.

44c42259-5932-46bc-87c2-07710746f144.title: Educated
44c42259-5932-46bc-87c2-07710746f144.summary:
Educated is a powerful memoir by Tara Westover, who grew up in a strict and isolated survivalist family in rural Idaho. Her parents, deeply distrustful of the government and modern medicine, did not send her to school or allow her to see doctors. Instead, Tara spent her childhood working in her father’s junkyard and preparing for the "end of days."

Despite never attending school, she teaches herself enough to take the ACT and is admitted to Brigham Young University at age 17. This journey opens her eyes to the world beyond her family's beliefs, leading her to study at Harvard and Cambridge University. Along the way, she struggles with her family’s expectations, her own identity, and the emotional cost of breaking free.

At its core, Educated is about resilience, self-discovery, and the power of knowledge. It’s an inspiring story for teens and adults about overcoming obstacles and forging your own path.

4633bc1e-1edd-40b5-9754-fc48f3677e57.title: Stardew Valley
4633bc1e-1edd-40b5-9754-fc48f3677e57.summary: In his will, your grandfather leaves you his old far in the hops that you can settle down and live a more peaceful life in Stardew Valley

46e0545c-4086-4af1-a454-26794ed3d871.title: Marvel's Spider-Man
46e0545c-4086-4af1-a454-26794ed3d871.summary: Peter Parker contends with supervillains and personal life management just as a power vacuum opens up in NYC's criminal underworld.

46e1fb5f-a54d-440b-b732-464e3168009c.title: Bunny My Honey
46e1fb5f-a54d-440b-b732-464e3168009c.summary: When Bunny gets lost and can't find his mother, he fears that Mummy and his friends may not be able to find him to take him home

49180c95-f75d-4a31-981c-47e0d61e1682.title: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion
49180c95-f75d-4a31-981c-47e0d61e1682.summary: In the final days of the 3rd Era, the forces of Oblivion seek to invade Tamriel, and it is up to you to help stop them.

49735fed-17aa-4517-9d6f-40b2889927f7.title: Be Who You Are
49735fed-17aa-4517-9d6f-40b2889927f7.summary: Picture book encouraging kids to be proud of what makes them unique, where they come from, and how they express themselves and see the world.

49ed090a-b469-4453-a8d5-3f515a5b4c6e.title: The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
49ed090a-b469-4453-a8d5-3f515a5b4c6e.summary:
This story, set in the pre-Civil War South, follows the journey of a young boy named Huck Finn as he travels down the Mississippi River with an escaped slave named Jim.

Huck Finn, who has been raised by the Widow Douglas, finds himself torn between his conscience and the laws and customs of society. When Huck's abusive father returns, threatening to take him away, Huck fakes his own death and escapes down the river with Jim, seeking freedom from his oppressive life.

As they journey together, Huck and Jim encounter a series of colorful characters and have various adventures along the river. Through their experiences, Huck learns about the complexities of human nature and begins to question the moral values and beliefs that have been instilled in him.

4b0e302d-accf-4e13-b429-e0b034b72ad2.title: The Paperboy
4b0e302d-accf-4e13-b429-e0b034b72ad2.summary: The paperboy and his dog enjoy the solitude each morning rain or shine to deliver newspapers in their neighborhood.

4b0f0898-5b76-4464-8062-82245f2ae0e5.title: Super Mario 64
4b0f0898-5b76-4464-8062-82245f2ae0e5.summary: Mario ventures into Princess Peach's castle to try and rescue her from the clutches of Bowser.

4b771833-1972-4230-bd0b-9a7a1b9df46f.title: There Was a Bold Lady Who Wanted a Star
4b771833-1972-4230-bd0b-9a7a1b9df46f.summary: This is a story of a determined lady who sets out on a quest to capture a star. The narrative follows her adventures as she tries various creative and bold methods to reach the star, including climbing a ladder and using a trampoline. However, each attempt presents its own challenges, and the lady learns that her ambition requires resilience and creativity. Ultimately, her journey is about the joy of pursuing dreams and the imaginative solutions one can find along the way. The story encourages readers to embrace their aspirations and think outside the box, showcasing the importance of perseverance and imagination in achieving one's goals.

4c089d04-b221-4c98-b8c6-c44f5132aad7.title: The Coffee Bean for Kids: A Simple Lesson to Create Positive Change
4c089d04-b221-4c98-b8c6-c44f5132aad7.summary: The story follows Gavin, a young boy starting the school year in a new town. One day, his teacher--Mrs. Spring--tells him the story of the carrot, egg, and coffee bean. With Gavin's new understanding of the coffee bean, and its power to transform the environment around it, he changes his outlook, makes new friends, and becomes a positive influence on those around him.

4d51c19d-167d-4b3a-9ea9-254ff37df714.title: Ulysses
4d51c19d-167d-4b3a-9ea9-254ff37df714.summary: Ulysses is a modernist novel by the Irish writer James Joyce. Parts of it were first serialized in the American journal The Little Review from March 1918 to December 1920, and the entire work was published in Paris by Sylvia Beach on 2 February 1922, Joyce's fortieth birthday. It is considered one of the most important works of modernist literature and has been called "a demonstration and summation of the entire movement." According to the writer Declan Kiberd, "before Joyce, no writer of fiction had so foregrounded the process of thinking."

4e9e9116-f3c2-4b06-8dbf-2f97a5869ef2.title: Big Red Barn
4e9e9116-f3c2-4b06-8dbf-2f97a5869ef2.summary: The story of various farm animals and how their activities revolve around a big red barn

4ead01d4-dffb-434b-a817-f7b49757b551.title: Atlas Shrugged
4ead01d4-dffb-434b-a817-f7b49757b551.summary: Atlas Shrugged is a 1957 novel by Ayn Rand. It is her longest novel, the fourth and final one published during her lifetime, and the one she considered her magnum opus in the realm of fiction writing. She described the theme of Atlas Shrugged as "the role of man's mind in existence" and it includes elements of science fiction, mystery and romance. The book explores a number of philosophical themes from which Rand would subsequently develop Objectivism, including reason, property rights, individualism, libertarianism and capitalism, and depicts what Rand saw as the failures of governmental coercion. Of Rand's works of fiction, it contains her most extensive statement of her philosophical system.

4ec98637-46a3-49bd-98bd-a536cefa1798.title: Celebrations
4ec98637-46a3-49bd-98bd-a536cefa1798.summary: A collection of poems on the holidays of the year, from New Year's Day through Martin Luther King Day, Passover, Labor Day, Halloween, and others, to Christmas Eve.

4ee4d6fd-c120-46c5-8ad8-17795c3b0ac5.title: What if the Zebras Lost Their Stripes?
4ee4d6fd-c120-46c5-8ad8-17795c3b0ac5.summary: If the zebras lost their stripes and became different from one another, some white and some black, would they turn and fight each other and stop living life as loving friends? This story examines issues of racial and ethnic diversity. It inspires children to explore their own identities and extend compassion toward all.

4f38ffc7-13f4-4a9f-ad82-b5ee6ba0594c.title: Hogwarts Legacy
4f38ffc7-13f4-4a9f-ad82-b5ee6ba0594c.summary: Uncover ancient magic, learn spells, uncover secrets, and defeat the forces of darkness as a new student of Hogwarts.

516b4f4d-68c9-49b6-9537-558511c0d091.title: Wide Sargasso Sea
516b4f4d-68c9-49b6-9537-558511c0d091.summary:
The story serves as a prequel to Charlotte Brontë's classic novel "Jane Eyre" and explores the backstory of Bertha Mason, the "madwoman in the attic" from Brontë's novel. 
Set in Jamaica during the early 19th century, it tells the story of Antoinette Cosway, a young Creole woman of mixed European and Caribbean descent. Born into a family that has fallen from wealth and prominence, Antoinette struggles to find her place in a society marked by racial tensions and colonial oppression.

As a child, Antoinette witnesses the decline of her family's estate, Coulibri, and experiences trauma and loss. She later marries an Englishman, Mr. Rochester, who takes her to his estate in England. However, their marriage is fraught with tensions and misunderstandings, exacerbated by racial and cultural differences.

Antoinette's descent into madness mirrors the unraveling of her identity and the erasure of her Caribbean heritage. The novel explores themes of identity, displacement, and the legacy of colonialism, as well as the complexities of power and control within marriage and society. Jean Rhys wrote it in 1966 to give a voice and a history to Bertha Mason, the woman locked away in Jane Eyre.

517dbd82-366e-42e2-a824-93b9f7b9626a.title: Sid Meier's: Civilization VI
517dbd82-366e-42e2-a824-93b9f7b9626a.summary: Build your civilization across the breadth of human history, from primitive tribal societies to a Post-Singularity future, all while contending with your society and other civilizations.

52cdb03e-446d-4554-950e-8b2a4e04ac76.title: Horizon Zero Dawn
52cdb03e-446d-4554-950e-8b2a4e04ac76.summary: Play as Aloy as you explore the far future Earth, fight animalistic machines, forge tribal alliances, and uncover the mysteries of the past.

53851715-2257-4af2-b22b-67d07cd9c3ce.title: The Outsiders
53851715-2257-4af2-b22b-67d07cd9c3ce.summary: The story follows the struggles of Ponyboy Curtis, a teenager from a lower-class background, and his group of friends, known as the Greasers. The Greasers are constantly at odds with the affluent Socs, or Socials, leading to conflicts and violence between the two groups. After a violent encounter leaves one of the Socs dead, Ponyboy and his friend Johnny go on the run, leading to a series of events that test their loyalty, friendship, and sense of identity.

5516a02c-ea62-5ee7-afd4-1df3c3869246.title: Out of My Dreams
5516a02c-ea62-5ee7-afd4-1df3c3869246.summary: Out of My Dreams is the third novel in Sharon M. Draper's Out of My Mind series, published by Atheneum in September 2024. Twelve-year-old Melody Brooks has cerebral palsy and cannot speak. When she sees her elderly neighbor, Miss Gertie, fall, she uses her talking board to call 911, and her quick action makes her a local hero. Miss Gertie turns out to be a former film star, and the attention leads to an invitation for Melody to speak for the United States at an international symposium in London for young people with different abilities. There she meets kids from other places who want a more equal world, runs into barriers such as a venue that is not accessible, and works toward a speech that will matter. Reviewers praise its warmth and the way it shows the world through Melody's eyes.

55c3b12c-f52f-47dc-bfb5-af200eec55f9.title: The Brothers Karamazov
55c3b12c-f52f-47dc-bfb5-af200eec55f9.summary: The Brothers Karamazov is a murder mystery, a courtroom drama, and an exploration of erotic rivalry in a series of triangular love affairs involving the "wicked and sentimental" Fyodor Pavlovich Karamazov and his three sons--the impulsive and sensual Dmitri; the coldly rational Ivan; and the healthy, red-cheeked young novice Alyosha. Through the gripping events of their story, Dostoevsky portrays the whole of Russian life, its social and spiritual striving, in what was both the golden age and a tragic turning point in Russian culture.

56229c21-8928-4934-b8fa-8f9a9d2677e5.title: Hardcore History: Destroyer of Worlds
56229c21-8928-4934-b8fa-8f9a9d2677e5.summary: What happens if human beings can’t handle the power of their own weaponry? This show  examines the dangerous early years of the Nuclear Age and humankind’s efforts to avoid self-destruction at the hands of its own creation.

56f91846-9035-55f7-92d9-12c2b54d76ab.title: My Life with the Walter Boys
56f91846-9035-55f7-92d9-12c2b54d76ab.summary: My Life with the Walter Boys is a young adult novel by Ali Novak, published in print in 2014 by Sourcebooks Fire. Jackie Howard, a high-achieving teenager from New York City, loses her parents in a car accident and moves to a Colorado ranch to live with her late mother's best friend, Katherine Walter, whose household holds twelve children. Jackie, who has always tried to be perfect, finds the loud, crowded home hard to live in, but she slowly bonds with the family, and two of the Walter sons begin to show romantic interest in her. Underneath, the book is about grief, about learning that perfection is not the only road to love, and about finding a new place to belong. It began as a story the author wrote as a teenager and posted online, was nominated for a Goodreads Choice Award in 2015, and was adapted as a Netflix series in 2023.

575c289a-1bf6-5860-b6d6-6e991651f965.title: Bad Education
575c289a-1bf6-5860-b6d6-6e991651f965.summary: Bad Education is a 2019 HBO Films crime drama directed by Cory Finley from a script by Mike Makowsky, who grew up in the school district at the center of the story. Hugh Jackman plays Frank Tassone, the admired superintendent of the Roslyn school district on Long Island, and Allison Janney plays his assistant superintendent, Pam Gluckin. Under them the high school climbs to one of the top rankings in the country, until a student reporter, Rachel Bhargava, starts asking about a school construction project and notices that money is going where it should not. The film follows how the thefts were hidden, how they came to light, and what happens to the people involved. In real life about 11 million dollars was taken, which has been called the largest school theft in American history. The film is based on that case and on a 2004 New York magazine article. It premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2019, aired on HBO in April 2020, and won the Emmy for Outstanding Television Movie.

579585e9-8c42-54fe-be02-6f8d70975a44.title: Out of My Mind
579585e9-8c42-54fe-be02-6f8d70975a44.summary: Out of My Mind is a 2010 middle-grade novel by Sharon M. Draper, published by Atheneum Books for Young Readers. Melody Brooks is eleven and has cerebral palsy. She has never spoken a word and cannot control her body, but behind the silence is a sharp mind with a photographic memory and a love of words, and most people, including some of her teachers, assume she has nothing to say. When her school opens inclusion classes and she gets a computer that speaks for her, she joins the Whiz Kids quiz team and helps it win a regional title. Her new voice does not fix everything: classmates leave her out, the trip to the national finals goes wrong, and a family accident shows what it costs when no one can understand her. Underneath, the book is about being underestimated, being heard, and the difference between being nice to someone and truly including them. It received starred reviews and several state readers' awards, and became a Disney+ film in 2024.

57aa2d50-82c3-4edf-ad39-bb9fe4db67c2.title: I Capture the Castle
57aa2d50-82c3-4edf-ad39-bb9fe4db67c2.summary:
The story revolves around the Mortmain family, who live in relative poverty in a dilapidated castle owned by their eccentric father, James. The family consists of Cassandra, her older sister Rose, their younger brother Thomas, and their stepmother Topaz.

Cassandra narrates the family's struggles to make ends meet and their unconventional lifestyle. James, a once-famous author, suffers from writer's block and has not produced any work in years. The family's financial situation becomes even more precarious when their wealthy American landlords, the Cottons, arrive to inspect the estate.

As the Mortmain family navigates their financial woes, Cassandra and Rose become enamored with the idea of marrying into wealth to improve their circumstances. They become entangled in romantic entanglements with the Cottons' two eligible sons, Simon and Neil.

Throughout the novel, Cassandra records the family's trials and tribulations in her journal, capturing their hopes, dreams, and misadventures. As the story unfolds, Cassandra grapples with her own coming-of-age, navigating the complexities of love, identity, and family loyalty.

57d81904-128f-5792-b5a5-99118b3d0286.title: Out of My Mind
57d81904-128f-5792-b5a5-99118b3d0286.summary: Out of My Mind is a 2024 film made for Disney+, directed by Amber Sealey from a screenplay by Daniel Stiepleman and based on Sharon M. Draper's 2010 novel. It premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2024 and began streaming in November 2024. Melody Brooks is a sixth grader in 2002 who has cerebral palsy and uses a wheelchair. She cannot speak, but she has a sharp mind and a photographic memory. Phoebe-Rae Taylor, who also has cerebral palsy, plays Melody, and Jennifer Aniston voices her inner thoughts. Placed in a regular class for part of each day, Melody is underestimated and sometimes shut out. With an electronic voice device and a classmate who becomes a friend, she earns a place on the school's quiz team, and then she insists that the people around her listen. The film won a Peabody Award in the children's and youth category.

58555cdc-b75d-5056-964c-c0b3a29708d8.title: Ender's Game
58555cdc-b75d-5056-964c-c0b3a29708d8.summary: Ender's Game is a science fiction novel by Orson Scott Card, first published by Tor in 1985 and grown out of his 1977 short story of the same name. Earth has survived two invasions by an insect-like alien species, and its International Fleet trains gifted children in an orbiting Battle School to command the next fight. Ender Wiggin, a rare third child in a world that limits families to two, is kept apart from the other students by his teachers, rises through zero-gravity war games, and is sent to Command School for a final series of simulations. Underneath, the book asks what it costs to turn a child into a weapon, and whether understanding an enemy and destroying him can be the same act. It won the 1985 Nebula and 1986 Hugo awards and the 2008 Margaret A. Edwards Award, and was filmed in 2013.

585b98fe-7691-4a95-af72-16c8b279b569.title: One Fine Day
585b98fe-7691-4a95-af72-16c8b279b569.summary: An old fox loses his tail after stealing the old woman's milk. He encounters a series of challenges throughout his day. With each obstacle he faces, the fox must find a creative solution to overcome it and get his tail back.

58c93aa0-7686-5f7c-92bb-dabc1bec4492.title: Royal Swindle
58c93aa0-7686-5f7c-92bb-dabc1bec4492.summary: Royal Swindle is a true crime limited podcast series of eight weekly episodes, released from July 23 to September 3, 2026, by Blanchard House and USG Audio with Exactly Right Media, and hosted by journalist Becky Milligan. It tells of two Australian women, Evelyn Burton and Laila Andre, who arrived in England in 1996 and presented themselves as wealthy society women. One of them pitched an exclusive investment, and the pair were welcomed into horse-racing and old-money circles, even meeting Queen Elizabeth II, according to a Channel 4 documentary. A small-town detective tried to stop them but struggled to catch them. Milligan tracks down one of the women, who agrees to tell her story. A request filed under the UK's Freedom of Information Act describes both women as pleading guilty and being sentenced to prison. It is a story of fraud, not violence, told with some adult material and humor, and it is rated Explicit.

59c8bd2e-bbd6-49b6-9b10-1695d24979cd.title: Flotsam
59c8bd2e-bbd6-49b6-9b10-1695d24979cd.summary: Flotsam is a children's wordless picture book written and illustrated by David Wiesner. Published by Clarion/Houghton Mifflin in 2006, it was the 2007 winner of the Caldecott Medal; the third win for David Wiesner. The book contains illustrations of underwater life with no text to accompany them.

5aee167b-e61b-4429-b26d-023282c33215.title: Jane Eyre
5aee167b-e61b-4429-b26d-023282c33215.summary:
Jane Eyre is an orphaned young girl who is mistreated by her aunt and cousins after the death of her parents. She is sent to Lowood Institution, a harsh boarding school for orphaned girls, where she faces deprivation and cruelty but also finds solace in her studies and friendships.

As a young woman, Jane takes up a position as a governess at Thornfield Hall, where she meets the brooding and enigmatic Mr. Rochester, the master of the estate. Despite their differences in social standing, Jane and Rochester develop a deep connection and fall in love.

However, Thornfield Hall holds dark secrets, including the presence of a mysterious woman named Bertha Mason, whom Rochester keeps hidden away. Jane's happiness is shattered when she learns of Rochester's plans to marry another woman for convenience, prompting her to flee Thornfield in search of independence and self-respect.

Jane eventually finds refuge at Moor House, where she discovers that she has wealthy relatives. She learns valuable lessons about love, forgiveness, and the importance of staying true to oneself. Eventually, Jane's integrity and strength of character lead her back to Rochester, where she finds true happiness and fulfillment in marriage.

5b636d5b-12b6-5e85-83e7-b08e66f4d1e3.title: Betsy and the Great World
5b636d5b-12b6-5e85-83e7-b08e66f4d1e3.summary: Betsy and the Great World, published in 1952, is the ninth book in Maud Hart Lovelace's Betsy-Tacy series. In January 1914, twenty-one-year-old Betsy Ray, an aspiring writer with an unhappy college year and a broken romance behind her, sets out on a long trip around Europe on her own for the first time. She sails across the ocean, stays for a long stretch in Munich and in Venice, and later in London, where the book includes an account of England declaring war. Along the way she makes friends, is courted by an Italian man named Marco, and keeps thinking about her high school sweetheart Joe Willard back in Minnesota. Underneath, the book is about growing up, independence and finding out what you want, set in the last peaceful months before the First World War. Lovelace based it on the journals she kept on her own 1914 trip. It is written for older readers than the early books in the series.

5b78e734-7ca0-5b6c-a051-ddc230ad1db6.title: The One and Only Bob
5b78e734-7ca0-5b6c-a051-ddc230ad1db6.summary: The One and Only Bob is a 2020 novel by Katherine Applegate, illustrated by Patricia Castelao and published by Harper, the sequel to her Newbery-winning The One and Only Ivan. Bob, a tiny, wisecracking stray with some Chihuahua in him, tells the story. He now lives with a girl named Julia and her parents; her father works at a zoo and sanctuary where Bob's friends Ivan the gorilla and Ruby the elephant live. But a betrayal by humans when Bob was a puppy has left him distrustful, sure he is a bad dog, and still wondering whether his long-lost sister survived the day their littermates were lost. When a violent storm strikes, Bob sets out on a dangerous journey to find her, with help from Ivan and Ruby, and discovers courage he never knew he had and what friendship and family mean. Kirkus lists it as a New York Times bestseller.

5c0a64b0-b3a1-4aae-95ec-fb1ac2692e0c.title: The Invisible Man
5c0a64b0-b3a1-4aae-95ec-fb1ac2692e0c.summary: The Invisible Man is a science fiction novel by British writer H. G. Wells. Originally serialised in Pearson's Weekly in 1897, it was published as a novel the same year. The Invisible Man to whom the title refers is Griffin, a scientist who has devoted himself to research into optics and who invents a way to change a body's refractive index to that of air so that it neither absorbs nor reflects light. He carries out this procedure on himself and renders himself invisible, but fails in his attempt to reverse it. A practitioner of random and irresponsible violence, Griffin has become an iconic character in horror fiction.

5c11eede-385f-4c7f-870d-76da62a0cbf7.title: Artificial Condition: The Murderbot Diaries, 2
5c11eede-385f-4c7f-870d-76da62a0cbf7.summary: It has a dark past - one in which a number of humans were killed. A past that caused it to christen itself Murderbot. But it has only vague memories of the massacre that spawned that title, and it wants to know more. Teaming up with a research transport vessel named ART (you don't want to know what the A stands for), Murderbot heads to the mining facility where it went rogue. What it discovers will forever change the way it thinks ..

5c25f2b9-1754-4c99-bc0c-cb048756da88.title: Lolita
5c25f2b9-1754-4c99-bc0c-cb048756da88.summary: Lolita is a 1955 novel written by Russian-American novelist Vladimir Nabokov that addresses the controversial subject of hebephilia. The protagonist is a French literature professor who moves to New England and writes under the pseudonym Humbert Humbert. He describes his obsession with a 12-year-old "nymphet", Dolores Haze, whom he kidnaps and sexually abuses after becoming her stepfather. Privately, he calls her "Lolita", the Spanish nickname for Dolores. The novel was originally written in English, but fear of censorship in the U.S. and Britain led to it being first published in Paris, France, in 1955 by Olympia Press.

5c896030-3ead-597d-8992-d6515aea87c6.title: The Graces
5c896030-3ead-597d-8992-d6515aea87c6.summary: The Graces is a young adult fantasy novel by the British author Laure Eve, published in 2016 (Amulet Books in the United States, Faber & Faber in the United Kingdom). The narrator, River, is about fifteen and has moved with her mother to a town by the sea after her father disappeared. Everyone at school is fascinated by the Graces, a glamorous family rumored to be witches, and River sets out to be accepted by the twins Thalia and Fenrin and their younger sister Summer. Underneath, it is about wanting a place in a circle of friends, the stories people tell about themselves, and a magic that may or may not be real. After a close friend drowns, River's efforts to get inside the circle backfire. Kirkus called it powerful; it was shortlisted for the 2017 YA Book Prize and is the first book of a series.

5cea60cf-2fbc-408a-a4e1-64bebe817833.title: A Red Herring Without Mustard: a Flavia de Luce mystery
5cea60cf-2fbc-408a-a4e1-64bebe817833.summary: In the hamlet of Bishop’s Lacey, the insidiously clever and unflappable eleven-year-old sleuth Flavia de Luce had asked a Gypsy woman to tell her fortune—never expecting to later stumble across the poor soul, bludgeoned almost to death in the wee hours in her own caravan. Was this an act of retribution by those convinced that the soothsayer abducted a local child years ago? Certainly Flavia understands the bliss of settling scores; revenge is a delightful pastime when one has two odious older sisters. But how could this crime be connected to the missing baby? As the red herrings pile up, Flavia must sort through clues fishy and foul to untangle dark deeds and dangerous secrets.

5d8363f6-ac0a-4966-9fce-b74f12086c25.title: Trinitite
5d8363f6-ac0a-4966-9fce-b74f12086c25.summary: Trinitite, also known as atomsite or Alamogordo glass, is the glassy residue left on the desert floor after the plutonium-based Trinity nuclear bomb test on July 16, 1945, near Alamogordo, New Mexico. The glass is primarily made of arkosic sand composed of quartz grains and feldspar that was melted by the atomic blast. It was first academically described in American Mineralogist in 1948.

5da91130-ee2e-4b1f-bfdf-cbf9ad35a18f.title: The Heroes of Telemark
5da91130-ee2e-4b1f-bfdf-cbf9ad35a18f.summary: The Heroes of Telemark is a 1965 British war film directed by Anthony Mann based on the true story of the Norwegian heavy water sabotage during the Second World War from Skis Against the Atom, the memoirs of Norwegian resistance soldier Knut Haukelid. The film stars Kirk Douglas as Dr. Rolf Pedersen and Richard Harris as Knut Straud, along with Ulla Jacobsson as Anna Pedersen. It was filmed on location in Norway.

5dd567dc-5ce4-51a0-9c42-34662fbdfc39.title: Fudge
5dd567dc-5ce4-51a0-9c42-34662fbdfc39.summary: Fudge is an American children's sitcom that ran on ABC's Saturday morning schedule in 1995, based on Judy Blume's Fudge books, mainly Fudge-a-Mania. It followed a prime-time TV movie pilot, Fudge-a-Mania, directed and written by Bob Clark, and ran two seasons and 24 episodes of about twenty minutes each. Peter Hatcher (Jake Richardson), a fourth grader, tells what life is like with his mischievous younger brother Fudge (Luke Tarsitano), their parents (Eve Plumb and Forrest Witt) and his friends Jimmy Fargo and Sheila Tubman. Episodes include Fudge's first day of kindergarten, a school project that sparks a family fight and a week without sweets after Fudge gets four cavities. TV Guide twice listed it among its Ten Best Shows for Children. The production companies were Kevin Slattery Productions, Amblin Television and MCA Television Entertainment.

creators.name: Bob Clark
creators.role: director of the pilot movie, Fudge-a-Mania

5def05cf-83cd-4752-8681-b7c5490a297d.title: The Trip
5def05cf-83cd-4752-8681-b7c5490a297d.summary: When his family moves to a new neighborhood, Louie has to leave his friends behind. Playing alone, he creates a scene out of a shoebox. it has a magical effect, calling his imagination back to old friends, old times. Then the spell ends, and -- satisfyingly -- a real-life adventure begins as Louie joins some new friends for Halloween night.

5e274334-b2ac-4cb3-80b7-04050d88bbc0.title: Chutes and Ladders
5e274334-b2ac-4cb3-80b7-04050d88bbc0.summary: Make your way across the game board while trying to reach as many helpful ladders and avoiding detrimental slides.

5e6191fe-ae05-45de-a32e-5b915d54d68c.title: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas
5e6191fe-ae05-45de-a32e-5b915d54d68c.summary: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas is a science fiction adventure novel by the French writer Jules Verne. It is often considered a classic within both its genres and world literature.

5f1c9f87-63bc-464e-bdbc-6e81f8c055de.title: Mercy
5f1c9f87-63bc-464e-bdbc-6e81f8c055de.summary: The song is about the singer’s desire to break free from a manipulative and unfaithful lover. "Mercy" is autobiographical and is about "sexual liberty" and not doing something somebody else wants you to do.

5f739980-3bef-42e8-8558-5616efa612ab.title: Starting Over
5f739980-3bef-42e8-8558-5616efa612ab.summary: "Starting Over" is a song co-written and recorded by American singer-songwriter Chris Stapleton, released on August 28, 2020 as the lead single from his fourth studio album of the same name, released on November 13, 2020. The song features background vocals from Stapleton's wife Morgane.

60cf5e33-544b-4ecc-9c92-6946291166c8.title: Snow Friends
60cf5e33-544b-4ecc-9c92-6946291166c8.summary: Little Bear is delighted to discover the fresh layer of snow outside his cave. But he quickly realizes snow isn't much fun when he's playing by himself. So, he decides to build a friend out of snow. As he begins to work, Otter and Rabbit appear, ready to help him. Together the three friends build a huge snowman, their work enhanced by the magical, sparkling finish throughout the book. When he finishes his creation, Little Bear realizes that while he has found friends, the snowman is alone. The three animals work together to build a friend for "the bestest snowman in the world" so that he is no longer lonely!

61154feb-ed01-4ef0-9c47-8a0ef21e584d.title: The Water Princess
61154feb-ed01-4ef0-9c47-8a0ef21e584d.summary: With its wide sky and warm earth, Princess Gie Gie’s kingdom is a beautiful land. But clean drinking water is scarce in her small African village. And try as she might, Gie Gie cannot bring the water closer; she cannot make it run clearer. Every morning, she rises before the sun to make the long journey to the well. Instead of a crown, she wears a heavy pot on her head to collect the water. After the voyage home, after boiling the water to drink and clean with, Gie Gie thinks of the trip that tomorrow will bring. And she dreams. She dreams of a day when her village will have cool, crystal-clear water of its own.

61c1dc67-4776-4b64-bc4e-88f83bdda173.title: Flowers
61c1dc67-4776-4b64-bc4e-88f83bdda173.summary: A song by Miley Cyrus that reflects on her relationship with her ex-husband Liam Hemsworth. It can be considered a love letter to herself and to remember to let go of a frustrating situation and being able to say goodbye to someone you loved.

63f5df88-1b22-4e12-922d-dcbe002e6a12.title: Hoosiers
63f5df88-1b22-4e12-922d-dcbe002e6a12.summary: A 1986 American sports drama film written by Angelo Pizzo and directed by David Anspaugh in his feature directorial debut. It tells the story of a small-town Indiana high school basketball team that enters the state championship. It is inspired in part by the Milan High School team who won the 1954 state championship.

6526d410-ec0d-43d2-8a6e-23802e730939.title: A Color of His Own
6526d410-ec0d-43d2-8a6e-23802e730939.summary: A chameleon, sad that he takes on the appearance of his environment and does not have a color of his own like other animals embarks on a journey to find a color that will stay with him forever.

6666753f-053a-45c7-85ba-3e77415aa9fd.title: Dreams
6666753f-053a-45c7-85ba-3e77415aa9fd.summary: This song was written by Stevie Nicks and was about after the break up of her and Lindsey Buckingham. Lindsey had a need for freedom and Stevie wants him to do his own thing, make music the way he wants, do what he wants with his life. She also reminds him that he will never find someone like her. The lyrics convey the aftermath of a failed romantic relationship, with Nicks expressing feelings of heartbreak and reflection. Despite the pain, there's a sense of resilience and determination to move forward. The song captures the loneliness and isolation that can accompany the end of a significant relationship, while also showcasing the band's musical creativity and unique sound.

66a22a4d-b916-4e8f-81ad-d9364c825c15.title: Cloudy With a Chance of Meatballs
66a22a4d-b916-4e8f-81ad-d9364c825c15.summary: Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs is a children's book written by Judi Barrett and illustrated by Ron Barrett. It was first published in 1978 by Atheneum Books, followed by a 1982 trade paperback edition from sister company Aladdin Paperbacks. It is now published by Simon & Schuster. Based on a 2007 online poll, the National Education Association listed the book as one of its "Teachers' Top 100 Books for Children". It was one of the "Top 100 Picture Books" of all time in a 2012 poll by School Library Journal.

6730825a-cbf3-47e0-9730-a1d3850598ad.title: If I Could Turn Back Time
6730825a-cbf3-47e0-9730-a1d3850598ad.summary: "If I Could Turn Back Time" is a song performed by American singer and actress Cher from her 1989 nineteenth studio album, Heart of Stone. It was released as the album's lead single in June 1989, by Geffen Records. The song was written specifically for Cher by Diane Warren, who produced it in collaboration with Guy Roche. Cher was unmoved by a demo of the song sung by Warren, but Roche insisted she record it. The lyrics talk about the feelings of remorse due to bad deeds and the willingness to reverse time to make things right.

67e9dfb4-9a86-575a-8788-f94214269fe3.title: Careers in Gaming
67e9dfb4-9a86-575a-8788-f94214269fe3.summary: Careers in Gaming is a reference guide for teens and young adults, published in September 2020 by Salem Press with Grey House Publishing credited in the library record. It treats gaming as a field of work with technical, creative and business roles, many of which did not exist two or three decades ago. It profiles 27 occupations, among them video game designer, computer and video game programmer, quality assurance tester, esports player, voice actor and sound engineering technician. Each profile gives a snapshot of pay, outlook, education and working conditions, how to become one, similar jobs, and a day in the life, and many end with an interview with a working professional. Underneath, the book is about how a hobby people enjoy can become a living, and what training and skills lead there. Back matter explains John Holland's Holland Code for matching interests to careers and lists web resources.

684acd0b-9d99-4c6a-8dfd-b0da00d97d75.title: Treasure Island
684acd0b-9d99-4c6a-8dfd-b0da00d97d75.summary: Treasure Island is an adventure novel by Scottish author Robert Louis Stevenson, telling a story of "buccaneers and buried gold". It is considered a coming-of-age story and is noted for its atmosphere, characters, and action.

68e2746f-9a17-4405-ba08-7a52b6d2e41c.title: The Peace Book
68e2746f-9a17-4405-ba08-7a52b6d2e41c.summary: This story aims to teach young readers about the importance of understanding, tolerance, and compassion, promoting a positive and harmonious approach to life. The book is a celebration of diversity and a call to action for creating a world filled with kindness and understanding.

69566963-b60b-48b8-bc7f-e29441e62b13.title: Five Little Pumpkins
69566963-b60b-48b8-bc7f-e29441e62b13.summary: Count with the pumpkins from one to five as they each experience the fun and spookiness of Halloween night!

6a454f99-41e6-5022-af7b-6ea3d58a74c6.title: Betsy and Joe
6a454f99-41e6-5022-af7b-6ea3d58a74c6.summary: Betsy and Joe, published in 1948, is the eighth book in Maud Hart Lovelace's Betsy-Tacy series and covers Betsy Ray's senior year at Deep Valley High School in Minnesota, 1909 to 1910. Betsy wants to be an author and sends her stories to magazines. Joe Willard, an orphan who works to support himself, has long been her rival in English class and the school essay contest, and over the year the two grow close. Their friend Tony Markham also wants Betsy's attention; she turns down Joe's offer to take her to every dance out of fairness to Tony, and Joe's anger over it keeps them from speaking for months. Around them, Tacy and Tib have romances of their own, their circle of friends stages a play, and Betsy's older sister Julia studies opera in Europe. Underneath, it is about first love, friendship and choosing what you want from your future. It is a fictionalized version of the author's own senior year, illustrated by Vera Neville.

6b0fe849-ade6-4510-ad00-6378e0f1eb0a.title: Superstition
6b0fe849-ade6-4510-ad00-6378e0f1eb0a.summary: Stevie Wonder is preaching against the idea of being superstitious. The singer is asserting that people who hold to such beliefs are adding additional suffering to their lives. The lyrics emphasize the importance of taking control of one's destiny and not succumbing to irrational fears. The song's lively groove, driven by Wonder's distinctive vocals and instrumental prowess, contributes to its timeless appeal. Overall, "Superstition" is a powerful blend of musical innovation and a message of empowerment.

6bc2b32a-44c5-5c9a-a379-f0bbe132ca53.title: The War I Finally Won
6bc2b32a-44c5-5c9a-a379-f0bbe132ca53.summary: The War I Finally Won is a 2017 historical novel by Kimberly Brubaker Bradley, the sequel to The War That Saved My Life. It is set in England during World War II. Eleven-year-old Ada has had surgery to correct her clubfoot, and she and her little brother, Jamie, live in Kent with Susan, who is now their legal guardian. Ada's cruel mother has been killed in an air raid, but years of abuse have left Ada anxious and slow to trust. As the war presses closer, a wealthy neighbor, Lady Thorton, moves in with them, a Jewish girl from Germany named Ruth comes to stay, and losses reach the household. With her horse, Butter, and the people around her, Ada slowly learns that she deserves love. Underneath, the book is about healing from trauma, found family, and what war does to ordinary people at home. It was a New York Times bestseller and a Best Book of the Year pick for several outlets, including Kirkus.

6c7ea0fe-2830-47a4-9ef7-e196da1ead78.title: Little Lion Man
6c7ea0fe-2830-47a4-9ef7-e196da1ead78.summary: The song expresses the singer's regret and self-blame for a failed relationship. The song uses the metaphor of a lion man to represent the singer's courage and pride, which he feels he has lost. The song also suggests that the singer's actions have hurt someone else, possibly a younger brother, who will never be able to resolve his issues because of the singer's influence.

6c91a75a-075b-4889-9bd3-addc880140db.title: Harold and the Purple Crayon
6c91a75a-075b-4889-9bd3-addc880140db.summary:
the story revolves around a young boy named Harold who, armed with a purple crayon, embarks on a creative and imaginative adventure of his own making.
Throughout the story, Harold's drawings take him to different places and situations, showcasing the power of a creativity. Eventually, Harold draws his way back home, completing his adventurous night with the purple crayon.

6d266622-9a59-48b7-ba79-126353629c5e.title: Radiolab: Double Blasted
6d266622-9a59-48b7-ba79-126353629c5e.summary:
In early August of 1945, Tsutomu Yamaguchi had a run of the worst luck imaginable. A double blast of radiation left his future, and the future of his descendants, in doubt. In this short: an utterly amazing survival story that spans ... well, 4 billion years when you get down to it.

On the morning of August 6, 1945, Tsutomu Yamaguchi was in Hiroshima on a work trip. He was walking to the office when the first atomic bomb was dropped about a mile away. He survived, and eventually managed to get himself onto a train back to his hometown ... Nagasaki. The very next morning, as he tried to convince his boss that a single bomb could destroy a whole city, the second bomb dropped.

6d4d7ac4-eec0-5d5e-b06c-02aeca7fc5d4.title: Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events
6d4d7ac4-eec0-5d5e-b06c-02aeca7fc5d4.summary: Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events is a 2004 dark comedy directed by Brad Silberling and released by Paramount Pictures and DreamWorks Pictures. It adapts the first three books of Lemony Snicket's series: The Bad Beginning, The Reptile Room and The Wide Window. After a fire destroys their home and kills their parents, the Baudelaire orphans, Violet, Klaus and baby Sunny, are placed with a distant relative, Count Olaf, played by Jim Carrey, who wants their family fortune. Each time they are moved to a new guardian he returns in disguise, and the children answer with Violet's inventions, Klaus's reading and Sunny's teeth. A narrator, Lemony Snicket, keeps warning the audience that the story is not a happy one. Underneath, it is about loss, adults who do not listen, and how siblings protect one another. The film won the Academy Award for Best Makeup and is rated PG.

6ec1efee-b643-435c-bf4d-726641b8231c.title: Things Fall Apart
6ec1efee-b643-435c-bf4d-726641b8231c.summary:
This is the story of Okonkwo, a proud and ambitious Igbo warrior in pre-colonial Nigeria. Set in the late 19th century, it explores the impact of British colonialism on traditional African society and the tragic consequences of cultural clash and change.

Okonkwo, determined to distance himself from his father's legacy of weakness and failure, rises to prominence through his strength, hard work, and determination. He becomes a respected leader in his village of Umuofia and strives to uphold the values of his ancestors, including honor, bravery, and tradition.

However, Okonkwo's life is thrown into turmoil with the arrival of European missionaries and colonial administrators, who seek to impose their religion, laws, and customs on the Igbo people. As Christianity and Western influence spread, tensions rise between the traditionalists, who resist change, and those who embrace the new ways.

Throughout the novel, Okonkwo grapples with his own sense of identity and belonging in a rapidly changing world. His efforts to preserve the integrity of his culture and maintain his status as a warrior are ultimately thwarted by the forces of colonialism and modernity. Chinua Achebe wrote the novel in part as an answer to European novels about Africa, such as Joyce Cary's Mister Johnson, that showed Africans without a voice of their own.

6eee3b75-70b4-4d17-aeb5-b19c023086f5.title: How Do I Live
6eee3b75-70b4-4d17-aeb5-b19c023086f5.summary: "How Do I Live" by LeAnn Rimes is a country ballad that explores the theme of enduring love and the emotional struggle of dealing with a breakup and  the struggle of letting go of someone you love. The lyrics express the singer's deep emotional connection to a past relationship and the difficulty of moving on. It captures the essence of hope and longing, as well as the fear of losing someone precious. The lyrics in the chorus – “How do I live without you? / I want to know / How do I breathe without you? / If you ever go / How do I ever, ever survive? / How do I, how do I, oh how do I live?” – perfectly convey the pain and helplessness that one experiences when faced with the possibility of losing a loved one. The song is known for its powerful vocals and poignant lyrics, capturing the universal emotions associated with love, loss, and the quest for healing.

6f93fa09-c932-4e6e-9db3-3337d3a110df.title: The Beautiful Ones
6f93fa09-c932-4e6e-9db3-3337d3a110df.summary: They are the Beautiful Ones, Loisail’s most notable socialites, and this spring is Nina’s chance to join their ranks, courtesy of her well-connected cousin and his calculating wife. But the Grand Season has just begun, and already Nina’s debut has gone disastrously awry. She has always struggled to control her telekinesis—neighbors call her the Witch of Oldhouse—and the haphazard manifestations of her powers make her the subject of malicious gossip. When entertainer Hector Auvray arrives to town, Nina is dazzled. A telekinetic like her, he has traveled the world performing his talents for admiring audiences. He sees Nina not as a witch, but ripe with potential to master her power under his tutelage. With Hector’s help, Nina’s talent blossoms, as does her love for him. But great romances are for fairytales, and Hector is hiding a truth from Nina — and himself — that threatens to end their courtship before it truly begins.

6fd501d3-005a-47a6-971e-ab470d0e2452.title: Coral Reef Hideaway: The Story of a Clown Anemonefish
6fd501d3-005a-47a6-971e-ab470d0e2452.summary: A clown anemonefish, that lives in the delicate tentacles of a sea anemone, finds a mate; lays her eggs; and protects them from other coral reef animals until they hatch.

701f734e-e8ca-4156-8cc9-8208c627f008.title: The Notebook
701f734e-e8ca-4156-8cc9-8208c627f008.summary: The Notebook is the debut novel by American novelist Nicholas Sparks. Released in 1996, the romance novel was later adapted into a popular 2004 film of the same name.

71532d75-2418-4efe-a2b0-bf024a0c0089.title: All-American Muslim Girl
71532d75-2418-4efe-a2b0-bf024a0c0089.summary:
Allie Abraham has it all going for her - she's a straight-A student, with good friends and a close-knit family, and she's dating cute, popular, and sweet Wells Henderson.

One problem: Wells's father is Jack Henderson, America's most famous conservative shock jock...and Allie hasn't told Wells that her family is Muslim. It's not like Allie's religion is a secret, exactly. It's just that her parents don't practice and raised her to keep her Islamic heritage to herself. But as Allie witnesses ever-growing Islamophobia in her small town and across the nation, she begins to embrace her faith--studying it, practicing it, and facing hatred and misunderstanding for it. Who is Allie, if she sheds the façade of the "perfect" all-American girl? What does it mean to be a "Good Muslim?" And can a Muslim girl in America ever truly fit in?

731a98ef-539f-4d5f-ac76-47b1e26bcf77.title: Ted 2
731a98ef-539f-4d5f-ac76-47b1e26bcf77.summary: Ted 2 is a 2015 comedy directed by Seth MacFarlane, who also co-wrote it and voices Ted, the teddy bear who came to life, with Mark Wahlberg, Amanda Seyfried and Morgan Freeman. Ted marries Tami-Lynn and they hope to adopt a child, but the state of Massachusetts rules that Ted is property, not a person. With his best friend John and a young lawyer, Ted goes to court to prove he is a person with civil rights. The film is crude adult humor, with drug jokes and sexual content (rated R), wrapped around a story about being recognized as fully human. Reviews were mixed to negative, but it was a box office success.

73c075a2-a2f6-44a6-80ff-df9ccfff0dd8.title: Pumpkin Soup
73c075a2-a2f6-44a6-80ff-df9ccfff0dd8.summary: In the heart of the forest, three friends – Duck, Cat, and Squirrel – share a cozy home and a love for making pumpkin soup. Their harmonious routine is disrupted when Duck decides he wants to stir the soup, causing a rift between the friends. As Duck storms off, Cat and Squirrel are left feeling incomplete, realizing the true value of their friendship.

7439908e-6a20-4555-86e0-bf353e5d1b58.title: Last Stop on Market Street
7439908e-6a20-4555-86e0-bf353e5d1b58.summary: Last Stop on Market Street is a 2015 children's book written by American author Matt de la Peña and illustrated by Christian Robinson, which won the 2016 Newbery Medal, a Coretta Scott King Illustrator Honor, and a Caldecott Honor. The book follows a young boy named CJ as he learns to appreciate the beauty in everyday things during a bus ride. De la Peña and Robinson both drew on personal experiences when working together to create the book. Through its story and illustrations, Last Stop on Market Street tackles issues of race and class as they may be seen through the eyes of a young teen. Last Stop on Market Street was met with widespread acclaim after its release, receiving positive reviews from Kirkus Reviews and the New York Times Book Review amongst many others. Last Stop on Market Street's Newbery win was monumental, as it is extremely rare for picture books to be awarded this medal. In 2018, the children's book was adapted into a children's musical which has been performed by various children's theater groups across the country.

7481fa09-08b7-42af-a9d9-a8cce2bec568.title: Wagon Wheel
7481fa09-08b7-42af-a9d9-a8cce2bec568.summary: Wagon Wheel" by Darius Rucker is a country song that tells the story of a man's journey to reunite with his significant other. Originally written by Bob Dylan and later completed by Ketch Secor of Old Crow Medicine Show, the song has become a popular anthem of travel, longing, and love. The protagonist begins his journey in New England, hitchhiking down to North Carolina. He's determined to reach his loved one in Raleigh, emphasizing the distance and effort he's willing to go to be with her. Along the way, he encounters various challenges and experiences the kindness of strangers. The chorus reflects his optimistic and hopeful attitude, as he imagines being reunited with his love, feeling the warmth of her embrace, and finally finding a place to call home.

74aea9db-ceb2-404e-8361-4cd32494170f.title: Planting a Rainbow
74aea9db-ceb2-404e-8361-4cd32494170f.summary: The story follows the progress of a mother and daughter in their backyard as they plant bulbs, seeds, and seedlings and nurture their growth into flowers.

74e9e705-6545-4590-bbd1-27df28f5cf62.title: Circus
74e9e705-6545-4590-bbd1-27df28f5cf62.summary: “Circus” by Britney Spears is a commentary on the entertainment industry and the pressure that comes with fame. Spears portrays herself as a performer who loves the spotlight, but she also acknowledges the darker reality of the industry. Her role as the ring leader symbolizes her power and control, but it also highlights the pressure she faces as a performer.

7523d807-1ae2-4e1c-bc03-368c001e7884.title: Lavender Haze
7523d807-1ae2-4e1c-bc03-368c001e7884.summary:
“Lavender haze means the ‘all-encompassing love glow.’” Taylor heard the term on an episode of “Mad Men,” and a common phrase used in the ‘50s, to describe being in love.
This is a song about other weighing in on and giving opinions about a relationship.

7533926f-1956-474d-b06f-7cdc8664f7f0.title: Secret Garden
7533926f-1956-474d-b06f-7cdc8664f7f0.summary: "Secret Garden" is a song by American musician Bruce Springsteen. It was originally released as a single from his Greatest Hits album on February 27, 1995, on Columbia Records. Upon its initial release, it peaked at number 63 on the Billboard Hot 100.

75b29453-3daf-5853-b7ba-4ea54fb20cc4.title: The Story of the Trapp Family Singers
75b29453-3daf-5853-b7ba-4ea54fb20cc4.summary: The Story of the Trapp Family Singers is the 1949 memoir of Maria Augusta Trapp, published by J. B. Lippincott in Philadelphia. She tells the family's story from its beginnings in Salzburg: how a young postulant at Nonnberg Abbey was sent out to tutor a child of a widowed naval captain, Georg von Trapp, came to love his seven children, and married him in 1927; how the family lost its fortune in a bank failure, began to sing together with the help of a priest, Father Franz Wasner, and became a touring choir; and how they left Nazi-annexed Austria for the United States and settled in Stowe, Vermont. The book looks back on family tragedies, successes and the kindness of strangers. It was a best-seller and the source of two German films, the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical The Sound of Music, and its 1965 film. She wrote it in 1948, after her husband's death in 1947, to promote the family's singing group.

766fa7c8-6501-4671-b702-8e79d037aa64.title: It Looked Like Spilt Milk
766fa7c8-6501-4671-b702-8e79d037aa64.summary: It looks like spilt milk, but it also looks like a bird, an ice cream cone, and many other shapes.

76bfb590-8c52-4431-997b-941c2f56646c.title: The Man
76bfb590-8c52-4431-997b-941c2f56646c.summary: "The Man" is a song by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift from her seventh studio album, Lover (2019). Swift wrote and produced the song with Joel Little. "The Man" is an uptempo synth-pop and electropop song with flashy harmonies, murky synths, and rumbling beats. In the lyrics, Swift imagines how she would be treated if she were a man. The song received a positive reception from critics, who praised its feminist message for the greater good.

7910d3ad-f895-4f7c-8c2b-2f61a8b1cde1.title: The Crossover
7910d3ad-f895-4f7c-8c2b-2f61a8b1cde1.summary: The Crossover is a novel in verse by Kwame Alexander, published by Houghton Mifflin Harcourt in 2014. Josh Bell is a twelve-year-old eighth grader who tells the story in poems that move like a basketball game. He and his twin brother, Jordan, are the stars of their school team, coached at home by their father, a former standout player whose own advice, his Basketball Rules, runs through the book. When Jordan starts spending time with a new girl, Josh feels left behind, loses his temper, and is suspended from the team. Meanwhile their father ignores warning signs about his health. The book follows the brothers through the season to a loss that changes the family and a hard-won reconciliation. Underneath, it is about brothers growing apart, anger, and grief. It won the 2015 Newbery Medal and a Coretta Scott King Honor, and was adapted as a Disney+ series in 2023.

7abd3332-72e1-4f64-9ac8-dac4d811e587.title: Sunflower
7abd3332-72e1-4f64-9ac8-dac4d811e587.summary: "Sunflower" is a song performed by Post Malone and Swae Lee for the soundtrack of the animated film "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse," which was released in 2018.  The song's lyrics convey feelings of infatuation and the desire to be with someone special.

7b3df681-d749-41c8-9087-939ce76e9174.title: Click, Clack, Moo: Cows That Type
7b3df681-d749-41c8-9087-939ce76e9174.summary: The story revolves around a group of farm animals, particularly the cows in the barn, who discover an old typewriter. The cows start typing messages to the farmer, demanding better living conditions. They request electric blankets for the cold barn, but when the farmer refuses, the cows decide to go on strike and withhold their milk until their demands are met.

7b54cbf3-8e9b-47a7-9c02-c2680878efc8.title: Middlemarch
7b54cbf3-8e9b-47a7-9c02-c2680878efc8.summary:
This story follows the life of Dorothea Brooke. She marries the scholar Edward Casaubon, a man she mistakes for her soul mate. In a parallel story, young doctor Tertius Lydgate, who is equally idealistic, falls in love with the pretty but vain and superficial Rosamond Vincy, whom he marries to his ruin.
Eliot surrounds her main figures with a gallery of characters drawn from every social class, from laborers and shopkeepers to the rising middle class to members of the wealthy, landed gentry. Together they form an extraordinarily rich and precisely detailed portrait of English provincial life in the 1830s. But Dorothea’s and Lydgate’s struggles to retain their moral integrity in the midst of temptation and tragedy remind us that their world is very much like our own.

7bbfd90e-1897-4353-8531-4ce2708f2d34.title: Destiny 2
7bbfd90e-1897-4353-8531-4ce2708f2d34.summary: In the far future, the last remnants of Humanity fight against the forces of the Darkness with the aid of Guardians, resurrected individuals gifted the power of the Light who can save the solar system.

7bf91f54-15bb-4a87-90e4-4e3ddc19ea0b.title: DuckTales Remastered
7bf91f54-15bb-4a87-90e4-4e3ddc19ea0b.summary: Play as Scrooge McDuck and take back the treasures stolen by his rivals on an adventure that takes you across the world and even to outer space.

7cd38c83-bbdc-4c2f-8d57-9b8398addc23.title: Anna Karenina
7cd38c83-bbdc-4c2f-8d57-9b8398addc23.summary: Anna Karenina is a novel by the Russian author Leo Tolstoy, first published in book form in 1878. Considered to be one of the greatest works of literature ever written, Tolstoy himself called it his first true novel. It was initially released in serial installments from 1875 to 1877, all but the last part appearing in the periodical The Russian Messenger. When William Faulkner was asked to list what he thought were the three greatest novels, he replied: "Anna Karenina, Anna Karenina, and Anna Karenina".

7d559d6e-af47-5440-902b-b71af978d2df.title: Superfudge
7d559d6e-af47-5440-902b-b71af978d2df.summary: Superfudge is a novel by Judy Blume, published by E. P. Dutton in 1980 with a cover by Roy Doty, and the third book in her Fudge series. Peter Hatcher, now eleven and starting sixth grade, tells the story. His parents are expecting a baby, and the family moves from New York City to Princeton, New Jersey, for a year. Peter worries that the baby will push him out of the family, while his little brother Fudge, starting kindergarten, is jealous of the new sister, Tootsie, and causes trouble at school. Kirkus Reviews calls the tone light and breezy, with Peter's wry narration shaping the story. Blume says readers had long asked for another Fudge book. The Library of Congress files it under Siblings, Family life, Babies and Humorous stories. It won the BILBY Early Readers Award in 1990-91, according to Wikipedia.

7d9b66bc-5c64-4311-b5c4-0dba169f61df.title: Argo
7d9b66bc-5c64-4311-b5c4-0dba169f61df.summary: Argo is a 2012 American biographical historical thriller film directed, produced by, and starring Ben Affleck. The screenplay, written by Chris Terrio, was adapted from the 1999 memoir The Master of Disguise by U.S. C.I.A. operative Tony Mendez and the 2007 Wired article "The Great Escape: How the CIA Used a Fake Sci-Fi Flick to Rescue Americans from Tehran" written by Joshuah Bearman and edited by Nicholas Thompson. The film deals with the "Canadian Caper", in which Mendez led the rescue of six U.S. diplomats from Tehran, Iran, under the guise of filming a science-fiction film during the 1979–1981 Iran hostage crisis.

7dc3f1af-aa8b-41da-affb-08c4f54f0354.title: Percy Jackson & the Olympians: The Lightning Thief
7dc3f1af-aa8b-41da-affb-08c4f54f0354.summary:
"Percy Jackson and the Lightning Thief" is an enthralling tale that introduces readers to Percy Jackson, a 12-year-old boy who discovers he is a demigod, the offspring of a mortal mother and the Greek god Poseidon. The story begins with Percy facing various troubles in school and feeling like an outcast until strange occurrences start happening around him, signaling his true heritage.
    After a series of events, Percy finds himself at Camp Half-Blood, a refuge for demigods like himself. There, he learns about his divine lineage and the existence of a world where Greek gods and mythological creatures are very much real. Soon, he's thrust into an epic quest to prevent a catastrophic war among the gods when Zeus's lightning bolt goes missing, and Percy becomes the prime suspect.
    Accompanied by his loyal friend Grover, a satyr, and Annabeth, daughter of Athena, Percy embarks on a perilous journey across the United States to retrieve the stolen lightning bolt and clear his name. Along the way, they encounter numerous challenges, including battles with monsters and gods.
    Through these trials, Percy discovers his unique abilities as a son of Poseidon, develops friendships, and gains a deeper understanding of the world of gods and monsters. Percy must now navigate his newfound identity and confront the responsibilities that come with it.

7debe7d1-4541-4a33-a292-474af679a3a4.title: Bette Davis Eyes
7debe7d1-4541-4a33-a292-474af679a3a4.summary: Kim Carnes’ song “Bette Davis Eyes” is a tribute to the legendary American actress Bette Davis. The song describes a woman who has the same alluring eyes as Bette Davis, but the lyrics are a warning to be wary of her. The woman is seductive and will go out of her way to please the object of her affection.  Despite her reputation, she still manages to seduce men with her looks.

7ea10743-8b69-4189-af7d-40070ccbc70f.title: Ratchet and Clank: Rift Apart
7ea10743-8b69-4189-af7d-40070ccbc70f.summary: Ratchet and Clank are separated across the multiverse, and will need to use all the tools, allies, and technology at their disposal to reunite and defeat Doctor Nefarious before he can take over the multiverse.

7ec9ec9b-3ee8-4497-bcb8-4e74e17ff12f.title: The Sandwich Swap
7ec9ec9b-3ee8-4497-bcb8-4e74e17ff12f.summary: Lily and Salma are best friends. They like doing all the same things, and they always eat lunch together. Lily eats peanut butter and Salma eats hummus—but what's that between friends? It turns out, a lot. Before they know it, a food fight breaks out. Can Lily and Salma put aside their differences? Or will a sandwich come between them?

7f0dda56-b633-479d-a3a8-cef969d467e8.title: Another Country
7f0dda56-b633-479d-a3a8-cef969d467e8.summary:
This story is set in New York City during the 1950s. It follows Rufus Scott, a talented jazz musician grappling with his racial identity and inner turmoil, and his relationships with his friends and lovers. Rufus struggles with his sense of belonging in a society marked by racial injustice and prejudice, and his experiences reflect the broader societal tensions of the time.

The novel also follows Rufus' friends and acquaintances, including his white lover Leona, her husband Hugh, Rufus' sister Ida, and the struggling actor Vivaldo. Through their intersecting lives and relationships, Baldwin paints a vivid portrait of the complexities of human connection and the search for authenticity and belonging.

As the characters navigate love, friendship, betrayal, and loss, they confront their own prejudices, fears, and desires, leading to moments of profound introspection and self-discovery.

7fd04c7d-c2b4-4737-b991-5138dba53e99.title: Dr. Seuss's ABC
7fd04c7d-c2b4-4737-b991-5138dba53e99.summary: Dr. Seuss's ABC, otherwise referred to as The ABC, is a 1963 English language alphabet book written by Dr. Seuss starring two anthropomorphic yellow dogs named Ichabod and Izzy as they journey through the alphabet and meet characters whose names begin with each letter. It was read as an audiobook by British comedian Rik Mayall as part of the 2000 audio release The Dr. Seuss Collection.

8019ad75-b5d3-52d3-b8c4-2befa8e90d4c.title: Life During the Crusades
8019ad75-b5d3-52d3-b8c4-2befa8e90d4c.year: 1998 (Library of Congress record and copyright date c1998; Goodreads and some retailer listings say 1997 - see dropped.md)
8019ad75-b5d3-52d3-b8c4-2befa8e90d4c.summary: Life During the Crusades is a nonfiction history for young readers by Earle Rice, Jr., published in 1998 by Lucent Books in its Way People Live series. In 96 illustrated pages with maps, it describes daily life in both the Christian West and the Muslim East during the three centuries of holy war, and asks why the armies of Christendom took part and what they hoped to accomplish. Its pages take in knights, castles, the city of Jerusalem and leaders such as Saladin, Godfrey of Bouillon and Richard the Lionheart. Underneath, it is about what drove people to fight a religious war and how that war touched ordinary lives on both sides. A bibliography and index close the book. Encyclopedia.com lists Booklist and School Library Journal reviews of it from 1998.

806a299e-794c-4d12-a686-700e9ca5ff1f.title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
806a299e-794c-4d12-a686-700e9ca5ff1f.summary:
This story is narrated by Chief Bromden, a Native American patient in an Oregon mental institution. Chief Bromden feigns deafness and dumbness to avoid interactions with the controlling and oppressive staff.

The arrival of Randle P. McMurphy, a charismatic and rebellious new patient, disrupts the rigid and authoritarian environment of the institution. McMurphy challenges the authority of Nurse Ratched, the tyrannical head nurse, and encourages the other patients to assert their independence and reclaim their dignity.

As McMurphy rallies the patients against Nurse Ratched's manipulative tactics and psychological abuse, tensions escalate, leading to a series of confrontations and power struggles. McMurphy's defiance inspires hope and courage among the patients, but it also exposes their vulnerabilities and insecurities.

Ultimately, McMurphy's battle against Nurse Ratched culminates in a tragic and symbolic showdown, highlighting the clash between individual freedom and institutional control.

80e3249d-e97e-4c17-ad09-4938db468cb5.title: Persona 4 Golden
80e3249d-e97e-4c17-ad09-4938db468cb5.summary: A group of high school students in a sleepy mountain town find their lives turned upside down after a series of mysterious murders reveals a dark reality hiding within their televisions.

81eb0561-868c-432a-91ac-cdde2bd23cb0.title: Copenhagen
81eb0561-868c-432a-91ac-cdde2bd23cb0.summary: Copenhagen is a play by Michael Frayn, based on an event that occurred in Copenhagen in 1941, a meeting between the physicists Niels Bohr and Werner Heisenberg, who had been Bohr's student. It premiered in London in 1998, at the National Theatre, running for more than 300 performances, starring David Burke, Sara Kestelman, and Matthew Marsh.

8297209b-c235-4c43-96c5-47289122cac5.title: Trinity (video game)
8297209b-c235-4c43-96c5-47289122cac5.summary: Trinity is an interactive fiction video game written by Brian Moriarty and published in 1986 by Infocom. It is widely regarded as one of the company's best works.

835174b9-1348-457e-8e78-e25f39d32462.title: The Carrot Seed
835174b9-1348-457e-8e78-e25f39d32462.summary: The Carrot Seed is a 1945 children's book by Ruth Krauss. As of 2004, The Carrot Seed has been in print continuously since its first publication in 1945.

84b0a030-b147-4fb9-a66f-8b7693e187aa.title: Kingdom Hearts
84b0a030-b147-4fb9-a66f-8b7693e187aa.summary: Sora, a boy from Destiny Islands, suddenly finds his entire world turned upside down when his home and friends become lost to the Darkness; however, with the help of his new friends Donald and Goofy, they team up to try and save the universe.

84ce042e-2986-52c7-aa47-d0e9abbbd899.title: Mrs. Dalloway
84ce042e-2986-52c7-aa47-d0e9abbbd899.summary: Mrs. Dalloway is a novel by Virginia Woolf, first published in London by the Hogarth Press on 14 May 1925. It follows one June day in London in 1923. Clarissa Dalloway, fifty-one, goes out to buy flowers for the party she is giving that evening. As she walks she remembers her youth and an old suitor, Peter Walsh, who returns from India. Elsewhere in the city Septimus Warren Smith, a decorated veteran of the First World War, is haunted by shell shock while the doctors who see him dismiss his distress; his story ends in his death by suicide. Their lives touch only at the party. Underneath, the book is about time and memory, mental illness and how society treats it, and the gap between a person's inner life and the face they show. It is told in stream of consciousness, and Time magazine put it on its 2005 list of the best English-language novels since 1923.

8573660b-0657-4047-9127-dad33d4c96e2.title: Waiting for Winter
8573660b-0657-4047-9127-dad33d4c96e2.summary: Deer has told Squirrel how wonderful snow is. But Squirrel gets bored with the wait. With his friend Hedgehog they pass the time by singing and waking Bear. Soon things are falling from the sky, but they aren't snow. But eventually they find what snow is

85a622b2-9b4d-446d-8aad-9fc7eb9639c6.title: What Was I Made For?
85a622b2-9b4d-446d-8aad-9fc7eb9639c6.summary:
Billie Eilish, the young and talented singer-songwriter, has captivated millions with her unique sound and thought-provoking lyrics. One of her most powerful songs, “What Was I Made For?”, delves deep into the human experience and the search for purpose and meaning in life. With hauntingly beautiful melodies and poignant lyrics, this song resonates with listeners on a profound level.

In “What Was I Made For?”, Billie Eilish contemplates the existential questions that many of us face at some point in our lives. The song explores themes of identity, self-discovery, and the constant search for one’s place in the world. Eilish’s evocative lyrics touch on the vulnerability and confusion that arise when we question our purpose and significance in the grand scheme of things.

Throughout the song, Eilish portrays a sense of longing and yearning for clarity. She explores the idea that each individual holds a unique purpose but may struggle to define it. The lyrics invite listeners to reflect on their own experiences, connecting with their own insecurities and uncertainties. Eilish’s raw and emotive vocals, combined with the melancholic melodies, create an atmosphere of introspection and introspection.

8742dc52-36d3-41af-a0d2-c4357c6f592e.title: Hot Wheels Unleashed
8742dc52-36d3-41af-a0d2-c4357c6f592e.summary: Race dozens of Hot Wheels cars across crazy track layouts in environments made to scale.

87499949-a13f-46e6-9fc1-5a13e157a4e5.title: Axis and Allies
87499949-a13f-46e6-9fc1-5a13e157a4e5.summary: Assume the role of one of the major military powers of World War 2 in this grand strategy board game.

88edc437-43c8-4226-bfd6-117f3f26ea6c.title: Enola Gay Aircraft
88edc437-43c8-4226-bfd6-117f3f26ea6c.summary: The Enola Gay is a Boeing B-29 Superfortress bomber, named after Enola Gay Tibbets, the mother of the pilot, Colonel Paul Tibbets. On 6 August 1945, during the final stages of World War II, it became the first aircraft to drop an atomic bomb in warfare. The bomb, code-named "Little Boy", was targeted at the city of Hiroshima, Japan, and destroyed about three-quarters of the city. Enola Gay participated in the second nuclear attack as the weather reconnaissance aircraft for the primary target of Kokura. Clouds and drifting smoke resulted in Nagasaki, a secondary target, being bombed instead.

89507fc9-3e33-4854-92da-00d626438531.title: East of Eden
89507fc9-3e33-4854-92da-00d626438531.summary: East of Eden is a novel by American author and Nobel Prize winner John Steinbeck, published in September 1952. Many regard the work as Steinbeck's most ambitious novel, and Steinbeck himself considered it his magnum opus. Steinbeck said of East of Eden: "It has everything in it I have been able to learn about my craft or profession in all these years," and later said: "I think everything else I have written has been, in a sense, practice for this." Steinbeck originally addressed the novel to his young sons, Thom and John. Steinbeck wanted to describe the Salinas Valley for them in detail: the sights, sounds, smells and colors.

8983e2a4-363c-42c6-8c5d-64223ff09b21.title: Disney's Extreme Skate Adventure
8983e2a4-363c-42c6-8c5d-64223ff09b21.summary: Explore and skate through a variety of Disney worlds as yourself, or a selection of real kids and Disney characters.

89d6b5cc-f765-432c-ac86-6aa942a1835f.title: The Making of the Atomic Bomb
89d6b5cc-f765-432c-ac86-6aa942a1835f.summary: The Making of the Atomic Bomb is a history book written by the American journalist and historian Richard Rhodes, first published by Simon & Schuster in 1987. The book won multiple awards, including the Pulitzer Prize for General Nonfiction. The narrative covers people and events from early 20th century discoveries leading to the science of nuclear fission, through the Manhattan Project and the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

8a5f5fd9-ee35-4e52-a7fe-1ba315947e51.title: Manhattan (TV Series)
8a5f5fd9-ee35-4e52-a7fe-1ba315947e51.summary: Manhattan is an American drama television series based on the project of the same name that produced the first atomic weapons. While some historical figures appear in Manhattan, most characters are fictional, and the show is not intended to maintain historical accuracy.

8c2f6517-cd99-43d3-a113-9ec3ae227d34.title: DEFCON
8c2f6517-cd99-43d3-a113-9ec3ae227d34.summary: DEFCON is a real-time strategy game created by independent British game developer Introversion Software. The gameplay is a simulation of a global nuclear war, with the game's screen reminiscent of the "big boards" that visually represented thermonuclear war in films such as Dr. Strangelove, Fail-Safe, and especially WarGames.

8d0974af-5798-4ac1-8a3a-c38639ef0f16.title: Umbrella
8d0974af-5798-4ac1-8a3a-c38639ef0f16.summary: "Umbrella" by Rihanna is a song about loyalty, support, and standing by someone through thick and thin. The song's lyrics describe a person promising to be there for their partner during difficult times, offering protection and comfort like an umbrella in the rain.
