The metaphor of the umbrella is used to symbolize strength, shelter, and unwavering support. Throughout the song, Rihanna expresses her commitment to her partner, promising to be their protector and confidante. The song's catchy melody and memorable chorus contributed to its commercial success, making it one of Rihanna's most iconic and recognizable songs. Overall, "Umbrella" is a powerful anthem about love, loyalty, and resilience.

8d18134b-1f31-47cd-a2aa-b9162069e1f0.title: Where the Wild Things Are
8d18134b-1f31-47cd-a2aa-b9162069e1f0.summary:
After being sent to bed without supper for misbehaving, Max, a young boy, embarks on a whimsical journey to the land of the Wild Things.

In his bedroom, Max's imagination takes flight, and he sails across a vast ocean to a mysterious island inhabited by wild creatures. He encounters the Wild Things, large and fearsome beasts, and declares himself their king. Max revels in the wild rumpus, dancing and playing with the creatures.

However, despite the excitement, Max begins to feel a longing for home. He realizes that even as king of the Wild Things, he misses the comfort and security of his own bedroom. Ultimately, Max decides to return home, where he finds his supper waiting for him, still hot.

8e00988b-506a-5b10-8015-b348c76462ed.title: Cracking the Luftwaffe Codes: The Secrets of Bletchley Park
8e00988b-506a-5b10-8015-b348c76462ed.summary: Cracking the Luftwaffe Codes is a memoir by Gwen Watkins, a former member of the Women's Auxiliary Air Force, published by Greenhill Books in London in 2006 with a foreword by the historian Asa Briggs. Watkins was posted to Bletchley Park, the British codebreaking center, in 1942, where she worked on the German air force's codes and met and married the poet Vernon Watkins. The publisher says nothing had been written before about the German Air Section, and her book fills that gap. She describes her interview, the eccentric workplace and the people in it, how the codes were broken, the daily routine, and the winding down of the section at the war's end, all under the secrecy that kept Bletchley quiet for decades. She wrote it partly to answer a novel about Bletchley that she thought full of mistakes, and the book becomes an affectionate elegy for a vanished world.

8e2f5315-5719-4d8f-8167-5ce7e1f09797.title: Pete the Cat and the Missing Cupcakes
8e2f5315-5719-4d8f-8167-5ce7e1f09797.summary: Pete the Cat and his friends are busy as can be baking cupcakes for a party, and Pete can't wait to perform with his groovy band. But some of the cupcakes have gone missing! Who could have taken them?

904b15a9-2804-526c-be8a-7c6c450cc5ae.title: The Haunting of Hill House
904b15a9-2804-526c-be8a-7c6c450cc5ae.summary: The Haunting of Hill House is a novel by Shirley Jackson, first published in 1959 by Viking and a finalist for the 1960 National Book Award for fiction. Dr. Montague, who studies the supernatural, rents a notorious mansion for a summer and invites people with unusual experiences to join him. Two accept: Eleanor Vance, a shy woman who spent years caring for her demanding mother, and the lively Theodora. Luke, the heir to the house, joins them. Doors slam, cold spots appear and messages show up on the walls, and the house seems to single out Eleanor. Underneath, the book is about loneliness, the wish to belong, and fear that lives in a mind as much as in a house; it never settles whether the haunting is real. Stephen King and other writers have named it a high point of the haunted-house story. It has been adapted for film and television.

911c09eb-99db-490e-bb4b-5ab1e3dbdf7d.title: We've Only Just Begun
911c09eb-99db-490e-bb4b-5ab1e3dbdf7d.summary: "We've Only Just Begun" is a single by the Carpenters, written by Roger Nichols (music) and Paul Williams (lyrics). It was ranked at No. 414 on Rolling Stone magazine's list of "The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time."

91770e60-2c9e-5aee-96d1-7265ecaacb6a.title: Magnifica Humanitas
91770e60-2c9e-5aee-96d1-7265ecaacb6a.summary: Magnifica Humanitas (Latin for 'magnificent humanity') is the first encyclical of Pope Leo XIV, signed on May 15, 2026 and published on May 25, 2026, with the subtitle On Safeguarding the Human Person in the Time of Artificial Intelligence. An encyclical is a formal letter from the pope to the Catholic Church, and this one also speaks to everyone. It argues that human dignity must be the test of every new technology, and that artificial intelligence, however useful, lacks conscience and responsibility. Over an introduction, five chapters and a conclusion it looks at truth and disinformation, education and children's use of devices, work and jobs, data and control, hidden exploitation in technology's supply chains, and war and peace, and it proposes a 'civilization of love' built on justice and dialogue. Its central image sets the Tower of Babel against Nehemiah rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem. The full text is free from the Holy See, and print editions came out from several publishers in 2026.

917b0efd-f57c-4fb3-8808-8ddbdc71b8b3.title: Rooster's Off to See the World
917b0efd-f57c-4fb3-8808-8ddbdc71b8b3.summary: An introduction to the meaning of numbers and sets as a rooster, on his way to see the world, is joined by fourteen animals along the way.

9187c49e-f913-4223-8560-3d088c104a62.title: No Man's Sky
9187c49e-f913-4223-8560-3d088c104a62.summary: You are a nameless traveler exploring a procedurally generated galaxy where you can fly spaceships, buy space freighters, trade, study, and fight.

91f0b61b-784c-406d-8214-c95a0981fbb7.title: Blinding Lights
91f0b61b-784c-406d-8214-c95a0981fbb7.summary:
"Blinded Lights" means “Blinded by streetlights” as you drive during the nighttime towards the one you desperately want to see. Nothing could stop you from trying to go see that person, because you’re so lonely. While the lyrics of "Blinding Lights" primarily focus on themes of longing, desire, and the intoxicating feeling of being in love, the title and certain phrases within the song could be interpreted metaphorically. Some listeners have interpreted the "blinding lights" mentioned in the song as a metaphor for fame, success, or the allure of a fast-paced lifestyle.
Overall, "Blinding Lights" has been widely praised for its infectious energy and nostalgic sound, becoming one of The Weeknd's biggest hits.

921a0b38-7a19-52cb-b623-3603a2b86e25.title: The Enigma Girls: How Ten Teenagers Broke Ciphers, Kept Secrets, and Helped Win World War II
921a0b38-7a19-52cb-b623-3603a2b86e25.summary: The Enigma Girls, by Candace Fleming (Scholastic Focus, 2024), is narrative nonfiction about ten British teenagers who took secret wartime jobs at Bletchley Park, the code-breaking center in Buckinghamshire, during the Second World War. Fleming follows them from 1939 to 1945: summoned by a terse telegram to a place they had never heard of, they listened for coded radio messages, ran the huge Bombe machines that helped break German Enigma ciphers, translated and sorted decoded messages, and learned to keep a secret so well that most said nothing for decades. Underneath, the book is about young people doing work that mattered and went unrecognized, and about what staying silent cost. Chapters marked 'Top Secret' let readers try breaking a cipher themselves, and the book includes photographs and primary sources. It was a Robert F. Sibert Honor Book and earned starred reviews from Kirkus, The Horn Book and School Library Journal.

9222b7a4-7be7-4439-8362-b106e2b26955.title: The Physicists
9222b7a4-7be7-4439-8362-b106e2b26955.summary: The Physicists is a German satirical drama/tragic comedy written in 1961 by Swiss writer Friedrich Dürrenmatt. The play was mainly written as a result of the Second World War and many advances in science and nuclear technology. The play deals with questions of scientific ethics and humanity's general ability to manage its intellectual responsibility. It is often recognized as his most impressive yet most easily understood work.

9284fdc2-21de-5a03-9847-d5d6df489397.title: Throughline
9284fdc2-21de-5a03-9847-d5d6df489397.summary: Throughline is NPR's history podcast, launched on February 7, 2019 as the network's first show devoted to history. Each episode asks how we got here: it takes a current event, a political debate or a forgotten figure and goes back to the history that explains it, using interviews with historians, archival audio and a carefully built soundscape instead of lists of dates. Hosts Rund Abdelfatah and Ramtin Arablouei, who developed the show together, tell stories that range from ancient civilizations to modern politics, with a special interest in people and communities that are usually left out. It won a Peabody Award for a 2021 episode on Afghanistan and the 2022 iHeartRadio award for best history podcast, and since 2021 NPR has offered it to local public radio stations as a radio program. VAST holds one episode, The Queen of Tupperware.

93406c23-80cc-4db1-85cc-5b8ba1493395.title: Dark Souls
93406c23-80cc-4db1-85cc-5b8ba1493395.summary: In the last days of the Age of Fire, take on the role of the Lost Undead as you fight across Lordran, felling foes and fulfilling your destiny.

93933731-9964-40cb-96b4-8835fa1c20b5.title: The ABC Bunny
93933731-9964-40cb-96b4-8835fa1c20b5.summary: The ABC Bunny by Wanda Gág is a children's alphabet book, illustrated by the author in black and white, and hand lettered by her brother Howard. The music for the "ABC Song", included as a score in the book, was composed by the author's sister, Flavia.

93be2ae1-6b24-5c6e-b235-a4b7ff1ec860.title: Die Trapp-Familie
93be2ae1-6b24-5c6e-b235-a4b7ff1ec860.summary: Die Trapp-Familie (The Trapp Family) is a 1956 West German comedy drama directed by Wolfgang Liebeneiner from a script by George Hurdalek and Herbert Reinecker, based on Maria von Trapp's 1949 memoir. A postulant at Nonnberg Abbey is sent to look after the children of a widowed navy hero, a stern baron who runs his house like a submarine. She teaches the children to play and to sing; he sends her away, then hears the children's songs, falls in love and marries her. When the baron loses his fortune, a chaplain, Franz Wasner, encourages the family to sing for charity, and they find a following. After the Anschluss in 1938 the baron, unwilling to live under the Nazis, takes the family to the United States, where they keep performing and where their troubles are not over. It was one of the biggest West German hits of the 1950s and the inspiration for the 1959 Broadway musical The Sound of Music.

942cc698-5c30-4152-b22b-1f39b3fb537d.title: The Berenstain Bears Out West
942cc698-5c30-4152-b22b-1f39b3fb537d.summary: Yee-ha! The Bear family is flying over rivers and mountains to get to Uncle Tex's ranch. There is so much to see! Uncle Tex and Aunt Min have plenty of ways to share the fun of the West with the Bear family.

9467a609-8de9-4f70-8e75-175c948ba833.title: The Winter Fortress: The Epic Mission to Sabotage Hitler’s Atomic Bomb

9467ce1f-2693-438a-a372-73c3e79ae7d9.title: Star Wars: Episode IV - A New Hope
9467ce1f-2693-438a-a372-73c3e79ae7d9.summary: A young man named Luke Skywalker is thrust into the ultimate conflict of good and evil as he rescues the beautiful Princess Leia and joins the Rebel Alliance in defeating the Galactic Empire and their new weapon, the Death Star. He makes friends with Han Solo, his loyal companion, Chewbacca, and the wise Jedi Master, Ben Kenobi.

967071fe-de8f-44db-bff7-8c105a5955db.title: Clay Boy
967071fe-de8f-44db-bff7-8c105a5955db.summary: Wanting a son, an old man and woman make a clay boy who comes to life and begins eating everything in sight until he meets a clever goat

96c5b69f-0c92-4754-8eb7-11f767d1a35a.title: Foolish Games
96c5b69f-0c92-4754-8eb7-11f767d1a35a.summary: "Foolish Games" is a song by Jewel and is a heartfelt ballad that explores the pain and frustration of unrequited love. Jewel uses poetic lyrics to convey the emotional toll of being in a relationship where one person's feelings are not reciprocated. The theme revolves around the sacrifices made in the name of love and the realization that some love can be foolish and unfulfilling. The song gained popularity for its soulful vocals and poignant lyrics, contributing to Jewel's success as a singer-songwriter.

97c5541c-6fd8-5994-8cb6-8fe564bb5a9c.title: Divergent
97c5541c-6fd8-5994-8cb6-8fe564bb5a9c.summary: Divergent is a young adult dystopian novel by Veronica Roth, first published in 2011 by Katherine Tegen Books, and the first of a trilogy. In a future Chicago, society is divided into five factions, each built around one virtue. At sixteen, Beatrice Prior must choose the faction she will live in for life. Her aptitude test shows she fits more than one, which makes her Divergent, a secret that could be dangerous. She leaves her selfless family faction for the brave Dauntless, renames herself Tris, and faces a violent initiation while a plot against her old faction takes shape. Underneath, the book is about identity, fear, courage and family. It won the Goodreads Choice Award for favorite book of 2011, spent 47 weeks on the New York Times young adult list, and was made into a 2014 film. It contains considerable violence.

97da9eff-3278-41ab-ab9b-abe9843b7ce9.title: Beloved
97da9eff-3278-41ab-ab9b-abe9843b7ce9.summary: Beloved is a 1987 novel by Toni Morrison that won the 1988 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction. It is set in 1873 outside Cincinnati, Ohio, where Sethe, who escaped slavery in Kentucky, lives with her daughter Denver in a house believed to be haunted by the baby daughter Sethe lost. When a young woman who calls herself Beloved appears, Sethe and Denver come to believe the dead child has come back. Moving between the present and Sethe's memories of Sweet Home, the novel slowly reveals what slavery took from her and what she did to keep her children from it. Underneath, it is about memory, mothers and children, and what a community owes the people it has shunned. Morrison was inspired by the true story of Margaret Garner, who fled slavery in 1856. The book deals with slavery, the death of a child, grief and violence, and is often taught in high school and college.

98f73fa5-3847-5e58-bc4b-6373a8f95503.title: Ivan: The Remarkable True Story of the Shopping Mall Gorilla
98f73fa5-3847-5e58-bc4b-6373a8f95503.summary: Ivan: The Remarkable True Story of the Shopping Mall Gorilla is a nonfiction picture book by Katherine Applegate, illustrated by G. Brian Karas and published by Clarion Books in 2014. It tells young children the real story of Ivan, an African gorilla stolen from the wild by poachers as a baby and kept for 27 years in a small enclosure at a shopping center in Washington State, until he was moved in 1994 to Zoo Atlanta, where he lived on grass among other gorillas. Applegate tells it in the third person, simplifying the story of her Newbery-winning novel and keeping the nonfiction focus. Karas's muted illustrations show Ivan's happy early life in Africa, his gloomy years in captivity and his new home. A detailed afterword gives more of the story and records his death in 2012. Publishers Weekly recommends it for ages 4-8.

9a12d28e-f93d-4def-bdd9-a7177ea25b19.title: The Little Mouse, the Red Ripe Strawberry, and the Big Hungry Bear
9a12d28e-f93d-4def-bdd9-a7177ea25b19.summary:
The little mouse discovers a juicy, red strawberry and becomes worried that the Big Hungry Bear will want to eat it. Throughout the story, the mouse comes up with various imaginative ways to hide and protect the strawberry. The mouse suggests using disguises, building fences, and even creating a tall tower to keep the strawberry safe.

Despite all the efforts, the mouse eventually realizes that there is no way to hide the strawberry from the Big Hungry Bear. In a surprising twist, the mouse decides to share the strawberry with the reader, and the book concludes with a lighthearted and delightful ending.

9b6da57c-ada7-4845-b61f-2c0227075617.title: Buddenbrooks
9b6da57c-ada7-4845-b61f-2c0227075617.summary:
This story traces the decline of a wealthy merchant family over several generations in the 19th century. Set in the northern German city of Lübeck, the story revolves around the Buddenbrook family, focusing primarily on three generations.

The novel begins with the patriarch, Johann Buddenbrook, who establishes the family's successful trading business and builds their fortune. His son, Consul Jean Buddenbrook, inherits the business and expands its prosperity, but struggles to maintain the family's prestige and social standing amidst changing times and values.

As the narrative progresses, the decline of the Buddenbrook family becomes apparent through a series of personal and professional setbacks. The family members grapple with financial troubles, marital discord, and the erosion of traditional values in the face of modernization and societal change.

9bce90a0-1dd7-4e3c-a2b5-dcd486d67fa8.title: Oblivion
9bce90a0-1dd7-4e3c-a2b5-dcd486d67fa8.summary: Set in the future, Oblivion tells the story of a drone repair man after and alien invasion has forced humans to abandon Earth. But not everything is as it seems and there are more questions than answers. Dreams (or memories) persuade this man to seek the truth about who he is and what really happened.

9c6a2e71-1c73-4f59-b2ce-1040240af6ed.title: Dune: Adventures in the Imperium
9c6a2e71-1c73-4f59-b2ce-1040240af6ed.summary: This Tabletop Role Playing Game is all about politics, subterfuge, and warfare taking place in the universe of the Imperium from the "DUNE" novels.

9c79fbd4-f55e-433b-b1e6-3d9f5c955e96.title: A House for Hermit Crab
9c79fbd4-f55e-433b-b1e6-3d9f5c955e96.summary: This story follows the journey of a hermit crab who embarks on a quest to find a new home. Along the way, the crab encounters various sea creatures who offer assistance, leading to delightful and unexpected adventures.

9ca7c728-0af4-43d4-ace7-107c9415ca8b.title: Happy in Our Skin
9ca7c728-0af4-43d4-ace7-107c9415ca8b.summary: The story follows a diverse group of children and families as they experience the joys of being together, playing, and exploring the world. Through playful and rhythmic text, the book highlights the beauty of various skin colors and the importance of loving oneself and others. The illustrations vividly depict families from different cultural backgrounds, emphasizing the commonalities and differences that make everyone special. Overall, the book promotes a message of self-acceptance, inclusivity, and the joy of embracing one's identity.

9cbb4153-1bd5-419f-9607-1ce4aac76773.title: Papers, Please
9cbb4153-1bd5-419f-9607-1ce4aac76773.summary: Papers, Please is a puzzle simulation video game created by indie game developer Lucas Pope, developed and published through his production company, 3909 LLC. The game was released on August 8, 2013, for Microsoft Windows and OS X, for Linux on February 12, 2014, and for iOS on December 12, 2014. A port for the PlayStation Vita was announced in August 2014 and was then released on December 12, 2017. A new port for iOS as well as for Android was released in August 2022.

9d9936b1-ed86-4441-87ce-5f2a6115a65e.title: K-19: The Widowmaker
9d9936b1-ed86-4441-87ce-5f2a6115a65e.summary: K-19: The Widowmaker is a 2002 historical submarine film directed and produced by Kathryn Bigelow, and produced by Edward S. Feldman, Sigurjon Sighvatsson, Christine Whitaker and Matthias Deyle with screenplay by Christopher Kyle. An international co-production of the United States, United Kingdom, Germany and Canada, the film takes place in 1961 and focuses its story on the Soviet Hotel-class submarine K-19.

9e4e91c6-4c0b-4e42-ab9a-d6d6f7cab1ea.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
9e4e91c6-4c0b-4e42-ab9a-d6d6f7cab1ea.summary:
This story is set in a totalitarian society ruled by the Party, led by the enigmatic figure known as Big Brother. We follow Winston Smith, a low-ranking member of the Party who works in the Ministry of Truth, where he alters historical records to align with the Party's propaganda.

As Winston navigates the oppressive and surveilled world of Oceania, he becomes disillusioned with the Party's control and begins to rebel against its totalitarian regime. He starts a forbidden love affair with Julia, a fellow Party member, and seeks to uncover the truth about the Party's manipulation of information and suppression of dissent.

As Winston delves deeper into his rebellion, he encounters O'Brien, a high-ranking Party member who claims to be a member of the Brotherhood, a secret resistance movement. However, Winston's trust in O'Brien is shattered when he is captured by the Thought Police and subjected to torture and brainwashing in the infamous Ministry of Love.

In the end, Winston's spirit is broken, and he comes to accept the Party's absolute power and authority. He learns to love Big Brother, embracing the Party's ideology and relinquishing his individuality and freedom.

9ec68e6f-cf78-4cde-8c1b-5ab2d793c12a.title: Knuffle Bunny Free: An Unexpected Diversion
9ec68e6f-cf78-4cde-8c1b-5ab2d793c12a.summary: Knuffle Bunny Free: An Unexpected Diversion is a children's picture book written and illustrated by Mo Willems. It is the third and final book in Willems' Knuffle Bunny series, which also includes Knuffle Bunny: A Cautionary Tale and Knuffle Bunny Too: A Case of Mistaken Identity. The book was released on September 28, 2010, by Balzer + Bray, an imprint of HarperCollins.

9ee26b02-840e-4ce8-85d9-e04a52519af9.title: The Rosenberg File
9ee26b02-840e-4ce8-85d9-e04a52519af9.summary:
A comprehensive account of the Julius and Ethel Rosenberg espionage case, a highly charged Cold War event. Initially believing the Rosenbergs were innocent, the authors, through extensive research, concluded Julius Rosenberg was indeed guilty of espionage, while Ethel's involvement remained less clear, though subsequent research suggests she was also implicated.
The book delves into the Rosenbergs' involvement with Communism and their spy activities, the legal proceedings surrounding their arrest and trial, and the political storm that ensued. Radosh and Milton explore the context of the Cold War, the American Communist Party, and the climate of fear that fueled the case. The authors also examine the motivations of key figures like David Greenglass, Ethel's brother, and the role of figures like J. Edgar Hoover and the media.

9f833429-2ff1-40d1-88c2-6e1de476b9f6.title: Starships
9f833429-2ff1-40d1-88c2-6e1de476b9f6.summary: Nicki Minaj's "Starships" is mainly about having the freedom to reach one's full potential while disregarding other people's expectations. The lyric "starships are meant to fly" is a line about reaching one's full potential in life. Minaj explained that the song is about "just go for it! Stop limiting yourself! And that's a great feeling. It's a great feeling to not box yourself into anyone's limitations or ideas or judgments.

9f93d7af-07e0-426f-9ef3-c26d175368c8.title: When Doves Cry
9f93d7af-07e0-426f-9ef3-c26d175368c8.summary: When Doves Cry” is just a metaphor of what happens when a beautiful relationship goes sour and the changes that have to happen. Doves are a universal symbol of peace so it seems he is actually taking an optimist’s view, hoping the two can work out their differences.

a0e00dc0-3e41-4c27-826f-976e0fa7640d.title: Shape of You
a0e00dc0-3e41-4c27-826f-976e0fa7640d.summary: "Shape of You" by Ed Sheeran revolves around the theme of attraction and romance. The song's lyrics depict a narrative where Sheeran meets someone at a bar, and despite not being interested in the typical bar scene, he is captivated by the physical and emotional connection he feels with the person. The song explores the excitement and energy of a new and passionate relationship, while highlighting the singer's fascination with the person's body and the overall chemistry between them.

a19689c6-98cf-5a5b-bafe-738c60c1e099.title: Animal Farm
a19689c6-98cf-5a5b-bafe-738c60c1e099.summary: Animal Farm is a short satirical novel by George Orwell, first published in London by Secker & Warburg on 17 August 1945, with a first American edition from Harcourt, Brace in 1946; its original subtitle was A Fairy Story. The animals of Manor Farm, led by the pigs, drive out their careless, drunken owner, rename the place Animal Farm and vow that all animals are equal. Slowly the pig Napoleon takes control, with guard dogs and the smooth-talking Squealer on his side, and the animals' rules are rewritten until the pigs live just like the humans they replaced. Underneath, it is a warning about how a revolution can turn into tyranny, and how propaganda and fear keep people quiet. Orwell meant it as a satire of Stalin's Soviet Union. Kirkus called it a clear fable about dictatorship in 1946.

a1cd2d32-e1af-4e77-9645-1ee7e9eed614.title: The Count of Monte Cristo
a1cd2d32-e1af-4e77-9645-1ee7e9eed614.summary: The Count of Monte Cristo is an adventure novel written by French author Alexandre Dumas (père) completed in 1844. It is one of the author's most popular works, along with The Three Musketeers. Like many of his novels, it was expanded from plot outlines suggested by his collaborating ghostwriter Auguste Maquet.

a2904c07-78f5-4fd9-a698-bdd6f2e7651e.title: You're No Good
a2904c07-78f5-4fd9-a698-bdd6f2e7651e.summary: "You're No Good" is a song written by Clint Ballard Jr., first performed by Dee Dee Warwick for Jubilee Records in 1963 with production by Jerry Leiber and Mike Stoller. It has since been covered by many artists, including charting versions by Betty Everett in 1963, The Swinging Blue Jeans in 1964, and Linda Ronstadt in 1974, whose version was a number 1 hit in the United States.

a2e96bd3-639b-5cad-953c-28cb0a6e5fc3.title: The Maze Runner
a2e96bd3-639b-5cad-953c-28cb0a6e5fc3.summary: The Maze Runner is a young adult science-fiction novel by James Dashner, published in 2009 by Delacorte Press. Sixteen-year-old Thomas wakes in a rising metal box remembering only his name and arrives in the Glade, a walled clearing where a community of boys has built a life, with a new boy arriving every month. Beyond the walls lies a huge Maze whose walls shift at night and whose machine-and-animal creatures, the Grievers, hunt there. Runners map it each day, looking for a way out. When Teresa, the first girl, arrives, Thomas pushes the group to act. Underneath, the book is about identity and memory, order against change, and what friends do for each other when hope runs thin. It spent 148 weeks on the New York Times best-seller list, earned a 2011 YALSA Best Fiction for Young Adults honor, and began a series; a film followed in 2014.

a32a6d01-bf3e-55a0-8d2f-46cadb5e9c14.title: Life of the Party: The Remarkable Story of How Brownie Wise Built, and Lost, a Tupperware Party Empire
a32a6d01-bf3e-55a0-8d2f-46cadb5e9c14.summary: Life of the Party is a biography of Brownie Wise by Orlando journalist Bob Kealing, published by Crown Archetype in 2016 as a revised edition of his 2008 book Tupperware, Unsealed. Wise was a divorced single mother in postwar America who built a business of her own and then caught the eye of Earl Tupper, whose plastic containers were selling poorly in stores. The home party she popularized, a gentle kind of demonstration selling, turned them into a runaway success and gave many housewives, including some African American women, a respectable way to earn their own money. In 1954 she became the first woman on the cover of Business Week. Then Tupper fired her under mysterious circumstances and wrote her out of the company's story. Kealing sets out to put her back into it, and asks who really made Tupperware: the inventor or the saleswoman.

a3aab8a2-5531-4f80-8b58-6ea4158d9067.title: We Belong Together
a3aab8a2-5531-4f80-8b58-6ea4158d9067.summary: "We Belong Together" is a song that revolves around the theme of heartbreak, longing, and the desire to reunite with a lost love. The lyrics tell the story of someone who is reflecting on a past relationship, expressing deep regret and sadness for letting their partner go.

a47628ee-f2db-5919-b09f-5b2fa5fc430e.title: The Icebound Land
a47628ee-f2db-5919-b09f-5b2fa5fc430e.summary: The Icebound Land is the third novel in John Flanagan's Ranger's Apprentice fantasy series, first published in Australia in 2005 and in the United States by Philomel in 2007. After a battle at the end of the previous book, apprentice Ranger Will and the disguised Princess Evanlyn are taken to Skandia as slaves. There Will is tricked into taking warmweed, a drug that dulls his mind and makes him obedient, and Evanlyn has to help him find his way back to himself. Meanwhile Will's mentor Halt, banished from the kingdom for a year after insulting the king, sets out to find him with the young warrior Horace and crosses a lawless Gallica. Underneath, it is a story about loyalty to friends and the work of recovering a self that was almost lost. Kirkus found it a middle volume that moves the main plot only slightly, but praised its clear prose and likable heroes.

a4ab8da9-e766-5976-8ab0-f485058e910e.title: Pride and Prejudice (TV series)
a4ab8da9-e766-5976-8ab0-f485058e910e.summary: Pride and Prejudice is a six-episode BBC drama first shown in 1995, adapted by Andrew Davies from Jane Austen's novel and directed by Simon Langton, with Jennifer Ehle as Elizabeth Bennet and Colin Firth as Mr. Darcy. Bingley rents Netherfield and admires Jane, Darcy snubs Elizabeth at a dance, and her dislike hardens when Wickham tells her a story against him. After Mr. Collins's proposal is refused and her friend Charlotte marries him, Darcy proposes in Kent and is turned down for his pride and for parting Bingley and Jane. His letter and a visit to Pemberley change her mind; Lydia's elopement with Wickham tests everyone, and Darcy secretly pays to set it right. Davies stayed close to the book, stressed money and marriage, and gave Darcy a famous lake scene of his own invention. About ten million British viewers watched, and Ehle won a BAFTA.

a57c4144-6f7f-4b6a-a4f4-9778cd0017e7.title: The Sound of Music
a57c4144-6f7f-4b6a-a4f4-9778cd0017e7.summary: A 1965 musical drama directed by Robert Wise from Ernest Lehman's screenplay, adapted from the 1959 Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical. In 1938 Salzburg, Maria, a high-spirited novice at Nonnberg Abbey, is sent to be governess to the seven children of a widowed naval officer, Captain Georg von Trapp, who runs his household with military discipline. She wins the children over with kindness and teaches them to sing, and the Captain changes too. Then Nazi Germany annexes Austria, and a man who opposes the regime must choose what he will not give up. The story is a fictionalized version of the real von Trapp family: in life Maria and Georg married in 1927, and the family left Austria by train, not on foot over the mountains. The film won five Academy Awards including Best Picture, became the highest-grossing film of its time, and entered the National Film Registry in 2001.

a5b4cbab-71ba-4cc1-ad03-1609b22c4e93.title: The Shawshank Redemption
a5b4cbab-71ba-4cc1-ad03-1609b22c4e93.summary:
In "The Shawshank Redemption", Andy Dufresne (played byTim Robbins) is convicted of murdering his wife and her lover.  He arrives at Shawshank State Prison to serve two consecutive life sentences. He spends the next 28 years in prison making lifelong friends all while planning his escape. 
Nominated in 1995 for seven Academy Awards including Best Picture.

a5d2374d-6acf-5047-a546-8e43a812aaf4.title: Walking Shadows
a5d2374d-6acf-5047-a546-8e43a812aaf4.summary: Walking Shadows is a Second World War spy novel by Fred Taylor, first published in 1984 by St. Martin's Press in New York. In 1942-43 an Abwehr agent, Otto von Bredow, approaches a veteran British spy, Jackie Bellingham, in Portugal. He offers to help British intelligence expose a rival German agent inside its own service, if Britain helps kill Hitler at a planned meeting on Rhodes. The head of the British service approves, and Bellingham gathers a commando team in Cairo, but the mission is compromised from the start by a double agent that London wants to keep in place at any cost. Underneath, it is a story about spies and the people they sacrifice. Kirkus found it a familiar tale, slow but serviceable; it was also reviewed in Publishers Weekly and The New York Times.

a895386e-fafd-4398-be27-c2d7a53c8989.title: The Little House
a895386e-fafd-4398-be27-c2d7a53c8989.summary: The journey of a little house as it experiences the changing world around it.

a8bca372-d004-4416-9d2d-e1510fedb521.title: I Really Like Slop!
a8bca372-d004-4416-9d2d-e1510fedb521.summary: Piggie really likes slop. She likes it so much, she wants Gerald to try some! But can Gerald find the courage to do it? Or will the smell alone be too much to handle?

ab21a9be-dd04-5a35-88f3-da7ea36c45bd.title: Tigers
ab21a9be-dd04-5a35-88f3-da7ea36c45bd.summary: Tigers is a 32-page nonfiction picture book by Laura Marsh, published in 2012 as a Level 2 title in National Geographic Kids Readers, a series for children reading on their own. Photographs and short chapters introduce one animal: where tigers live, from the warm forests of Southeast Asia to the frozen north of western Russia, how their bodies are built for hunting, what they eat, how they mark out their territory, and how cubs grow up. Later chapters look at the rare white tiger, at why tigers are in trouble, and at ways of helping them, and a last page of questions invites readers to stump their parents. Underneath, it is a first lesson in how a wild animal lives and why it needs protecting.

ab3a71b3-9496-4052-bcc4-9f36c114dfdb.title: Little Red Riding Hood
ab3a71b3-9496-4052-bcc4-9f36c114dfdb.summary: Little Red Riding Hood is a European fairy tale about a young girl and a sly wolf. Its origins can be traced back to several pre-17th-century European folk tales. The two best known versions were written by Charles Perrault and the Brothers Grimm.

ab574128-461d-57ea-b708-65b319f59fbe.title: Kozier & Erb's Techniques in Clinical Nursing: Basic to Intermediate Skills
ab574128-461d-57ea-b708-65b319f59fbe.year: 2002 (fifth edition; Tri-County and a Nevada State College announcement say 2002, Open Library says Sept 10, 2001; the earliest edition Library of Congress shows is 1982)
ab574128-461d-57ea-b708-65b319f59fbe.summary: A nursing skills textbook, the fifth edition of a reference that Kozier and Erb were already publishing as Techniques in Clinical Nursing in 1982, here carrying their names in the title. It walks a student through nearly 200 hands-on techniques step by step, giving the reason behind each key step and linking every technique to the body science it rests on. Infection-control precautions are built into each technique, and the book adds questions that ask the reader to weigh a clinical judgment, notes on how care changes with a patient's age, and guidance for care outside the hospital, including at home. It is written for nursing skills courses, fundamentals and medical-surgical courses, new graduates and working nurses. It runs to roughly 700 pages. No review of this edition was found.

ac64ecd2-afc4-5f8c-bc0d-5e44f7586159.title: Give Up the Ghost
ac64ecd2-afc4-5f8c-bc0d-5e44f7586159.summary: The third studio album by the American singer-songwriter Brandi Carlile, released October 6, 2009 by Columbia Records. Rick Rubin produced it at Sunset Sound in Los Angeles, and Paul Buckmaster arranged strings. It is a bigger, harder-rocking record than her last, with Elton John on piano and vocals for 'Caroline,' Amy Ray singing backup, and her bandmates Phil and Tim Hanseroth writing or co-writing seven of its eleven songs. Reviewers heard love at its center and hardship met with grace. Carlile has said the title is not about death: she meant it as a figure of speech for a big transition from one life to the next, growing by moving past who she had been. It holds 'Pride and Joy,' the breakup song 'I Will,' and 'That Year,' which Carlile wrote about a high school friend who died by suicide and which she describes as being about reconciliation and forgiveness. It reached number 26 on the Billboard 200 and brought Carlile a GLAAD Media Award nomination.

acc67354-e624-49fd-87cd-08ea2c1d2280.title: The Catcher in the Rye
acc67354-e624-49fd-87cd-08ea2c1d2280.summary:
This story is narrated by Holden Caulfield, a disenchanted and disillusioned teenager who has been expelled from his prep school in Pennsylvania. The story follows Holden over a few days as he wanders around New York City, grappling with feelings of alienation, confusion, and disillusionment with the adult world.

Holden shares his thoughts, observations, and encounters with various people he meets during his journey, offering insight into his troubled mind and his struggle to find authenticity and meaning in a world he perceives as superficial and phony.

Throughout the novel, Holden struggles with issues of identity, authenticity, and the loss of innocence. He is haunted by the death of his younger brother, Allie, and feels disconnected from his parents and peers. As he navigates the streets of New York, Holden searches for connection and authenticity but encounters disappointment and disillusionment at every turn.

adb45849-86fc-47db-bb57-c0d8bc5d56ab.title: The Great Gatsby
adb45849-86fc-47db-bb57-c0d8bc5d56ab.summary:
The novel is narrated by Nick Carraway, who moves to Long Island's North Shore and becomes neighbors with the mysterious and wealthy Jay Gatsby. Gatsby is known for hosting extravagant parties in the hopes of reuniting with his former lover, Daisy Buchanan. Daisy is married to Tom Buchanan, a wealthy and arrogant man.

As the narrative unfolds, it becomes clear that Gatsby is infatuated with Daisy and is determined to win her back. Nick becomes a confidant and intermediary between Gatsby and Daisy. The novel delves into the complexities of love, social class, and the pursuit of the American Dream.

Gatsby's wealth is built on illusions, and his desire for Daisy is intertwined with the idea of achieving success and social status. The story climaxes with a tragic event that exposes the superficiality and moral decay of the characters in the Jazz Age. Tom Buchanan's racist talk belongs to a character the novel shows as careless and cruel; it is not the book's own view.

adc59865-afaf-45f1-98f1-04711cf82e86.title: Polar Babies
adc59865-afaf-45f1-98f1-04711cf82e86.summary: Explore the lives of various baby animals living in the polar regions. Young readers are introduced to creatures such as polar bear cubs, seal pups, penguin chicks, and more. The book follows these baby animals as they navigate their icy environments, learning to survive and thrive alongside their families.

ae2fa85e-b9f2-4841-8016-1c50d59d3cb2.title: The Color Purple
ae2fa85e-b9f2-4841-8016-1c50d59d3cb2.summary: The Color Purple is a 1982 epistolary novel by American author Alice Walker that won the 1983 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction and the National Book Award for Fiction.

ae903de4-9ef8-5e63-9e3e-aab991abf8b4.title: Laughing
ae903de4-9ef8-5e63-9e3e-aab991abf8b4.summary: Laughing: A Historical Selection of American Humor is an anthology compiled by Charles Keller and published by Prentice-Hall in 1977 (299 pages). It gathers American humor from colonial times to 1969 and opens each selection with an introduction by Keller that traces how humor developed in the United States. It includes a bibliography and an index. Library catalogers filed it under American wit and humor and under wit and humor for young readers. Underneath, it is a short history of what Americans have found funny, told through the writing itself. No fetched page lists the individual selections or gives a review, so none are described here.

afc26f84-df62-5fa4-9a7a-e2cb75af5bd2.title: Beloved
afc26f84-df62-5fa4-9a7a-e2cb75af5bd2.summary: Beloved is a 1998 American drama directed by Jonathan Demme, adapted from Toni Morrison's 1987 novel, with Oprah Winfrey as Sethe, Danny Glover as Paul D, Kimberly Elise as Denver and Thandiwe Newton as Beloved. Shortly after the Civil War, Sethe, who escaped slavery, lives outside Cincinnati with her daughter Denver in a house haunted by an angry spirit. Paul D, a man she knew at the plantation called Sweet Home, drives the spirit out, and then a young woman named Beloved arrives and is taken in. The film moves back and forth in time, showing what slavery did to Sethe and what she did to keep her children from it, and why the house is haunted. Underneath, it is about memory, guilt, a mother's love and how far a community will go to pull someone back. It was nominated for an Oscar for costume design, though it did poorly at the box office. It is rated R and deals with slavery, sexual assault and the death of a child.

afcbbf6b-6df7-4050-924d-45b7195eefdc.title: The Old Man and the sea
afcbbf6b-6df7-4050-924d-45b7195eefdc.summary: The Old Man and the Sea is a 1952 novella written by the American author Ernest Hemingway. Written between December 1950 and February 1951, it was the last major fictional work Hemingway published during his lifetime. It tells the story of Santiago, an aging fisherman, and his long struggle to catch a giant marlin. The novella was highly anticipated and was released to record sales; the initial critical reception was equally positive, but attitudes have varied significantly since then.

afcc0b37-1791-4c1b-8484-96e305d845b5.title: All Along the Watchtower
afcc0b37-1791-4c1b-8484-96e305d845b5.summary: "All Along the Watchtower" is a song originally written by Bob Dylan and later famously covered by Jimi Hendrix. Hendrix's rendition of the song, released in 1968, is particularly notable for its unique interpretation and guitar work. The song has a mysterious and apocalyptic atmosphere, with cryptic lyrics that evoke a sense of foreboding and uncertainty. The lyrics of "All Along the Watchtower" depict a conversation between two characters, often interpreted as a jester and a thief, discussing the challenges and changes happening around them. The watchtower becomes a symbolic setting for observing the world's turmoil and impending doom.

affdd5b2-71aa-4641-be99-e5290b8ba0b1.title: Klaus Fuchs FBI Files
affdd5b2-71aa-4641-be99-e5290b8ba0b1.summary: Klaus Emil Julius Fuchs (1911-1988) was a German-born atomic scientist who emigrated to Great Britain in the late 1930s. He worked on the joint U.S./British effort to build the atomic bomb. Following an FBI and British investigation, Fuchs was convicted of espionage in Great Britain for supplying atomic secrets to the Soviet Union. The Fuchs file is tied closely to that of Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, two U.S. citizens who were convicted in 1950 of passing atomic secrets to the USSR. The file ranges from 1949 to 1976.

b1794720-a43f-49b9-a8b6-9db8a01e151d.title: Uncharted: Drake's Fortune
b1794720-a43f-49b9-a8b6-9db8a01e151d.summary: Treasure hunter Nathan Drake uncovers a centuries old mystery, while contending with adversarial fortune hunters all the while.

b1797a01-35d0-449c-a6e6-43f147b6a367.title: Breaking Bad
b1797a01-35d0-449c-a6e6-43f147b6a367.summary: Breaking Bad is an American crime drama television series created and produced by Vince Gilligan for AMC. Set and filmed in Albuquerque, New Mexico, the series follows Walter White, an underpaid, dispirited high-school chemistry teacher struggling with a recent diagnosis of stage-three lung cancer. White turns to a life of crime and partners with a former student, Jesse Pinkman, to produce and distribute methamphetamine to secure his family's financial future before he dies, while navigating the dangers of the criminal underworld. Breaking Bad premiered on AMC on January 20, 2008, and concluded on September 29, 2013, after five seasons consisting of 62 episodes.

b20e9072-b90b-4230-bd42-cbfe0649cacf.title: I Want to Hold Your Hand
b20e9072-b90b-4230-bd42-cbfe0649cacf.summary: "I Want to Hold Your Hand" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles, written by John Lennon and Paul McCartney. Recorded on 17 October 1963 and released on 29 November 1963 in the United Kingdom, it was the first Beatles record to be made using four-track recording equipment.

b22bbe2d-9871-4c6e-9957-50f2e0e0095c.title: Olivia's Opposites
b22bbe2d-9871-4c6e-9957-50f2e0e0095c.summary: Olivia explores the concept of opposites through engaging illustrations and simple text. From big and small to quiet and loud, Olivia encounters various opposites in her playful and imaginative world.

b35d72b9-78ac-4628-852b-7a9382f32437.title: A Hat in Time
b35d72b9-78ac-4628-852b-7a9382f32437.summary: After her hat-themed spaceship is damaged, Hat Kid goes on a series of adventures to find magical hourglasses needed to refuel and repair her ship.

b36507f9-9d03-4e18-944c-92dcd38f0c00.title: John Denver's Take Me Home, Country Roads
b36507f9-9d03-4e18-944c-92dcd38f0c00.summary:
Take Me Home, Country Roads, a book following the lyrics of John Denver's first hit song, is a great teaching tool for young readers about family and appreciation for the natural world around us.

This brilliant picture book adaptation of John Denver's first hit song is all about roots, family, and country. Set in Appalachia, a humorously diverse bunch of relatives and their in-laws go up, down and around the hills of West Virginia to converge by car, pickup, and motorcycle to a family reunion at Grandma and Grandpa's country home. True to Appalachian style, Canyon portrays it all as if on a quilt, complete with little stitches between the "fabric." The lyrics demand to be sung!

b3891728-906b-4d3c-9878-098ecfb44883.title: The Kissing Hand
b3891728-906b-4d3c-9878-098ecfb44883.summary: The Kissing Hand is an American children's picture book written by Audrey Penn and illustrated by Ruth E. Harper and Nancy M. Leak. It features a mother raccoon comforting a child raccoon by kissing its paw. First published by the Child Welfare League of America in 1993, it has been used "to reassure children upset by separation anxiety."

b416d31d-d8f6-5496-af85-73a8148bb01b.title: My Favorite Murder with Karen Kilgariff and Georgia Hardstark
b416d31d-d8f6-5496-af85-73a8148bb01b.summary: My Favorite Murder is a true crime comedy podcast hosted by comedians Karen Kilgariff and Georgia Hardstark, who met at a Halloween party in 2014 and found they shared an interest in true crime. In each episode one host tells a murder, a survivor's story or a historical event she has researched while the other reacts, jokes and asks questions. The first episode came out in January 2016, and the show grew into live tours, a 2019 bestselling memoir, and Exactly Right, a podcast network the hosts founded in 2018. Fans call themselves Murderinos and gather online and at meet-ups. The hosts describe the show as a way to ease their own anxiety about crime, and they talk openly about therapy and mental health between stories. The tone is chatty and profane. Critics have questioned whose stories the show chooses to tell, and the hosts address mistakes in a segment called Corrections Corner. The episodes deal with real killings and are rated Explicit, so it is meant for adults.

b4a54247-1e0c-4768-a777-3122143a7d25.title: Arthur's Thanksgiving
b4a54247-1e0c-4768-a777-3122143a7d25.summary: When Arthur is picked to direct his school's Thanksgiving play, all his friends beg him for the lead role. But not everyone can be the star, and someone has to be the turkey! Can Arthur find the perfect lead, the perfect turkey, and save the day?

b4b05545-fb37-5cf0-9c5b-166331e70de7.title: The Sound of Music
b4b05545-fb37-5cf0-9c5b-166331e70de7.summary: The Sound of Music is a 1959 Broadway musical with music by Richard Rodgers, lyrics by Oscar Hammerstein II and a book by Howard Lindsay and Russel Crouse, based on Maria von Trapp's 1949 memoir; it was the last show Rodgers and Hammerstein wrote together. Set in Salzburg in 1938, it follows Maria, a free-spirited postulant at Nonnberg Abbey who is sent to be governess to the seven children of a widowed naval captain, Georg von Trapp. She teaches the children to sing and brings warmth into a strict household, and she and the Captain fall in love and marry. When Nazi Germany annexes Austria and he is ordered to serve in its navy, he refuses and the family escapes. Songs such as Do-Re-Mi, My Favorite Things and Edelweiss became standards. The original production, starring Mary Martin and Theodore Bikel, ran 1,443 performances and won five Tony Awards, including Best Musical. The authors changed many details of the real family's story.

b5de6765-3fcf-49b3-b392-b0d659c9886d.title: This Is Us
b5de6765-3fcf-49b3-b392-b0d659c9886d.summary: This Is Us is an American drama television series created by Dan Fogelman that aired on NBC from September 20, 2016, to May 24, 2022. The series follows the lives and families of two parents and their three children in several different time frames. It stars an ensemble cast featuring Milo Ventimiglia, Mandy Moore, Sterling K. Brown, Chrissy Metz, Justin Hartley, Susan Kelechi Watson, Chris Sullivan, Ron Cephas Jones, Jon Huertas, Alexandra Breckenridge, Niles Fitch, Logan Shroyer, Hannah Zeile, Mackenzie Hancsicsak, Parker Bates, Eris Baker, Faithe Herman, Lonnie Chavis, Melanie Liburd, Lyric Ross, Asante Blackk, Griffin Dunne, Caitlin Thompson and Chris Geere. This Is Us was filmed in Los Angeles.

b60700df-5ec7-4f7b-9a11-07af1e0321a3.title: Yellow
b60700df-5ec7-4f7b-9a11-07af1e0321a3.summary:
"Yellow" by Coldplay is a song that primarily explores the theme of intense and unconditional love. The lyrics use the color yellow as a metaphor to describe the brightness and positivity associated with the emotion of love. The song suggests a sense of admiration and awe for someone special. The color yellow symbolizes warmth, joy, and happiness, reflecting the emotional depth of the singer's feelings.

Overall, "Yellow" is a love song that conveys a sense of devotion and appreciation, capturing the beauty and intensity of a romantic connection. It has become one of Coldplay's most iconic and beloved songs

b690e104-c6d3-545a-9b79-ed2f507e95ee.title: Everything Is Tuberculosis (99% Invisible episode)
b690e104-c6d3-545a-9b79-ed2f507e95ee.summary: Everything Is Tuberculosis is episode 623 of the design podcast 99% Invisible, released April 8, 2025. Host Roman Mars interviews author John Green about his book of the same name on the world's deadliest infectious disease. Green explains why tuberculosis, which has been curable since the middle of the twentieth century, still kills over a million people a year: treatment takes months of daily drugs that poor patients struggle to finish, and drug resistance follows when it is interrupted. He also traces the disease's odd effects on everyday life, from romantic ideas of 'consumption' to Adirondack chairs, sanatoriums, New Mexico's statehood and the cowboy hat. He describes meeting a teenage patient named Henry in Sierra Leone, the price of drugs and tests, and recent cuts to international health aid, and ends by refusing to feel hopeless. The episode discusses illness, death and malnutrition, including a child patient.

b69959a2-3de8-473b-9db4-e5de70196853.title: The Berenstain Bears Don’t Pollute (Anymore)
b69959a2-3de8-473b-9db4-e5de70196853.summary: When careless citizens pose a threat to Bear Country's environment, Brother and Sister Bear form the Earthsavers Club. Their spirited ecological efforts deliver a timely message about the urgent need to mend our polluting and wasteful ways.

b785ddf3-0f37-436b-8355-b59751191e04.title: Batman: Arkham City
b785ddf3-0f37-436b-8355-b59751191e04.summary: Batman infiltrates Arkham City, a megalithic prison facility in Gotham City, and needs to contend with supervillains and the prison's warden as he uncovers the conspiracies and dangerous power structures within.

b78d873b-12fa-5066-87f2-3d3ede70457c.title: Pride & Prejudice
b78d873b-12fa-5066-87f2-3d3ede70457c.summary: Pride & Prejudice is a 2005 British romantic drama directed by Joe Wright, in his first feature, from a screenplay by Deborah Moggach based on Jane Austen's novel. Keira Knightley plays Elizabeth Bennet, one of five sisters in a muddy, crowded country household in Hertfordshire, where her mother is set on marrying them well. Elizabeth takes an instant dislike to the proud, wealthy Mr. Darcy, played by Matthew Macfadyen, and believes a charming officer's story against him. Darcy's first proposal, in a rainstorm, is refused. His letter then shows her how wrong she was about both men, and a visit to his estate, Pemberley, changes her view again. When her youngest sister runs off with the officer, Darcy quietly steps in. The film moves the story to the late 1700s and makes the Bennets' money worries plain. It earned four Academy Award nominations and was rated PG.

b7abfe81-0792-4429-bb40-7338d2f5bffe.title: Bridge of Spies
b7abfe81-0792-4429-bb40-7338d2f5bffe.summary: Bridge of Spies is a 2015 historical drama film directed and co-produced by Steven Spielberg, written by Matt Charman and the Coen brothers, and starring Tom Hanks in the lead role, Mark Rylance, Amy Ryan, and Alan Alda. Set during the Cold War, the film tells the story of lawyer James B. Donovan, who is entrusted with negotiating the release of Francis Gary Powers—a convicted Central Intelligence Agency pilot whose U-2 spy plane was shot down over the Soviet Union in 1960—in exchange for Rudolf Abel, a convicted Soviet KGB spy held by the United States, whom Donovan represented at trial. The name of the film refers to the Glienicke Bridge, which connects Potsdam with Berlin, where the prisoner exchange took place. The film was an international co-production of the United States, India, Germany and the United Kingdom.

b7ba40e9-95ef-5973-9618-d7052931fea4.title: Everything Is Tuberculosis
b7ba40e9-95ef-5973-9618-d7052931fea4.summary: Everything Is Tuberculosis is a 2025 nonfiction book by John Green about the world's deadliest infectious disease. In 2019 Green visited Lakka Government Hospital in Sierra Leone with Partners In Health and met Henry, a teenage patient whose tuberculosis had stopped responding to the usual drugs. Henry's story runs through the book, alternating with chapters on how the disease was once romanticized as consumption, how it pushed people to move and build, and how it became curable in the twentieth century. Green argues that tuberculosis still kills well over a million people a year because of human choices about money, race, colonial history and who receives medicine, not because of the germ alone. Underneath, the book is about injustice and attention: we tend to solve the problems we pay attention to. It deals with illness, hunger, poverty and death. It reached number one on the New York Times nonfiction list and drew starred reviews from Booklist and School Library Journal.

b7f22f28-dbe6-4095-b02c-1bedf3353584.title: The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
b7f22f28-dbe6-4095-b02c-1bedf3353584.summary: The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde is an 1886 novella by Robert Louis Stevenson. In London, the lawyer Gabriel Utterson grows uneasy about his friend Dr. Henry Jekyll's connection to Edward Hyde, a violent man who seems to have some hold over him. The truth, revealed at the end, is that Jekyll has made a drug that turns him into Hyde, releasing everything he keeps hidden. Underneath, it is about the divided self - the respectable face and what it conceals - and the danger of a scientist experimenting on human nature. The names Jekyll and Hyde have become shorthand for a split personality.

b824fbd8-0fe9-4af2-8235-a4ff6d3bd533.title: Scoop
b824fbd8-0fe9-4af2-8235-a4ff6d3bd533.summary: Scoop is a 1938 novel by the English writer Evelyn Waugh. It is a satire of sensationalist journalism and foreign correspondents.

b8b25a3e-0e42-4184-97d4-301ac5464221.title: Matthew's Dream
b8b25a3e-0e42-4184-97d4-301ac5464221.summary: Matthew the mouse lives in a dreary corner of a dusty attic. But a trip to the museum helps him to see his surroundings in a new way. With brush in paw, Matthew sets out to paint “the shapes and colors of joy.”

b9c05ca4-b79a-4fe7-9de6-dea6135c1dcf.title: Crazy
b9c05ca4-b79a-4fe7-9de6-dea6135c1dcf.summary: This song is about insisting upon doing things a certain way, and the thin line between being crazy and being convinced that you’re right. The song has a literal meaning, which is that anyone who thinks they are in control of their lives is a fool when so many unconscious influences govern our actions.

b9cfe4b4-79c2-500f-ac15-63a39319dbb1.title: Pivot
b9cfe4b4-79c2-500f-ac15-63a39319dbb1.summary: Pivot is a news commentary podcast in which technology journalist Kara Swisher and NYU marketing professor Scott Galloway talk through the biggest stories in tech, business and politics every Tuesday and Friday. They make bold predictions, name winners and losers and argue with each other, in a lively, unfiltered way. It was created in 2018 by New York magazine and Vox, and it now belongs to the Vox Media Podcast Network. Between regular shows there are extra episodes called Pivot Extra, and the hosts tour live; a stop in Minneapolis is set for November 4, 2026. By October 2026 Apple Podcasts lists 819 episodes. It is opinionated commentary rather than straight reporting, the hosts often disagree with each other, and Apple Podcasts marks the show Explicit, so it is meant for older listeners.

b9f45071-14bc-4dcf-871b-d0fe476593c3.title: Glad Monster, sad monster: a book about feelings
b9f45071-14bc-4dcf-871b-d0fe476593c3.summary: Monsters of different colors explain what makes them feel glad, sad, loving, worried, silly, and angry. Fold-out masks encourage readers to talk about their feelings

ba062b5e-b78e-5e07-b495-eb5539cf0068.title: Rebound
ba062b5e-b78e-5e07-b495-eb5539cf0068.summary: Rebound is a prequel to Kwame Alexander's Newbery Medal-winning The Crossover, written in verse and illustrated with comic-style panels by Dawud Anyabwile, published by Houghton Mifflin Harcourt in 2018. In the summer of 1988, twelve-year-old Chuck Bell is angry, sad and lost after the sudden death of his father. After he steals from a neighbor, his mother sends him to his grandparents near Washington, D.C., where his cousin Roxie pulls him into basketball despite his protests, he discovers jazz, and he learns more about his family's past. His friend CJ helps him put his feelings in a journal. By the end he understands his father better and has begun to heal. Chuck grows up to be the father and coach of the twins in The Crossover, so the book is also the story of how that man became who he is. It was shortlisted for the 2019 Carnegie Medal.

bc56db23-f249-52c9-b96b-ff9b484b65cd.title: A Series of Unfortunate Events (TV series)
bc56db23-f249-52c9-b96b-ff9b484b65cd.summary: A Series of Unfortunate Events is a dark comedy drama that Netflix released in three seasons and 25 episodes, from January 13, 2017 to January 1, 2019. It adapts all thirteen books by Lemony Snicket, the pen name of Daniel Handler, who wrote scripts and served as an executive producer with director Barry Sonnenfeld. Neil Patrick Harris plays Count Olaf, Patrick Warburton the narrator Lemony Snicket, and Malina Weissman, Louis Hynes and Presley Smith the Baudelaire orphans. After a fire kills their parents, Violet, Klaus and baby Sunny are placed with Olaf, who wants their fortune, and they keep escaping one guardian after another as he follows them in disguise. Along the way they learn that their parents belonged to a secret society. Time and place are deliberately left vague. Underneath, it is about loss, adults who do not listen, and how good people choose what is right. It won a Peabody Award.

bc9ed07b-f126-409f-85bb-33bc1a5a3186.title: Rocky
bc9ed07b-f126-409f-85bb-33bc1a5a3186.summary: A small-time Philadelphia boxer gets a supremely rare chance to fight the world heavyweight champion in a bout in which he strives to go the distance for his self-respect.

bca46341-87d1-4271-b73c-3d108949d751.title: Persuasion
bca46341-87d1-4271-b73c-3d108949d751.summary:
This story follows Anne Elliot, a 27-year-old woman who lives with her vain and frivolous father, Sir Walter Elliot, and her older sister, Elizabeth, in the English countryside.

Eight years prior to the events of the novel, Anne had been engaged to Frederick Wentworth, a naval officer with no fortune or connections. However, Anne broke off the engagement upon the persuasion of her family and Lady Russell, a trusted family friend, who believed Wentworth was not suitable.

The novel begins when Captain Wentworth returns to the neighborhood as a wealthy and successful man, having made his fortune in the Napoleonic Wars. Anne and Captain Wentworth find themselves thrown into each other's company once more, but both are reluctant to acknowledge their lingering feelings.

As the story unfolds, Anne navigates the complexities of her family's relationships and social circles, including encounters with various suitors who vie for her attention. Meanwhile, Captain Wentworth's presence stirs up old emotions and rekindles the possibility of a renewed relationship. The limits placed on women in its time - in marriage, money and work - are part of the novel's subject, shown so the reader feels them.

bcc8e415-041c-4179-bd70-b2bb9ef857d8.title: When the Wind Blows
bcc8e415-041c-4179-bd70-b2bb9ef857d8.summary: "When the Wind Blows" is a 1986 song from the soundtrack of the film of the same name, performed by David Bowie and written by Bowie and Erdal Kızılçay. It was released as a single in October 1986 and released digitally in 2007.

be123dea-f4e0-41c8-86c7-e854341b9d0c.title: Frozen
be123dea-f4e0-41c8-86c7-e854341b9d0c.summary: Frozen is a 2013 American animated musical fantasy film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios and released by Walt Disney Pictures. Inspired by Hans Christian Andersen's 1844 fairy tale "The Snow Queen", it was directed by Chris Buck and Jennifer Lee and produced by Peter Del Vecho, from a screenplay by Lee, who also conceived the film's story with Buck and Shane Morris.

be1826a8-90f4-404a-8860-5cc5f334b732.title: Chernobyl
be1826a8-90f4-404a-8860-5cc5f334b732.summary: Chernobyl is a 2019 television miniseries created and written by Craig Mazin and directed by Johan Renck, about the 1986 nuclear disaster in Soviet Ukraine and the effort to contain it. Jared Harris plays Valery Legasov, the scientist who tries to establish what happened while officials deny it. It follows the firefighters, miners, soldiers and scientists who paid for the cleanup, often with their lives. Underneath, it is about the cost of lies: what happens when the people who understand a danger are not allowed to say so. It won wide acclaim and several Emmy Awards.

bea8d856-eecd-438c-8761-838b62c58cb0.title: Abracadabra
bea8d856-eecd-438c-8761-838b62c58cb0.summary: The lyrics of the song are about a man who is under the spell of a woman who has magical powers. The lyrics are suggestive and playful, with lines like “I heat up, I can’t cool down” and “Every time you call my name, I heat up like a burning flame.” The chorus of the song features the repeated phrase “Abra-cadabra,” which is a reference to the magic word used by magicians when performing a trick.

bea8e01a-b7e0-437f-8c77-abdd5c44b2fb.title: Black Horse and the Cherry Tree
bea8e01a-b7e0-437f-8c77-abdd5c44b2fb.summary: "The Black Horse and the Cherry Tree" is a song by Scottish singer-songwriter KT Tunstall. Released in 2005 as part of her debut album "Eye to the Telescope," the song gained popularity for its unique blend of folk, rock, and blues influences. The lyrics of the song convey themes of resilience and overcoming challenges. The title refers to a metaphorical black horse representing difficulties and a cherry tree symbolizing a source of inspiration or hope. Tunstall's energetic and soulful performance, coupled with the catchy chorus, contributed to the song's success.

bf36d7e7-4d90-40b8-adb2-54bd6f2f83d0.title: Tess of the d'Urbervilles
bf36d7e7-4d90-40b8-adb2-54bd6f2f83d0.summary:
This is the story of Tess Durbeyfield, a young woman living in rural England during the late 19th century. After learning of her family's noble lineage, Tess's parents send her to claim kinship with the wealthy d'Urberville family. There, she meets Alec d'Urberville, who seduces her and leads to her downfall.

After becoming pregnant and giving birth to a child who dies in infancy, Tess seeks work as a milkmaid and encounters Angel Clare, a kind and idealistic young man. They fall in love and marry, but Tess struggles with guilt over her past. When she confesses her past to Angel on their wedding night, he rejects her, unable to accept her previous relationship with Alec.

Devastated, Tess returns to Alec, who has remained infatuated with her. Their relationship leads to further tragedy when Alec becomes possessive and manipulative. In a desperate act, Tess murders Alec and is eventually captured and executed.

bfd1f8d9-ae77-504a-b970-096f41916b81.title: Live at Benaroya Hall with the Seattle Symphony
bfd1f8d9-ae77-504a-b970-096f41916b81.summary: A live album by Brandi Carlile, released May 3, 2011 by Columbia Records, recorded on November 19-21, 2010 at two sold-out concerts at Benaroya Hall in Seattle with the Seattle Symphony. Carlile had wanted her fourth release to be a live album and chose the hall because she had played there with the symphony in 2008. Her band, with Phil and Tim Hanseroth, plays alongside a roughly 30-member orchestra, using arrangements by Paul Buckmaster and others. The set mixes songs from her albums The Story and Give Up the Ghost, including a seven-minute 'Pride and Joy,' with three covers: Elton John and Bernie Taupin's 'Sixty Years On,' Paul Simon's 'The Sound of Silence' (sung by the Hanseroth brothers) and Leonard Cohen's 'Hallelujah.' It reached number 63 on the Billboard 200. Reviewers praised the orchestral arrangements and her raw voice, though one found her singing haphazard in places.

c00d9fb1-0271-512c-9993-427790e40cd3.title: Ruby Finds a Worry
c00d9fb1-0271-512c-9993-427790e40cd3.summary: Ruby Finds a Worry is a picture book written and illustrated by Tom Percival, one of the Big Bright Feelings books, published in the United States by Bloomsbury in 2019 (the UK title is Ruby's Worry). Ruby is a cheerful, adventurous girl until she finds a Worry, a small yellow blob with a frowning brow. At first it hardly matters, but it grows the more she thinks about it, and the pages lose their color as it takes over. She tries to ignore it and stops enjoying the things she loves. At the playground she meets a boy with a sky-blue Worry of his own. When she asks what is bothering him and he talks, his Worry shrinks, and when she shares hers, it shrinks too. The book ends with Ruby knowing that she can handle worries by talking about them. Kirkus lists it for ages 4 to 6 and calls it a good way to start conversations about feelings.

c154bfe1-4a16-4366-ac52-01e8cad2b440.title: Pinball Wizard
c154bfe1-4a16-4366-ac52-01e8cad2b440.summary: "Pinball Wizard" tells the story of a young man named Tommy Walker, who becomes a "Pinball Wizard" and gains fame and admiration for his exceptional skill at playing pinball. The lyrics describe the excitement and amazement of those who witness Tommy's pinball skills, portraying him as a mysterious and almost otherworldly figure.

c15a7f35-71f6-48c0-992e-223f03c79d54.title: Maybe
c15a7f35-71f6-48c0-992e-223f03c79d54.summary: A story about all the possibilities ahead of you. It’s for who you are right now and it’s for all the magical, unbounded potential you hold inside. With its beautiful visual storytelling and timeless message, Maybe is an inspiring story for kids of all ages.

c238fe1a-dc79-5168-b7cc-a91167c653fc.title: Laff-o-tronic Monster Jokes!
c238fe1a-dc79-5168-b7cc-a91167c653fc.summary: Laff-o-tronic Monster Jokes! is a joke book by Michael Dahl, who bills himself on the title page as 'The Mad Scientist of Laffology,' illustrated by Daryll Collins and Doug Holgate. Stone Arch Books, a Capstone imprint, published it in 2014 in its Laff-o-tronic joke books series. Library catalogs describe it as a collection of jokes all about monsters, from Bigfoot to werewolves, and give it about 91 pages, chiefly illustrations. The Library of Congress files it under Monsters, Juvenile humor. It is a book to dip into, read aloud and try out on a friend, and its pictures carry much of the fun. It is a different book from Dahl's earlier Monster Laughs (2003) and his later Silly Jokes About Monsters (2022).

c260c163-6a60-4324-91c2-f03eb9c2e236.title: Cherry Pie
c260c163-6a60-4324-91c2-f03eb9c2e236.summary: "Cherry Pie" by Warrant is a song that expresses the singer's intense attraction and lust for a woman who is sweet and irresistible, but also elusive and unpredictable123. The cherry pie is a metaphor for his passion for her and his hope to have a taste of her love. The song describes their adventurous and spontaneous encounters in various places, but also hints at the uncertainty and risk of their relationship.

c2815adf-4694-4714-92a9-36115893494a.title: Don't Stop Believin'
c2815adf-4694-4714-92a9-36115893494a.summary: "Don't Stop Believin'" is a classic rock song by Journey, released in 1981. The song narrates the story of two characters—a small-town girl and a city boy—who meet on a journey. They are on a quest for fulfillment and excitement, symbolizing the broader human experience of seeking dreams and aspirations. The lyrics reflect themes of hope, perseverance, and the pursuit of happiness despite challenges. The song's chorus encourages listeners to "hold on to that feeling" and not to give up on their dreams, making it an anthem of optimism and resilience. The song's memorable melody and powerful message have made it an enduring favorite.

c2fbaeaf-e65b-438f-8c00-0d9d54d6e778.title: Walking on Sunshine
c2fbaeaf-e65b-438f-8c00-0d9d54d6e778.summary: “Walking on Sunshine” is a fun optimistic song. It describes the sheer joy and happiness that can be found in life’s simple pleasures. The song serves as a reminder that no matter what challenges are faced, there is always the power to choose happiness. It encourages us to embrace and focus on the good in our lives instead of negativity.

c313403e-d6a3-45ad-b516-617bfa5d906b.title: Tomato Soup
c313403e-d6a3-45ad-b516-617bfa5d906b.summary: When Baby Mouse catches a cold, she finds a mischievous way to avoid taking her medicine.

c318be53-fc70-42d9-a9bf-37697927fa43.title: When I was little: A four-year-old's memoir of her youth.
c318be53-fc70-42d9-a9bf-37697927fa43.summary: A four-year-old describes how she has changed since she was a baby. When I was little, I could hardly do anything. But now I can do lots of things, like braid my own hair and go to nursery school. I'm not a baby anymore. I'm me! Jamie Lee Curtis and Laura Cornell perfectly capture a little girl's simple, childlike celebration of herself, as she looks back on her childhood from the lofty height of four and a half years.

c36b0086-0b7b-4736-9f9d-8880a162e57c.title: Rogue Protocol: The Murderbot Diaries, 3
c36b0086-0b7b-4736-9f9d-8880a162e57c.summary: Sci-Fi's favorite antisocial AI is back on a mission. The case against the too-big-to-fail GrayChris Corporation is floundering, and more importantly, authorities are beginning to ask more questions about where Dr. Mensah's SecUnit is. And Murderbot would rather those questions went away. For good.

c3a032d2-1464-41dc-931d-c7db6cd9f28e.title: Lazy Ozzie
c3a032d2-1464-41dc-931d-c7db6cd9f28e.summary: This is the story of a lazy koala named Ozzie who prefers lounging in his eucalyptus tree to doing any sort of work or helping out. However, when a group of other animals needs his assistance to save their habitat from destruction, Ozzie must overcome his laziness and rise to the occasion.

c3e9a231-7811-5c8a-8af1-3a0035af2469.title: The Battle of the Labyrinth
c3e9a231-7811-5c8a-8af1-3a0035af2469.summary: The Battle of the Labyrinth is the fourth book in Rick Riordan's Percy Jackson and the Olympians series, first published in 2008 by Hyperion Books for Children. Percy, now fourteen, learns that the Labyrinth, a maze built by the legendary inventor Daedalus, has an entrance near Camp Half-Blood, and that the Titan lord Kronos's army could use it to attack the camp. Percy, Annabeth, Grover and Tyson enter the maze to persuade Daedalus not to help the Titans, joined by Rachel, a mortal who can see through the Mist that hides the gods' world. Underneath the adventure, the book is about friendship and loyalty, grief, and how people face death. Kirkus judged it the strongest of the series so far, and it can be read on its own.

c4709cf9-4b59-4785-b00d-d2e8b726bdbc.title: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
c4709cf9-4b59-4785-b00d-d2e8b726bdbc.summary: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory is a 1964 children's novel by British author Roald Dahl. The story features the adventures of young Charlie Bucket inside the chocolate factory of eccentric chocolatier Willy Wonka.

c4b086a7-339a-4fda-b0cc-e22bcbeb920b.title: Uptown Funk
c4b086a7-339a-4fda-b0cc-e22bcbeb920b.summary: The lyrics describe a confident and stylish individual who is ready to hit the town, turn heads, and have a good time. "Uptown Funk" celebrates self-assurance, swagger, and the joy of dancing and partying.  The song talks about having a good time, letting loose, and dancing. The lyrics are filled with references to dancing, music, and the excitement of a night out on the town. It’s a feel-good, upbeat song that aims to get people in the mood to have fun and enjoy themselves this contributed to the song's massive commercial success and its status as a dancefloor anthem.

c56460d7-ea85-5506-a458-5fb72e70edce.title: Pope Leo's AI Warning, UFC at the White House, and CBS Shakeups
c56460d7-ea85-5506-a458-5fb72e70edce.summary: Episode 721 of Pivot, released May 29, 2026, in which technology journalist Kara Swisher and NYU marketing professor Scott Galloway talk through the week's news in business, technology and politics. The heart of the 79-minute show is their conversation about Pope Leo XIV's first encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, published four days earlier. It argues that human dignity should be the test for artificial intelligence, and the hosts discuss who controls the technology, what automation means for workers, and what easy answers from AI may take away from young people's learning. They also cover a delayed White House order on AI, the cost of AI inside companies, the planned UFC event on the White House lawn, and changes at CBS's 60 Minutes. It is opinionated commentary, not reporting, and it is rated Explicit. Pivot itself began in 2018 and appears every Tuesday and Friday.

c6000707-d56b-56b5-84b1-de0fda3bcbaf.title: Project Hail Mary
c6000707-d56b-56b5-84b1-de0fda3bcbaf.summary: A 2026 science-fiction film directed by Phil Lord and Christopher Miller from Drew Goddard's screenplay, adapted from Andy Weir's 2021 novel of the same name. Ryland Grace, a former molecular biologist who became a middle-school teacher, wakes aboard the spacecraft Hail Mary with amnesia and learns he is the sole survivor of a mission to the Tau Ceti system. Flashbacks show why: a microbe called astrophage is dimming the Sun and threatening a deep freeze on Earth. Far from home, Grace meets Rocky, an alien engineer, and the two must find a way to talk and to work together. Ryan Gosling stars, with Sandra Hüller as the taskforce chief Eva Stratt and James Ortiz performing Rocky as a puppet. It premiered in London on March 9, 2026, opened in US theaters on March 20, and earned about $685 million worldwide with strongly positive reviews. It is about friendship across differences, scientific problem-solving and hope.

c607eeac-3dac-4864-99a0-a6185f182be0.title: In Cold Blood
c607eeac-3dac-4864-99a0-a6185f182be0.summary:
The Clutter family - Herb, Bonnie, Nancy, and Kenyon are living a peaceful life on their farm in rural Kansas. However, their tranquility is shattered when two ex-convicts, Perry Smith and Dick Hickock, learn about Herb Clutter's apparent wealth and plan to rob the family.

On the night of November 15, 1959, Perry and Dick break into the Clutter home, expecting to find a safe filled with money. However, they find no safe and end up brutally murdering all four members of the Clutter family. The crime shocks the small community of Holcomb and captures the attention of the nation.

Truman Capote meticulously reconstructs the events leading up to the murders, the investigation that follows, and the eventual capture, trial, and execution of Perry Smith and Dick Hickock. He delves into the backgrounds of the killers, exploring their motivations and psychological states.

c6480f6e-8e44-5617-8cce-1cbce5d4e2ca.title: Love Letters to the Dead
c6480f6e-8e44-5617-8cce-1cbce5d4e2ca.summary: A young adult novel by Ava Dellaira, her first, published in 2014 and told entirely in letters. Fifteen-year-old Laurel starts at a new high school in Albuquerque after the death of her older sister, May. When her English teacher asks the class to write to someone who has died, Laurel writes to Kurt Cobain, whom May loved, and keeps writing to other dead artists, actors and adventurers such as Amy Winehouse, Judy Garland and Amelia Earhart. She never hands the letters in. They tell of new friends, a first love and a family pulling apart, and slowly of what happened to May and to Laurel herself. Underneath, it is about grief, guilt and the courage to tell the truth. It deals plainly with abuse, a death that may have been a suicide, and teen drinking and drugs. Reviewers praised its lyrical, honest voice while finding the ending rushed; it was a CCBC Choices 2015 title.

c74a851c-ae56-5950-903b-df11d99dd0ef.title: Bridget Jones's Diary
c74a851c-ae56-5950-903b-df11d99dd0ef.summary: Bridget Jones's Diary is a 1996 comic novel by Helen Fielding, told as a year of diary entries by Bridget, a single woman in her thirties who works in publishing in London. Each entry opens with her tally of weight, cigarettes and drinks, and she vows to find a boyfriend or learn to feel whole without one. She falls for her charming boss, Daniel Cleaver, who proves unfaithful, while overlooking Mark Darcy, a serious human-rights lawyer she dismissed at a family friends' party. Meanwhile her mother leaves her father for a man named Julio, and a time-share fraud scandal drags the family in. Bridget's close friends support her throughout, and Mark steps in to help her family. The diary grew out of Fielding's newspaper column in The Independent, and it is loosely based on Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice. It won the 1998 British Book of the Year. It is written for adults and deals with drinking, smoking, dieting and sex.

c85af050-7079-41cb-a7ef-1f403a6b4523.title: Not Afraid
c85af050-7079-41cb-a7ef-1f403a6b4523.summary: “Not Afraid” is a positive song about not giving into fear, standing up for what you believe in and keep pushing through life to achieve goals and greatness. The chorus serves as a powerful affirmation of self-empowerment, with Eminem proclaiming that he is not afraid to take a stand, face his fears, and confront the adversities that life presents. The song encourages listeners to find strength within themselves and not be afraid to tackle their own obstacles.

c95d1404-a8f8-4c9e-912a-8d126186fd79.title: Love Story
c95d1404-a8f8-4c9e-912a-8d126186fd79.summary:
