"Love Story" is a song by American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift. It was released on September 12, 2008, as the lead single from her second studio album, "Fearless" (2008). The song is known for its catchy melody, storytelling lyrics, and its theme of young love.

"Love Story" is inspired by William Shakespeare's play "Romeo and Juliet" and reimagines the classic tale with a modern twist. The song's lyrics tell the story of a forbidden romance between two young lovers who come from different backgrounds and face opposition from their families. Despite the challenges they encounter, the couple remains determined to be together, believing in the power of their love to overcome any obstacle.

The song's upbeat tempo and catchy chorus contributed to its commercial success, making it one of Taylor Swift's signature songs. "Love Story" topped the charts in several countries and received widespread acclaim from critics for its infectious melody and heartfelt lyrics. It remains one of Swift's most beloved and iconic songs.

c99832ce-a573-4b7a-a44c-925de6f2009a.title: Bioshock
c99832ce-a573-4b7a-a44c-925de6f2009a.summary: BioShock is a 2007 first-person shooter by Irrational Games, set in 1960 in Rapture, an underwater city built by the industrialist Andrew Ryan as a place where great minds would be free of government, religion and restraint. The player arrives after the city has collapsed into violence, its people ruined by a substance that rewrites their genes. Underneath, it is a game about the belief that a superior person should answer to no one, and about the choices it lets a player make - and the ones it does not. It is widely counted among the most important video games ever made.

c9f65c9b-b0a5-458f-9237-699c41cbddca.title: Immortals: Fenyx Rising
c9f65c9b-b0a5-458f-9237-699c41cbddca.summary: Fenyx, chosen hero of the gods, must use their mythical tools and skills to rescue the trapped gods of Mount Olympus and defeat the evil Typhon.

c9f96b8b-0748-4202-ae91-87f2655775b3.title: Zombie
c9f96b8b-0748-4202-ae91-87f2655775b3.summary: The lyrics of “Zombie” are primarily about the infamous Warrington bombings and the innocent victims it left behind. The song’s title is used as a metaphor to describe the dehumanizing effects of war and violence on individuals and communities. The song captures the profound loss and anguish experienced by both sides of the conflict.

cae09cf7-cb9b-5a3e-bf0f-4dc88302b55d.title: Diary of a Worm
cae09cf7-cb9b-5a3e-bf0f-4dc88302b55d.summary: Diary of a Worm is a picture book by Doreen Cronin with pictures by Harry Bliss, first published in 2003 by Joanna Cotler Books. A young worm in a red cap keeps a diary of his days: he lives with his parents, goes to school, plays with his friend Spider, and finds that being a worm has some good and some not-so-good sides. He cannot do the Hokey Pokey without legs, never needs a bath, eats his homework, and gets in trouble for teasing his older sister. Underneath the jokes, the book shows that a worm's life is odd and ordinary at the same time, and that worms help take care of the Earth. Kirkus and Publishers Weekly both reviewed it in 2003 and praised its wit. It was followed by Diary of a Spider (2005) and Diary of a Fly (2007).

cc882a8f-71a2-44fc-9bb3-76f9f0e90885.title: Stuff You Missed in History Class: The Demon Core and Other Criticality Accident

cc9ac35b-f8c5-4831-9d2a-b04832956cef.title: A Thousand Years
cc9ac35b-f8c5-4831-9d2a-b04832956cef.summary: "A Thousand Years" is a song recorded by American singer and songwriter Christina Perri, and written by Perri and its producer David Hodges, for The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1. The song was released as a digital download on October 18, 2011, worldwide, and serves as the second single by Atlantic Records for the movie. Perri re-recorded the song with vocals from Steve Kazee for the sequel The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 2 (2012). It was also produced by Hodges.

ccc506ad-00ca-51b4-9aa5-3abc317f2995.title: Tupperware: The Promise of Plastic in 1950s America
ccc506ad-00ca-51b4-9aa5-3abc317f2995.summary: Tupperware: The Promise of Plastic in 1950s America is a social history by design historian Alison J. Clarke, published by the Smithsonian Institution Press in 1999. It follows Earl Tupper's polyethylene containers from their design in the 1940s, when he meant them to promote thrift and cleanliness, to their place as a symbol of postwar suburban life. Clarke argues that the party plan, a selling system that gathered women in a hostess's home for demonstrations, did more for the company than its patented seal or its streamlined shapes. At the center of the story is Brownie Wise, a divorced single parent from Detroit who created the Tupperware party and became a company vice president. Through her, the book looks at what modern design meant in postwar America, the economic and social choices women faced in the 1950s, and the gender politics of marketing. Publishers Weekly called it a lucid and entertaining social history.

cd011f43-d99f-4b37-8a67-66bcf1361279.title: Cities: Skylines
cd011f43-d99f-4b37-8a67-66bcf1361279.summary: Create the city of your dreams as you build roads, services, and transportation to build, sustain, and expand its bounds.

cd772175-43fd-46b1-8b28-53b12f34292c.title: Crime and Punishment
cd772175-43fd-46b1-8b28-53b12f34292c.summary:
The story follows the life of Rodion Raskolnikov, a young and impoverished ex-student living in St. Petersburg. Raskolnikov formulates a theory known as the "extraordinary man" theory, which suggests that certain individuals are above moral and legal boundaries and have the right to commit crimes for the greater good.

Driven by his theory and desperate financial circumstances, Raskolnikov murders an old pawnbroker woman and her sister. However, he is consumed by guilt and paranoia after the act. The novel explores his psychological torment as he grapples with his conscience and struggles to reconcile his actions.

Throughout the story, Raskolnikov interacts with various characters, including Sonya, a young woman forced into prostitution to support her family, and Porfiry Petrovich, a cunning police detective who suspects Raskolnikov's involvement in the crime.

As the plot unfolds, Raskolnikov's inner turmoil intensifies, leading to his eventual confession and redemption.

ce163bdd-b465-5feb-9753-a8bdf755b0a2.title: Whitney Houston
ce163bdd-b465-5feb-9753-a8bdf755b0a2.summary: The self-titled debut album by Whitney Houston, released February 14, 1985 by Arista Records with Clive Davis as executive producer. Four producers share its ten tracks of pop, soul and dance: Michael Masser, Kashif, Jermaine Jackson and Narada Michael Walden. It produced three number-one singles on the Billboard Hot 100 - 'Saving All My Love for You,' 'How Will I Know' and 'Greatest Love of All' - plus the top-three 'You Give Good Love,' and it includes duets with Jermaine Jackson and Teddy Pendergrass. It was the best-selling album of 1986 in the United States and is certified 14 times Platinum there. Houston won her first Grammy, for Best Female Pop Vocal Performance, for 'Saving All My Love for You,' and the album was nominated for Album of the Year. The songs are mostly about love - new, devoted or secret - and the album closes with a ballad about loving yourself.

ce2e2cfc-e7b2-510d-9b8a-7cf6f00b8e01.title: Born a Crime: Stories from a South African Childhood
ce2e2cfc-e7b2-510d-9b8a-7cf6f00b8e01.summary: Born a Crime is a memoir by South African comedian Trevor Noah, first published in 2016 by Spiegel & Grau. Noah was born in 1984 to a Black Xhosa mother and a white Swiss father at a time when their relationship was illegal under apartheid, so he was kept mostly indoors in his earliest years. The book is a set of linked stories about growing up in and around Johannesburg: moving between neighborhoods and schools, using languages to fit in, finding ways to earn money, and above all his bond with his fearless, deeply religious mother. Underneath, it is about identity, how race and language decide where a person is allowed to belong, and how humor and a mother's determination can carry a child through poverty and violence. Its last section describes domestic violence. It won the Thurber Prize for American Humor and was a No. 1 New York Times bestseller.

ce528c1d-c1cc-5881-a31b-b5cb02e06966.title: The Hunger Games
ce528c1d-c1cc-5881-a31b-b5cb02e06966.summary: The Hunger Games is a young adult novel by Suzanne Collins, first published in 2008 by Scholastic Press. Sixteen-year-old Katniss Everdeen lives in District 12, the poorest district of Panem, a future North America ruled by the wealthy Capitol. When her little sister is chosen for the yearly Games, a televised fight among twenty-four young people, Katniss volunteers in her place. Underneath, the book is about hunger and poverty, the cost of sacrifice, and how a government can turn suffering into entertainment. It was an ALSC Notable Children's Book for 2009, opened a trilogy, and was made into a 2012 film. It is also among the most often challenged books in the United States, largely for its violence.

ce6d57b3-b142-4891-92c0-26a31f45d463.title: Walk
ce6d57b3-b142-4891-92c0-26a31f45d463.summary: "Walk" is a song by American rock band Foo Fighters, released as the third single from their seventh studio album Wasting Light. It was written by Dave Grohl and co-produced by Butch Vig.

ce8a8faa-7a65-5a5b-925b-3a918f868adb.title: 542 - Dracula Ambitions
ce8a8faa-7a65-5a5b-925b-3a918f868adb.summary: Episode 542 of My Favorite Murder, released July 23, 2026, is a scam-themed episode made in honor of the hosts' new limited series Royal Swindle. As on every episode, one host tells a story while the other reacts. Georgia Hardstark covers the Roslyn school embezzlement scandal, in which officials of a New York school district took millions of dollars, a theft that came to light after a story in the high school's student newspaper. Karen Kilgariff tells the story of Elizabeth Bigley, known as Cassie Chadwick, the Ohio con artist called the Queen of Ohio, who borrowed a fortune by claiming to be a rich man's daughter. Both cases are fraud, not violence, and both are matters of public record. The hosts are comedians, their tone is chatty and profane, and the episode is rated Explicit.

cf5c6baa-f708-4921-9cc2-8f05cff900ff.title: The Odyssey
cf5c6baa-f708-4921-9cc2-8f05cff900ff.summary: The Odyssey is one of two major ancient Greek epic poems attributed to Homer. It is one of the oldest extant works of literature still widely read by modern audiences. As with the Iliad, the poem is divided into 24 books. It follows the Greek hero Odysseus, king of Ithaca, and his journey home after the Trojan War. After the war, which lasted ten years, his journey from Troy to Ithaca, via Africa and southern Europe, lasted for ten additional years during which time he encountered many perils and all of his crewmates were killed. In his absence, Odysseus was assumed dead, and his wife Penelope and son Telemachus had to contend with a group of unruly suitors who were competing for Penelope's hand in marriage.

d0121514-17c9-56c9-9605-4e9fcc8a9044.title: Ravi's Roar
d0121514-17c9-56c9-9605-4e9fcc8a9044.summary: Ravi's Roar is a picture book written and illustrated by Tom Percival, part of his Big Bright Feelings series. It came out from Bloomsbury in the UK in August 2019, with a New York edition in 2020. Ravi is the smallest and youngest in his family, and he is tired of coming last. He has trouble keeping up at hide-and-seek, the playground equipment is too big for him, and when the ice cream runs out before his turn, his anger bursts out and he turns into a tiger. His roar gets him what he wants, but the other children back away, because no one wants to play with a roaring tiger. Ravi sees what his outburst has cost him, says sorry and turns back into a boy. Underneath, the book is about big feelings, belonging and making amends. Publishers Weekly found its family warmth clear, and its pictures change from color to gray as Ravi transforms. The publisher lists it for ages 3 to 6.

d17673c5-9607-4f39-a15b-c945d1cab74e.title: Midnight's Children
d17673c5-9607-4f39-a15b-c945d1cab74e.summary:
This story follows the life of Saleem Sinai, who was born at the exact moment of India's independence from British rule on August 15, 1947. The story is narrated by Saleem himself, who recounts his life and the lives of other children born at the stroke of midnight, each endowed with special powers and connected to the fate of their nation.

As Saleem grows up, he discovers that he possesses telepathic abilities that allow him to communicate with the other "midnight's children." He also learns that his life is intertwined with the tumultuous history of India, as he experiences the partition of the country and the subsequent political upheavals.

The novel spans several decades and covers significant events in Indian history, including the partition of India and Pakistan, the Emergency period, and the war with Pakistan. Throughout his journey, Saleem grapples with questions of identity, belonging, and the nature of power. The novel follows India's independence from British rule in 1947 and the partition that followed, and is read as a critique of colonialism and its aftermath.

d28ff6aa-c862-5875-8712-aed645084abd.title: Defy Me
d28ff6aa-c862-5875-8712-aed645084abd.summary: Defy Me is a young adult dystopian novel by Tahereh Mafi, the fifth book of the Shatter Me series, published in April 2019. Juliette Ferrars, whose touch is deadly, is supreme commander of North America, but her time in charge goes badly. When the children of other world leaders arrive, Aaron Warner tells her secrets about her family and identity, and she learns that her whole life has been built on lies. She must survive a war being fought against her own mind and remember who she was. Underneath, the book is about identity, memory, trust and love when the truth arrives late. Readers praise the romance and the twists, and it was a Goodreads Choice Awards nominee for 2019.

d3a1e259-5612-4a9b-b83e-ebd6e0ea279b.title: Crocodile Rock
d3a1e259-5612-4a9b-b83e-ebd6e0ea279b.summary: Crocodile Rock is a song by Elton John that takes a nostalgic look at early rock 'n' roll, dating and youthful independence of that era. The song is about a crocodile rock, which is a type of music popular in Australia in the 1950s. The lyrics describe a young man’s excitement about going to a crocodile rock concert. The deeper meaning of the song's lyrics is that good friends and memories can last a lifetime, and that nothing lasts forever the fun times are worth remembering.

d3f7f9ca-8772-47d7-8625-f573daca9295.title: Blank Space
d3f7f9ca-8772-47d7-8625-f573daca9295.summary: "Blank Space" by Taylor Swift is a song that delves into the theme of love and relationships. The lyrics depict the singer's experiences with love and the challenges that come with it. In particular, the song addresses the media's portrayal of Taylor Swift's personal life and relationships. The chorus of the song emphasizes the idea that the singer's "blank space" can be filled with new experiences and relationships, challenging the stereotypes and narratives surrounding her love life. Overall, "Blank Space" is a catchy and self-aware pop song that blends elements of romance and satire.

d40ea589-7231-4607-825f-10a8b43e5384.title: Classical and modern cryptography for beginners
d40ea589-7231-4607-825f-10a8b43e5384.summary: This textbook offers the knowledge and the mathematical background or techniques that are required to implement encryption/decryption algorithms or security techniques.  It also provides the information on the cryptography and a cryptosystem used by organizations and applications to protect their data and users can explore classical and modern cryptography.

d40fe9b1-55e7-5553-96b8-843a781c4987.title: The One and Only Ivan
d40fe9b1-55e7-5553-96b8-843a781c4987.summary: The One and Only Ivan is a 2020 American fantasy comedy-drama directed by Thea Sharrock from Mike White's screenplay, based on Katherine Applegate's 2012 novel and inspired by the true story of a gorilla. Disney released it on Disney+ on August 21, 2020. Sam Rockwell voices Ivan, who has been the star of a circus inside a Florida shopping mall for twenty years, run by the ringmaster Mack (Bryan Cranston). Ivan has a stray dog, Bob, for company, and Julia, the caretaker's daughter, gives him crayons. When a baby elephant, Ruby, arrives and the old elephant Stella dies after asking Ivan to keep Ruby free, Ivan sets out to do it, and his paintings help Julia win the public over. The animals are freed, and Ivan ends up at Zoo Atlanta with other gorillas. Under the credits, photos of the real Ivan tell his own story.

d42d32f5-1e0a-435e-b0b5-18c162846aa7.title: Sweet Caroline
d42d32f5-1e0a-435e-b0b5-18c162846aa7.summary: It’s about feeling joy in the moment and connecting with others. Neil wrote this song inspired by the innocence and sweetness of a young Caroline Kennedy he saw in a magazine photo. While it’s a tribute to her, it’s also an anthem of happiness and communal experiences.

d4634ff9-adcd-4a0d-9009-15e7a2daa823.title: Dracula
d4634ff9-adcd-4a0d-9009-15e7a2daa823.summary: Dracula is an 1897 novel by Bram Stoker, told through letters, diaries and newspaper cuttings. Jonathan Harker, a young English solicitor, travels to Transylvania to help Count Dracula buy a house in England and discovers that his host is a centuries-old vampire. When Dracula arrives in England and preys on Lucy Westenra and then Mina Harker, a band led by Professor Van Helsing sets out to destroy him. Underneath, it is about fear of the outsider, of desire, and of a past that will not stay buried. It created the vampire most people picture today.

d4dc3234-90ca-4e89-838d-bfd6ceba9d89.title: A Tale of Two Cities
d4dc3234-90ca-4e89-838d-bfd6ceba9d89.summary: A Tale of Two Cities is a historical novel published in 1859 by Charles Dickens, set in London and Paris before and during the French Revolution. The novel tells the story of the French Doctor Manette, his 18-year-long imprisonment in the Bastille in Paris, and his release to live in London with his daughter Lucie whom he had never met. The story is set against the conditions that led up to the French Revolution and the Reign of Terror.

d52a30a5-cce9-4a00-8e49-f417700ef266.title: Sense and Sensibility
d52a30a5-cce9-4a00-8e49-f417700ef266.summary: Sense and Sensibility is the first novel by the English author Jane Austen, published in 1811. It was published anonymously; By A Lady appears on the title page where the author's name might have been. It tells the story of the Dashwood sisters, Elinor and Marianne as they come of age. They have an older half-brother, John, and a younger sister, Margaret.

d5c18051-f0cd-50d8-b044-bafd9f88b880.title: The Giver
d5c18051-f0cd-50d8-b044-bafd9f88b880.summary: The Giver is a novel by Lois Lowry, first published in 1993 by Houghton Mifflin. Twelve-year-old Jonas lives in a peaceful community where Sameness has removed pain, conflict, color and choice, and where the Elders assign each person's work. At the Ceremony of Twelve he is chosen as the next Receiver of Memory and begins receiving, from an old man called the Giver, the memories of the world before: snow and color, the warmth of family, and also pain and war. What he learns makes him question what his community gave up in exchange for safety. Underneath, the book is about memory, freedom and the cost of a life without feeling. It won the 1994 Newbery Medal, has sold more than 12 million copies and is widely taught, while also being one of the most often challenged books in the United States. It opened the four-book Giver Quartet and was made into a film in 2014.

d653425e-4549-4acc-b487-3b7b84be1fd6.title: Railroad Hank
d653425e-4549-4acc-b487-3b7b84be1fd6.summary: Railroad Hank is headed up the mountain in his fine little train to see Granny Bett. She's feeling kind of blue. Along the way, he stops to talk to Missy May, Country Carl, Cinnamon Cobbler, and Reel-'Em-In Sam. Each friend offers up something to cheer Granny Bett, but Hank has bigger ideas. By the time he reaches the mountaintop, his train is bursting with crazy cargo! And Granny Bett has a great idea for what to do with it all.

d6d7c29a-bc80-5eb7-8ce9-e264567cddc4.title: Twilight
d6d7c29a-bc80-5eb7-8ce9-e264567cddc4.summary: Twilight is a young adult novel by Stephenie Meyer, first published in 2005 by Little, Brown. Seventeen-year-old Bella Swan leaves sunny Phoenix to live with her father, the police chief of rainy Forks, Washington. At her new high school she is drawn to Edward Cullen, a classmate who turns out to be a vampire from a family that feeds on animals rather than people. Their romance deepens while Edward fights the pull of her scent, and a hunting vampire sets his sights on Bella. Underneath, the book is about choice, self-control and a love that puts a person at risk. Kirkus praised its dangerous romance, and Wikipedia reports a starred Publishers Weekly review and a New York Times bestseller run. It opened the Twilight Saga and was made into a 2008 film.

d71a6901-2c2d-5574-8083-371605e62cc0.title: The Bad Beginning
d71a6901-2c2d-5574-8083-371605e62cc0.summary: The Bad Beginning (1999) is the first book in A Series of Unfortunate Events, written by Lemony Snicket, the pen name of Daniel Handler, and illustrated by Brett Helquist. After their parents die in a house fire, the three Baudelaire children - inventive fourteen-year-old Violet, book-loving twelve-year-old Klaus and baby Sunny - are sent to live with a distant relative, Count Olaf, who wants their family fortune. Olaf makes them work, threatens them, and forces Violet to play his bride in a play whose wedding would be legally real, so the three must use their wits to stop him. Underneath, the book is about loss, adults who do not listen, and how brothers and sisters look out for each other. A gloomy narrator warns readers that the story has no happy ending, and that warning is part of its dark humor. It was adapted in part as a 2004 film and as the first episodes of a Netflix series.

d741d30d-a7c4-4537-9206-226ffeba8f35.title: Splatoon 3
d741d30d-a7c4-4537-9206-226ffeba8f35.summary: As a squidling (a human/squid mutant hybrid), you must use your paint spraying, transformation powers, and agility to paint the world whatever color you want, so long as it's yours.

d7fbc0d9-9e7c-4c91-9d70-9d00aed75f99.title: The Death of the Heart
d7fbc0d9-9e7c-4c91-9d70-9d00aed75f99.summary:
This story revolves around a sixteen-year-old orphan named Portia Quayne, who is sent to live with her half-brother Thomas and his wife Anna.

Portia struggles to find her place in the emotionally distant and dysfunctional household, where she feels like an outsider. She forms a close bond with a young man named Eddie, who seems to understand her loneliness and vulnerability. However, when Eddie's true intentions are revealed, Portia experiences heartbreak and betrayal.

d86b3611-f2ba-43b3-9e0b-5a6768b12f0d.title: Inch by Inch
d86b3611-f2ba-43b3-9e0b-5a6768b12f0d.summary: Inch by Inch is a 1960 picture book written and illustrated by Leo Lionni. The book tells the story of an inchworm who likes to measure everything. The book was a recipient of a 1961 Caldecott Honor for its illustrations.

d8c7d08e-3193-4def-99a6-23d90b158212.title: I'm Stretched
d8c7d08e-3193-4def-99a6-23d90b158212.summary: A girl who feels stretched too thin by homework, soccer try-outs, concerns at home, and much more learns some techniques from her mother for dealing with stress in healthy and helpful ways.

d95680de-02fc-50fc-b7a7-946236e70d31.title: Fahrenheit 451
d95680de-02fc-50fc-b7a7-946236e70d31.summary: Fahrenheit 451 is a science-fiction novel by Ray Bradbury, first published by Ballantine Books in 1953 and expanded from his 1951 novella "The Fireman." In a future America where books are outlawed, fireman Guy Montag burns them for a living. A teenage neighbor, Clarisse McClellan, asks questions that unsettle him, and after he secretly keeps a book from a burning house he turns to a retired professor, Faber, and then to a band of exiles who have memorized books so they will not be lost. Underneath, it is about censorship, a society numbed by constant screen entertainment, and what is lost when people stop thinking for themselves. It won the 1954 Commonwealth Club of California Gold Medal and a 2004 Retro Hugo, and is widely taught in schools.

d966ab7d-5f53-52a5-a5ba-a6cdec4fbb20.title: Out of My Heart
d966ab7d-5f53-52a5-a5ba-a6cdec4fbb20.summary: Out of My Heart is the second novel in Sharon M. Draper's Out of My Mind series, published by Atheneum in 2021. Melody Brooks, now twelve, has cerebral palsy, uses a wheelchair and speaks through a communication device. Wanting a summer of her own, away from her family's routines, she persuades her parents to let her go to Camp Green Glades, a camp in Ohio for kids with disabilities. During one week she swims, rides a horse, flies down a zip line, makes her first close friends in her cabin, and has her first crush. She also faces fears, including a fear of the horses she loves, and finds out how much she can do when the people around her expect more of her. Reviewers describe it as a warm, hopeful story about independence, friendship and belonging.

dac2a373-0cc5-4d8a-b3ee-dedbbe6202ea.title: When Sophie Gets Angry-Really, Really Angry...
dac2a373-0cc5-4d8a-b3ee-dedbbe6202ea.summary: Follow Sophie as she experiences the inevitable and natural highs and lows of feeling angry.

db40935e-81b6-4203-bb52-5c8a8c576b68.title: Barchester Towers
db40935e-81b6-4203-bb52-5c8a8c576b68.summary: This story is the sequel to The Warden, the second novel in Trollope’s series, the Chronicles of Barsetshire. It focuses on the power struggle between Archdeacon Grantly, Mr. Slope and the Proudies as they fight for control of the diocese of Barchester. Meanwhile, another struggle is taking place for the heart of Eleanor Bold. Who will win her? The vile Mr. Slope, the idling Bertie Stanhope or someone else entirely? This is a witty and sparkling novel about greed, hate and love;

db5cf1f4-5956-4aa6-92a3-42ca58f6529b.title: Great Expectations
db5cf1f4-5956-4aa6-92a3-42ca58f6529b.summary:
The story follows the life of an orphan named Pip as he navigates the complexities of Victorian society and grapples with his own desires and ambitions. The story begins with Pip living with his harsh sister and her husband, the blacksmith Joe Gargery, in rural England. One evening, Pip encounters an escaped convict, Abel Magwitch, who demands food and a file to remove his chains. Pip helps him, but the encounter haunts him.

Soon after, Pip is introduced to Miss Havisham, an eccentric old woman who lives in a dilapidated mansion called Satis House. Miss Havisham enlists Pip to play with her adopted daughter, Estella, with whom Pip falls deeply in love. Miss Havisham manipulates Pip's emotions, fostering his desire to become a gentleman in order to win Estella's affections.

Pip's life takes a dramatic turn when he learns that an unknown benefactor has granted him a substantial fortune, allowing him to leave his humble beginnings behind and pursue a life of wealth and status in London. As Pip enters high society, he encounters a cast of colorful characters, including the kind and generous Herbert Pocket and the mysterious lawyer Jaggers.

As Pip rises in social status, he becomes increasingly disconnected from his roots and estranged from his true friends and family. However, as he uncovers the truth about his benefactor and confronts the consequences of his actions, Pip undergoes a profound transformation, learning valuable lessons about love, loyalty, and the true meaning of greatness.

db7cd97a-b1b0-5482-a0ff-5702554c2d69.title: The Glass Castle: A Memoir
db7cd97a-b1b0-5482-a0ff-5702554c2d69.summary: The Glass Castle is a memoir by the journalist Jeannette Walls, published by Scribner in 2005. She tells of a childhood spent moving with her brother and sisters from town to town across the western United States and then to Welch, West Virginia, with parents, Rex and Rose Mary, who were imaginative and free-spirited but often left their children without enough food, shelter or care. Her father's heavy drinking and his unbuilt dream house, the glass castle, run through the story. As teenagers the children help one another leave for New York City, where their parents later end up homeless. Underneath, the book is about loyalty, blame and resilience: Walls neither excuses nor condemns her parents. It won a 2006 ALA Alex Award, has sold millions of copies, was made into a film in 2017, and has also been challenged in some school districts.

dca35363-f77b-4114-9be4-302122d29e10.title: Iris
dca35363-f77b-4114-9be4-302122d29e10.summary: “Iris” is a love song relayed from the perspective of someone who is more or less unknown to the person that he has fallen in love with. The song was featured in the movie City of Angels and the singer is portraying the role of the lead character of that film, who is an angel who falls in love with a woman and is willing to exchange his immortality in order to romance her. The singer expresses a longing to be seen for who they truly are and the hope that love can overcome obstacles. The chorus, with the iconic line "And I'd give up forever to touch you," captures the emotional essence of the song. The word "iris" itself is used metaphorically to convey the idea of seeing someone clearly and being seen in return.

dda39eb6-169d-5ad3-bafe-461b04a658f6.title: Let's Go for a Drive!
dda39eb6-169d-5ad3-bafe-461b04a658f6.summary: Let's Go for a Drive! is a picture book by Mo Willems, published in 2012 by Hyperion, in his Elephant & Piggie series of books told in speech bubbles. Gerald the elephant and his best friend Piggie, a pig, want to go for a drive. Gerald thinks of one thing after another they will need, such as a map, sunglasses, umbrellas and bags, until they realize they are missing the most important thing of all. Underneath, it is a funny story about planning, disappointment and a friend who helps you change course. Kirkus called it typically elegant and entirely satisfying, and it was a 2013 Theodor Seuss Geisel Honor book.

de411a88-0d00-4b03-8af8-4e50a7c855f1.title: Perfect Soup
de411a88-0d00-4b03-8af8-4e50a7c855f1.summary:
Murray the mouse likes everything to be perfect. Naturally, his perfect meal on a perfect winter day is Perfect Soup. But Murray doesn’t have a carrot, and Perfect Soup isn’t perfect without a carrot. With the snow falling around him, Murray ventures out of his little house to track down the final ingredient for his Perfect Soup. And there’s no time for playing around—Murray is in a hurry.

The farmer will be happy to provide a carrot if Murray will haul some logs. The horse will gladly haul the logs for Murray if he’ll give him some fancy jingle bells in return. It looks like Murray just might get his carrot, but it only takes one grumpy person for a delicate chain of favors like this to fall apart. Can a friendly snowman help Murray make the soup perfect anyway?

df213621-2184-5997-87af-32fb4ee2d36d.title: Pride and Joy
df213621-2184-5997-87af-32fb4ee2d36d.summary: A song by the American singer-songwriter Brandi Carlile, the third track (4:20) on her third studio album, Give Up the Ghost, released October 6, 2009 by Columbia Records. Rick Rubin produced the album, recorded at Sunset Sound in Los Angeles, and Paul Buckmaster arranged the strings on this track. A reviewer called it the album's big, beautiful ballad, though he found its chorus lofty and repetitive. Carlile reportedly began performing it in 2007, two years before the album. Writers who explain the song read it differently - as a grown child who has lost a parent, or as longing for a parent's or a loved one's approval - so this record does not state one meaning. It is Carlile's song, not Marvin Gaye's 1963 'Pride and Joy' or Stevie Ray Vaughan's 1983 song of the same name. She was born in 1981 in Ravensdale, Washington.

dfe24487-a847-58cc-ab86-e2f630115186.title: Sunrise on the Reaping
dfe24487-a847-58cc-ab86-e2f630115186.summary: Sunrise on the Reaping is a young adult novel by Suzanne Collins, published by Scholastic on March 18, 2025. It is set in Panem 24 years before The Hunger Games. On the morning of his sixteenth birthday, Haymitch Abernathy of District 12 is picked as a tribute for the fiftieth Games, a special Quarter Quell in which each district sends four tributes instead of two. Taken to the Capitol and then into the arena, he is drawn into a plan to sabotage it, with his family and his girlfriend Lenore Dove behind him. Underneath, the book is about propaganda, who controls what people are allowed to remember, and the cost of resisting. Kirkus gave it a starred review, and a film adaptation is scheduled for November 2026.

e0e8d7bb-bbe8-41af-ba39-1fc12348e735.title: Ordinary World
e0e8d7bb-bbe8-41af-ba39-1fc12348e735.summary: "Ordinary World" is a song by English rock band Duran Duran, released in December 1992 by Parlophone, EMI and Capitol as the first single from their self-titled album (1993), commonly known as the Wedding Album. The ballad, both written by the band and co-produced with John Jones, reached No. 1 on the US Billboard Top 40/Mainstream chart, the Canadian RPM 100 Hit Tracks chart, and the Italian Singles Chart. It also peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100, No. 2 in Iceland and Sweden, and No. 6 on the UK Singles Chart. The song's music video was directed by Nick Egan and filmed in California.

e14c1b80-b1f2-5f7f-afd0-8b8242a8b616.title: Monster Laughs: Frightfully Funny Jokes About Monsters
e14c1b80-b1f2-5f7f-afd0-8b8242a8b616.summary: Monster Laughs: Frightfully Funny Jokes About Monsters is a short joke book by Michael Dahl, illustrated by Brandon Reibeling and published by Picture Window Books in 2003. The Library of Congress describes it as an easy-to-read collection of riddles about vampires, mummies and other monsters. It runs 24 pages with color pictures, and Open Library files it in the Laugh it! readers series with the note Read-it! joke books, green level, a level made for beginning readers. The cover shows a grinning mad scientist and a laughing green monster. The book turns creatures that usually frighten us into the butt of the joke, so a young reader can laugh at them and try the riddles out on a friend or family member. It is a light, low-pressure first book for a new reader. It is a different book from Dahl's Laff-o-tronic Monster Jokes! (2014) and Silly Jokes About Monsters (2022).

e17c9b98-9a60-4b34-a39d-38ca41371da2.title: Atomic Bomb Casings
e17c9b98-9a60-4b34-a39d-38ca41371da2.summary: An atomic bomb's casing, or "torpedo," protects the sensitive nuclear core during transport and contains explosives and electronics for detonation. The casing's material, such as the high-strength steel of Little Boy or the aerospace-grade aluminum of Fat Man, is designed to withstand the forces of air travel and the intense pressure and heat of detonation.

e2500ffc-0fc9-42b7-80b6-6cb617984ff3.title: Star Wars Battlefront 2
e2500ffc-0fc9-42b7-80b6-6cb617984ff3.summary: Take part in a variety of warzones throughout Star Wars history, choosing your side and picking franchise heroes to fight as or alongside.

e2f55452-e4be-4f51-8f77-5c7a69c8c5ad.title: The Crown
e2f55452-e4be-4f51-8f77-5c7a69c8c5ad.summary: The Crown is a historical drama television series about the reign of Queen Elizabeth II, created and principally written by Peter Morgan and produced by Left Bank Pictures and Sony Pictures Television for Netflix. Morgan developed the series from his film The Queen (2006) and his stage play The Audience (2013), which also focused on Elizabeth.

e3c3f417-0a66-4db8-a75e-e03bc01f2004.title: What's My Age Again?
e3c3f417-0a66-4db8-a75e-e03bc01f2004.summary: "What's My Age Again?" is a song by American rock band Blink-182. It was released in April 1999 as the lead single from the group's third studio album, Enema of the State (1999), released through MCA Records. "What's My Age Again?" shares writing credits between the band's guitarist Tom DeLonge and bassist Mark Hoppus, but Hoppus was the primary composer of the song. It was the band's first single to feature drummer Travis Barker. A mid-tempo pop punk song, "What's My Age Again?" is memorable for its distinctive, arpeggiated guitar intro.

e512e7af-dbeb-4d68-84e4-e3c2f6836388.title: Girl on Fire
e512e7af-dbeb-4d68-84e4-e3c2f6836388.summary: "Girl on Fire" by Alicia Keys is a powerful anthem that celebrates empowerment and strength. The lyrics convey a sense of self-discovery, resilience, and confidence. The central theme revolves around a woman who has found her inner fire and is unapologetically embracing her power. The metaphor of being a "girl on fire" symbolizes a state of passion, determination, and fearlessness. The song encourages individuals to embrace their unique qualities, overcome challenges, and shine brightly in their own way. With its catchy melody and uplifting lyrics, "Girl on Fire" has become an inspirational anthem for many listeners.

e540854d-bac2-4131-8d4c-bac91921e811.title: Call Me Maybe
e540854d-bac2-4131-8d4c-bac91921e811.summary: The song is written from the perspective of a girl who just met a boy and thinks he’s cute. The girl gives him her phone number and really wants her new crush to call her back. It's about love at first sight.

e54c2f4f-9725-5165-9839-ca61f1beb294.title: The Hate U Give
e54c2f4f-9725-5165-9839-ca61f1beb294.summary: The Hate U Give is a young adult novel by Angie Thomas, her first, published in 2017 by Balzer + Bray, an imprint of HarperCollins. Sixteen-year-old Starr Carter lives in Garden Heights, a mostly poor Black neighborhood, and goes to Williamson Prep, a wealthy, mostly white private school. When she sees a police officer kill her unarmed childhood friend Khalil, his death becomes national news and the media judges him harshly. Starr is the only witness, and she must decide what to say and what saying it could cost her family and neighborhood. Underneath, the book is about finding your voice, belonging in two worlds, and justice. It deals with a police shooting, grief and racism. It was a Printz Honor and Coretta Scott King Honor book, reached number one on the New York Times young adult list, was among the most challenged books in the United States in several years, and became a film in 2018.

e566ce33-6450-5b71-be63-f112e1c51e96.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
e566ce33-6450-5b71-be63-f112e1c51e96.summary: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder is a young adult mystery by British author Holly Jackson, first published in 2019 and brought out in the United States in 2020. In the American edition, set in the small town of Fairview, Connecticut, seventeen-year-old Pip chooses a five-year-old murder as her senior capstone project. Everyone believes Andie Bell was killed by her boyfriend, Sal Singh, who then died by suicide, but Pip knew Sal and doubts it. With Sal's younger brother Ravi, she interviews witnesses and keeps a project journal, finds that people she knows have been hiding things, and begins to receive threats. Underneath, it is about how a town decides who is guilty and what it costs to question that. It was a New York Times bestseller, opened a three-book series and was adapted as a television series in 2024. It includes murder, suicide, sexual assault and drug use.

e5b8ba3e-b859-4a5a-a623-ff05d0aa19f8.title: Frankenstein
e5b8ba3e-b859-4a5a-a623-ff05d0aa19f8.summary:
The story revolves around Victor Frankenstein, a young scientist who becomes obsessed with the idea of creating life. Victor successfully brings a creature to life through a scientific experiment but is horrified by its appearance and abandons it.

The creature, rejected and lonely, becomes vengeful and seeks revenge on Victor. The novel explores themes of ambition, morality, and the consequences of playing god. As the story unfolds, both Victor and the creature suffer from the consequences of their actions. The narrative is presented through a series of letters and recounts Victor's journey and the creature's experiences.

e5f59b1e-a028-4a37-b12d-af23a371de9f.title: Atomic Heritage Foundation
e5f59b1e-a028-4a37-b12d-af23a371de9f.summary: The Atomic Heritage Foundation (AHF) is a nonprofit organization originally based in Washington, DC, dedicated to the preservation and interpretation of the Manhattan Project, the Atomic Age, and its legacy. Founded by Cynthia Kelly in 2002, the Foundation's stated goal is, "to provide the public not only a better understanding of the past but also a basis for addressing scientific, technical, political, social and ethical issues of the 21st century." AHF works with Congress, the Department of Energy, the National Park Service, state and local governments, nonprofit organizations and the former Manhattan Project communities to preserve and interpret historic sites and develop useful and accessible educational materials for veterans, teachers, and the general public. In June 2019, the Atomic Heritage Foundation and the National Museum of Nuclear Science & History signed an agreement that granted stewardship of the Atomic Heritage Foundation website and all of the AHF's physical collections to the museum. The Atomic Heritage Foundation website is now run by the National Museum of Nuclear Science & History. Additionally, the museum now houses the Atomic Heritage Foundation's physical collections which have been integrated into the Nuclear Museum's own collection.

e6da1278-e7ad-45d5-93b0-6c7e7a089721.title: Demon's Souls (Remake)
e6da1278-e7ad-45d5-93b0-6c7e7a089721.summary: An ancient evil has unleashed monstrosities and demons across the world of Boletaria, and it is up to you you to overcome them and attempt to save the land.

e75b3c01-f515-43b8-9ac1-357d2b6be801.title: I Wish You Happiness
e75b3c01-f515-43b8-9ac1-357d2b6be801.summary: I Wish You Happiness empowers children to be the best they can be.

e8df5c2f-bdca-45ed-8e77-550b28bfebf6.title: Emma
e8df5c2f-bdca-45ed-8e77-550b28bfebf6.summary: Emma is a novel written by English author Jane Austen. It is set in the fictional country village of Highbury and the surrounding estates of Hartfield, Randalls and Donwell Abbey, and involves the relationships among people from a small number of families. The novel was first published in December 1815, although the title page is dated 1816. As in her other novels, Austen explores the concerns and difficulties of genteel women living in Georgian–Regency England. Emma is a comedy of manners. The limits placed on women in its time - in marriage, money and work - are part of the novel's subject, shown so the reader feels them.

e8ffb772-f087-426f-9269-f884cbd23506.title: Helldivers 2
e8ffb772-f087-426f-9269-f884cbd23506.summary: Helldivers 2 takes place in a satirical, futuristic setting in which mankind is ruled by the "managed democracy" of Super Earth. Players take the roles of Helldivers, expendable elite soldiers who fight and die to protect the rest of humanity from various enemy factions. As of now, there are only 2 enemy factions, although more are rumored to be more on the way. Helldivers 2 is a tactical shooter presented from a third-person perspective, unlike its predecessor which was designed as an isometric top-down shooter. Missions focus on cooperative gameplay between up to four players, who are encouraged to coordinate their actions and tactics to eliminate enemies and complete objectives. Helldivers 2 carries several hallmarks of the first game, including permanent friendly fire and a feature called stratagems, which summons specific tools and abilities to the team's side.

e9003cc8-aab8-507b-b7df-da3312ddfb78.title: Booked
e9003cc8-aab8-507b-b7df-da3312ddfb78.summary: Booked is a novel in verse by Kwame Alexander, published by Houghton Mifflin Harcourt on April 5, 2016, a follow-up to his Newbery Medal-winning The Crossover. Twelve-year-old Nick Hall loves soccer and would rather daydream about an elite tournament in Dallas than read, which is a problem because his father is a linguistics professor who keeps pressing him to study the dictionary he wrote. Then his parents announce they are separating, the school bullies return, his best friend Coby joins another team, and an injury takes soccer away. A school librarian, Mr. Mac, and April from the book club begin handing him books, and he finds more in them than he expected. The poems play with language, with footnotes that define the words Nick learns. Underneath, it is about family change, bullying, and how reading can hold a person up when the thing he loves is taken away. Kirkus named it one of the best books of 2016.

e90fafd4-fea6-55ad-b92a-0e8bd9b4f3f0.title: The Scorch Trials
e90fafd4-fea6-55ad-b92a-0e8bd9b4f3f0.summary: The Scorch Trials is a young adult science-fiction novel by James Dashner, published by Delacorte Press in 2010 as the second book of the Maze Runner series. Thomas and the other Gladers, who escaped the Maze, wake to find the facility where they were resting under attack by infected people called Cranks. Teresa is missing, and a boy named Aris has taken her place. The organization WICKED tells them they carry a deadly virus, the Flare, and must cross a burned-out wasteland, the Scorch, within two weeks to reach a cure. Along the way they face traps, storms, hunger and the Cranks, and Thomas must decide whom to trust. Underneath, the book is about trust and betrayal, manipulation, and whether a good goal can excuse harm. Kirkus recommends it for readers 12 and up, and a film followed in 2015.

e918e4c8-f327-4d7d-9732-baa21f94a665.title: The Grouchy Ladybug
e918e4c8-f327-4d7d-9732-baa21f94a665.summary: A grouchy ladybug, looking for a fight, challenges everyone she meets regardless of their size or strength.

e9d702e6-8677-4ba4-a734-b03282762728.title: Orlando: A Biography
e9d702e6-8677-4ba4-a734-b03282762728.summary: Orlando: A Biography is a novel by Virginia Woolf, first published on 11 October 1928. Inspired by the tumultuous family history of the aristocratic poet and novelist Vita Sackville-West, Woolf's lover and close friend, it is arguably one of her most popular novels; Orlando is a history of English literature in satiric form. The book describes the adventures of a poet who changes sex from man to woman and lives for centuries, meeting the key figures of English literary history. Considered a feminist classic, the book has been written about extensively by scholars of women's writing and gender and transgender studies.

ea756051-7770-583d-a670-155ef6829f27.title: Betsy's Wedding
ea756051-7770-583d-a670-155ef6829f27.summary: Betsy's Wedding, published in 1955, is the tenth and last book in Maud Hart Lovelace's Betsy-Tacy series. Betsy Ray comes home from her trip to Europe and finds Joe Willard waiting in New York, and the book follows their engagement and first years of marriage in Minneapolis. Joe searches the newspaper offices and finds a publicity job so that Betsy's father will approve; the couple find an apartment, Betsy struggles to learn to cook, and Joe's widowed aunt moves in, which causes their first serious disagreement. Betsy and Tacy try to find a husband for their friend Tib. When the United States enters the First World War in 1917, Joe leaves for officer training and Betsy moves back with her parents. Underneath, it is about adjusting to married life, generosity, and friendships that carry on through change. It was written in the 1950s and some modern readers find its attitudes about marriage dated.

ea76d25c-18aa-49e0-9e35-87231c5a8c96.title: To Kill A Mockingbird
ea76d25c-18aa-49e0-9e35-87231c5a8c96.summary:
The novel is set in the fictional town of Maycomb, Alabama, during the Great Depression. Scout Finch, her older brother Jem, and their father, Atticus Finch, a lawyer, are at the center of the narrative. Atticus is appointed to defend Tom Robinson, a black man accused of raping Mayella Ewell, a white woman.

As Atticus takes on the case, the Finch family faces backlash from the racially prejudiced community. The novel explores themes of racial injustice, moral growth, and the loss of innocence. Scout and Jem befriend Dill, a boy visiting Maycomb, and the three children become fascinated with their reclusive neighbor, Boo Radley.

The trial of Tom Robinson unfolds, revealing the deeply rooted racism and prejudice in Maycomb. Despite Atticus presenting a compelling defense, Tom is convicted due to the racial bias of the jury. The injustice shakes Scout and Jem's understanding of morality and fairness.

The story also involves the mysterious Boo Radley, who eventually plays a crucial role in saving Scout and Jem from an attack. This event prompts Scout to see the world from Boo's perspective, challenging preconceived notions.

eb47cc45-4e40-425a-b1a4-70908a016ec5.title: Pride and Prejudice
eb47cc45-4e40-425a-b1a4-70908a016ec5.summary:
The story is set in England during the early 19th century. It follows the life and romantic journey of Elizabeth Bennet. 

The Bennet family consists of Mr. and Mrs. Bennet and their five daughters—Jane, Elizabeth, Mary, Catherine (Kitty), and Lydia. The family's estate is entailed, meaning that it can only be inherited by a male heir, putting pressure on Mr. Bennet to find suitable husbands for his daughters.

The arrival of the wealthy and eligible bachelor Mr. Charles Bingley in the neighborhood sparks the interest of Mrs. Bennet, who hopes he will marry one of her daughters. Bingley is accompanied by his friend, the proud and reserved Mr. Fitzwilliam Darcy.

Bingley is immediately attracted to Jane Bennet, while Darcy is drawn to Elizabeth. However, Darcy's initial pride and reserved demeanor create misunderstandings and lead to a strained relationship between him and Elizabeth. Elizabeth, in turn, forms a negative opinion of Darcy based on these interactions.

As the story unfolds, misunderstandings and societal expectations play a significant role in the relationships. Jane's budding romance with Bingley faces challenges, and Elizabeth discovers the truth about Darcy's character and the role he played in separating her sister from Bingley. The limits placed on women in its time - in marriage, money and work - are part of the novel's subject, shown so the reader feels them.

ec58e5de-eb15-4ac3-8d23-e70d76f9f752.title: Enola Gay
ec58e5de-eb15-4ac3-8d23-e70d76f9f752.summary: "Enola Gay" is an anti-war song by the English electronic band Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark (OMD), and the only single taken from their second studio album Organisation (1980). Written by lead vocalist and bassist Andy McCluskey, it addresses the atomic bombing of Hiroshima by the aircraft Enola Gay on 6 August 1945, toward the conclusion of World War II. As is typical of early OMD singles, the song features a melodic synthesizer break instead of a sung chorus.

ecbde0e0-a9be-4a1c-adbb-228feb03f9c1.title: Lose Yourself
ecbde0e0-a9be-4a1c-adbb-228feb03f9c1.summary: "Lose Yourself" is a 2002 hip hop single by Eminem, written for the film 8 Mile. Sung from inside the seconds before a battle rapper takes the microphone, it opens in fear rather than confidence and builds into an argument about opportunity: chances are finite, hesitation is a decision, and the only guaranteed failure is not taking the shot. The stakes underneath are material — poverty, a mother, a young daughter. It spent twelve weeks at number one, won two Grammys, and became the first hip hop song to win the Academy Award for Best Original Song. It endures as a motivational standard because it never pretends you will feel ready.  Released in October 2002 as the lead single from the 8 Mile soundtrack, it was written for the film on its set.

ecd5544c-cf9c-5a46-8841-01063b29dec0.title: In Search of Lost Time
ecd5544c-cf9c-5a46-8841-01063b29dec0.summary: In Search of Lost Time is a novel in seven volumes by the French writer Marcel Proust, published in France between 1913 and 1927 and first translated into English as Remembrance of Things Past. A sensitive narrator whose name is never given looks back on his life: a childhood in the country town of Combray, where the taste of a madeleine cake dipped in tea suddenly brings the past back; the salons of Paris society; a summer at the seaside town of Balbec; a possessive love for a young woman named Albertine; and, years later, a party at which he finally sees what his life has been for and decides to write. Underneath, it is about memory and time, jealousy, loss, and how art can save from time what would otherwise be lost. It is known for its length and for the idea of involuntary memory. The novel deals with grief, jealousy, snobbery and antisemitism, homosexuality, and the First World War. In Ruth Ozeki's A Tale for the Time Being, a diary is hidden inside a copy of it.

ed3de3e4-b90e-4327-8e5e-68318c7258de.title: The Office
ed3de3e4-b90e-4327-8e5e-68318c7258de.summary: The Office is an American mockumentary sitcom television series based on the 2001–2003 BBC series of the same name created by Ricky Gervais and Stephen Merchant. Adapted for NBC by Greg Daniels, a veteran writer for Saturday Night Live, King of the Hill, and The Simpsons, the show depicts the everyday work lives of the office employees at Scranton, Pennsylvania, branch of the fictional Dunder Mifflin Paper Company, and aired from March 24, 2005, to May 16, 2013, with a total of nine seasons consisting of 201 episodes. The show was co-produced by Daniels' Deedle-Dee Productions, Reveille Productions and 3 Arts Entertainment in association with Universal Television. The original executive producers were Daniels, Gervais, Merchant, Howard Klein and Ben Silverman, with numerous others being promoted in later seasons.

ee8c5a51-3ef0-5ac8-b526-2dd35007373f.title: I Must Betray You
ee8c5a51-3ef0-5ac8-b526-2dd35007373f.summary: A historical novel for young adults by Ruta Sepetys, first published in 2022. In Bucharest in the fall of 1989, seventeen-year-old Cristian Florescu wants to be a writer in a country where words are watched. The Securitate, Romania's secret police, catch him with an American dollar and force him to become an informer, offering medicine for his sick grandfather in return. Told by Cristian and broken up by secret police reports, the story is about what fear does to trust inside families and friendships, and what it costs to tell the truth. It follows him into the December 1989 revolution that ended Nicolae Ceaușescu's rule. It drew starred reviews from Kirkus, Booklist, Publishers Weekly and School Library Journal and won the Josette Frank Award. It brings a little-taught chapter of recent European history to readers who were born long after it.

ee9b26a2-b504-4b33-a991-e0d3d6de14ee.title: Applause
ee9b26a2-b504-4b33-a991-e0d3d6de14ee.summary: Lady Gaga’s song “Applause” is about how many people think celebrities only desire recognition and approval. She also conveys her authenticity and the struggle to stay true to oneself in the entertainment industry. The lyrics express Gaga's love for the applause and admiration she receives during her performances. It explores the idea of the symbiotic relationship between the artist and the audience, with the applause serving as a form of validation and appreciation for Gaga's artistry.

ef58713f-0bfb-50ba-8f7d-286fcd0bf1c2.title: Plain Truth
ef58713f-0bfb-50ba-8f7d-286fcd0bf1c2.summary: Plain Truth is a legal drama by Jodi Picoult, her seventh novel, first published in 2000. A newborn is found dead in the barn of an Amish dairy farm in Paradise, in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, and eighteen-year-old Katie Fisher is charged in its death while insisting she was never pregnant. Ellie Hathaway, a Philadelphia defense attorney distantly related to the family, takes the case and moves onto the farm until the trial. Underneath, the book is about the different kinds of truth and justice held by a court, a church and a family, and what a close community will protect. It also follows Ellie's doubts about her work and her return to an old relationship. People magazine named it Book of the Week; Publishers Weekly found the courtroom scenes slow. A television film followed in 2004.

efe52f13-a9ba-469c-ab65-92bddc85d822.title: The War of the Worlds
efe52f13-a9ba-469c-ab65-92bddc85d822.summary: The War of the Worlds is a science fiction novel by English author H. G. Wells. It was written between 1895 and 1897, and serialised in Pearson's Magazine in the UK and Cosmopolitan magazine in the US in 1897. The full novel was first published in hardcover in 1898 by William Heinemann. The War of the Worlds is one of the earliest stories to detail a conflict between humankind and an extraterrestrial race. The novel is the first-person narrative of an unnamed protagonist in Surrey and his younger brother who escapes to Tillingham in Essex as London and southern England is invaded by Martians. It is one of the most commented-on works in the science fiction canon.

f08eba56-04e8-4b2c-aaba-181d87f90069.title: Civilization VI
f08eba56-04e8-4b2c-aaba-181d87f90069.summary: Sid Meier's Civilization VI is a 2016 4X turn-based strategy video game developed by American company Firaxis Games and published by 2K. The mobile and Nintendo Switch ports were published by Aspyr Media. It is the sequel to Civilization V (2010), and was released on Windows and macOS in October 2016, with later ports for Linux in February 2017, iOS in December 2017, Nintendo Switch in November 2018, PlayStation 4 and Xbox One in November 2019, and Android in 2020.

f1052674-1877-440e-a8d9-c2d2f5acf579.title: Smells Like Teen Spirit
f1052674-1877-440e-a8d9-c2d2f5acf579.summary: Smells Like Teen Spirit” is a song by the American rock band Nirvana. It was released in 1991 and became an instant hit. The song’s lyrics are often interpreted as a commentary on the youth culture of the time, which was characterized by apathy and disillusionment. The phrase “smells like teen spirit” is thought to be a reference to a deodorant marketed for teenagers, and it is used to suggest a sense of rebellion or rejection of mainstream culture.

f22aadce-ed7e-4dcf-bc57-4ee1be724267.title: Rudy
f22aadce-ed7e-4dcf-bc57-4ee1be724267.summary:
Rudy is a 1993 American biographical sports film directed by David Anspaugh. It is an account of the life of Daniel "Rudy" Ruettiger, who harbored dreams of playing football at the University of Notre Dame despite significant obstacles. It was the first film that the Notre Dame administration allowed to be shot on campus since Knute Rockne, All American in 1940.

In 2005, Rudy was named one of the best 25 sports movies of the previous 25 years in two polls by ESPN (#24 by a panel of sports experts, and #4 by ESPN.com users).[2] It was ranked the 54th-most inspiring film of all time in the American Film Institute's "100 Years" series.[3]

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 18, 1993, and was released in the United States on October 13, 1993, by TriStar Pictures. It stars Sean Astin as the title character, along with Ned Beatty, Jason Miller, Robert Prosky and Charles S. Dutton. The film had supporting roles from Jon Favreau and Vince Vaughn, being both actors' first film roles. The script was written by Angelo Pizzo, who created Hoosiers (1986), which was also directed by Anspaugh.

f384417e-2436-4f4b-98f6-43f6061d244f.title: Two Suns in the Sunset
f384417e-2436-4f4b-98f6-43f6061d244f.summary: "Two Suns in the Sunset" is the closing track on Pink Floyd's 1983 concept album The Final Cut, and Roger Waters' final chronological contribution to the band, before leaving in 1985.

f431781a-1bc9-430c-bd90-fa09eaf73d79.title: The Chrysalids
f431781a-1bc9-430c-bd90-fa09eaf73d79.summary:
This story is set in a remote community called Waknuk, where strict religious and genetic purity laws are enforced.

The protagonist, David Strorm, lives in Waknuk and discovers that he possesses telepathic abilities, which are considered mutations and are forbidden by the community's doctrine. David befriends other telepathic children, including Rosalind and Petra, and they form a secret group to protect themselves from persecution.

As the story unfolds, David and his friends face increasing danger as their abilities are discovered by the community's leaders. They must flee Waknuk to escape persecution and find refuge in the mysterious land of Sealand, where telepathy is celebrated rather than feared.

f465962e-97e4-490c-95eb-5efce3e0021b.title: The Americans
f465962e-97e4-490c-95eb-5efce3e0021b.summary: The Americans is an American period spy drama television series created by Joe Weisberg for FX. It aired for six seasons from 2013 to 2018. Weisberg and Joel Fields also served as showrunners and executive producers. Set during the Cold War, the show follows Elizabeth and Philip Jennings, two Soviet KGB intelligence officers posing as an American married couple living in Falls Church, a Virginia suburb of Washington, D.C. The couple combine their spying duties with raising their American-born children Paige and Henry.

f471e442-a89f-5f89-9abc-fdc7f176e8ac.title: Of Mice and Men
f471e442-a89f-5f89-9abc-fdc7f176e8ac.summary: Of Mice and Men is a short novel by John Steinbeck, first published in New York by Covici-Friede in 1937 and written to work as both a novel and a play. During the Great Depression, two migrant farm workers, the quick-witted George and the huge, gentle Lennie, who has an intellectual disability, take work on a ranch near Soledad, California. They share a dream of a small farm of their own where Lennie can tend rabbits, and an older ranch hand asks to join them. But the tensions of the ranch, and Lennie's great strength, which he cannot control, bring on a tragedy and a painful choice for George. Underneath, the book is about friendship, loneliness, the hope of a place of one's own, and how little power poor and vulnerable people have. It was a Book of the Month Club selection and is widely taught, and it is also often challenged in schools and libraries, for its language and its ending.

f4a4a7bd-b5bb-48af-8aff-283839d218b2.title: Epic Mickey
f4a4a7bd-b5bb-48af-8aff-283839d218b2.summary: Whisked away to the forgotten world of the Wasteland, Mickey Mouse must use his new paint and thinner powers to shape the future of this world; all the while contending with the embittered Oswald, the scheming Mad Doctor, and the monstrous Blot.

f4feea9a-9b7b-47c7-b75c-7258980c5398.title: Grey's Anatomy
f4feea9a-9b7b-47c7-b75c-7258980c5398.summary: Grey's Anatomy is an American medical drama television series focusing on the personal and professional lives of surgical interns, residents, and attendings at the fictional Seattle Grace Hospital, later named the Grey Sloan Memorial Hospital. The series premiered on March 27, 2005, on ABC as a mid-season replacement. The show's title is an allusion to Gray's Anatomy, a classic human anatomy textbook. Writer Shonda Rhimes developed the pilot and served as showrunner, head writer, and executive producer until stepping down in 2015. Set in Seattle, Washington, the series is filmed primarily in Los Angeles, California, and Vancouver, British Columbia.

f5280822-11bf-4e34-a3eb-7e63c9a4f2ac.title: National Security Archive Atomic Documents
f5280822-11bf-4e34-a3eb-7e63c9a4f2ac.summary: Founded in 1985 by journalists and scholars to check rising government secrecy, the National Security Archive combines a unique range of functions: investigative journalism center, research institute on international affairs, library and archive of declassified U.S. documents ("the world's largest nongovernmental collection" according to the Los Angeles Times), leading non-profit user of the U.S. Freedom of Information Act, public interest law firm defending and expanding public access to government information, global advocate of open government, and indexer and publisher of former secrets.

f5860259-cbf6-4678-859b-d2101526dc11.title: Final Fantasy XV
f5860259-cbf6-4678-859b-d2101526dc11.summary: Prince Noctis of Lucis and his royal retinue of his closest friends must band together after their home kingdom's destruction to claim the power of past Kings and save the world.

f5be7280-0c6b-58db-89d1-f39b9be0f86d.title: The Anthropocene Reviewed
f5be7280-0c6b-58db-89d1-f39b9be0f86d.summary: The Anthropocene Reviewed is a 2021 essay collection by John Green, based on his podcast of the same name. Each short essay reviews one part of the human-centered planet, from the QWERTY keyboard, sunsets and Canada geese to Diet Dr Pepper, Indianapolis and the Lascaux cave paintings, and rates it from one to five stars like an online review. The ratings are a joke; each essay is really a personal story, and together, arranged roughly in order of Green's life, they read like a memoir. Along the way he writes openly about his obsessive-compulsive disorder, illness and doubts about faith, and many essays were written during the COVID-19 pandemic. Underneath, it is a book about wonder and hard-won hope: paying attention to ordinary things as a way of falling in love with the world, even while the world suffers. It reached number one on the New York Times list. It deals with illness and anxiety.

f62997c1-9bb1-4484-a5e3-1af52fb617b2.title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
f62997c1-9bb1-4484-a5e3-1af52fb617b2.summary: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes is a collection of short stories by British writer Arthur Conan Doyle, first published on 14 October 1892. It contains the earliest short stories featuring the consulting detective Sherlock Holmes, which had been published in twelve monthly issues of The Strand Magazine from July 1891 to June 1892. The stories are collected in the same sequence, which is not supported by any fictional chronology. The only characters common to all twelve are Holmes and Dr. Watson, and all are related in first-person narrative from Watson's point of view.

f68e62df-b38b-4a73-9ff3-661e45a7595d.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
f68e62df-b38b-4a73-9ff3-661e45a7595d.summary: The story chronicles the rise and fall of the Buendía family over a century in the town of Macondo. It explores magical realism, blending elements of fantasy with historical events. The Buendía family experiences love, conflict, and political upheavals, and their actions are marked by a repeating cycle of successes and tragedies. The complex tapestry of characters and events illustrates the interplay of history, memory, and the inexorable passage of time.

f6a7ec70-24a8-42ae-b7f5-0201c502ce62.title: Red Cloud at Dawn: Truman, Stalin, and the End of the Atomic Monopoly
f6a7ec70-24a8-42ae-b7f5-0201c502ce62.summary:
Following the trail of espionage and technological innovation, and making use of newly opened archives, Michael D. Gordin provides a new understanding of the origins of the nuclear arms race and fresh insight into the problem of proliferation.

On August 29, 1949, the first Soviet test bomb, dubbed "First Lightning," exploded in the deserts of Kazakhstan. This surprising international event marked the beginning of an arms race that would ultimately lead to nuclear proliferation beyond the two superpowers of the Soviet Union and the United States.

With the use of newly opened archives, Michael D. Gordin follows a trail of espionage, secrecy, deception, political brinksmanship, and technical innovation to provide a fresh understanding of the nuclear arms race.

f6cff49f-4235-4e9f-ae3e-8cf5e71088c7.title: Top Cat
f6cff49f-4235-4e9f-ae3e-8cf5e71088c7.summary: Top Cat rules the house until an unexpected box arrives with someone new--and cute--inside. At first, Top Cat doesn't want to share his house and favorite things, but soon he learns that two cats can be lots more fun than one.

f6d117cb-3919-4a96-876c-7ae5be882a16.title: Gone with the Wind
f6d117cb-3919-4a96-876c-7ae5be882a16.summary: Gone with the Wind is a novel by American writer Margaret Mitchell, first published in 1936. The story is set in Clayton County and Atlanta, both in Georgia, during the American Civil War and Reconstruction Era. It depicts the struggles of young Scarlett O'Hara, the spoiled daughter of a well-to-do plantation owner, who must use every means at her disposal to claw her way out of poverty following Sherman's destructive "March to the Sea." This historical novel features a coming-of-age story, with the title taken from the poem "Non Sum Qualis eram Bonae Sub Regno Cynarae", written by Ernest Dowson.

f6fcfe77-cf9a-4754-ae3f-64e89e9dc3a6.title: The Age of Innocence
f6fcfe77-cf9a-4754-ae3f-64e89e9dc3a6.summary:
This is the story of Newland Archer, a young lawyer from a wealthy and respected family during the late 19th century in New York City. We follow as he navigates the intricate social norms and expectations of upper-class society.

Newland is engaged to May Welland, a beautiful and proper young woman who represents the epitome of innocence and conformity to societal standards. However, their engagement is disrupted with the arrival of May's cousin, Countess Ellen Olenska, who has fled an unhappy marriage in Europe.

Ellen's unconventional behavior and independent spirit captivate Newland, leading him to question the suffocating conventions of his society and his own feelings for May. Despite his growing attraction to Ellen, Newland is torn between his duty to his family and his desire for personal fulfillment.

As Newland grapples with his emotions, he must navigate the rigid social hierarchy of New York's elite and the expectations placed upon him by his family and society. Ultimately, he must decide whether to pursue a life of conformity and stability with May or risk everything for the possibility of true love and personal freedom with Ellen.

f70b950b-60b4-50f8-99af-9029c1383b16.title: The Canterbury Tales
f70b950b-60b4-50f8-99af-9029c1383b16.year: 1992 (this audio recording, Recorded Books, release date 10/01/1992). The work itself was written 1387-1400 and first printed by William Caxton in 1476.
f70b950b-60b4-50f8-99af-9029c1383b16.summary: The Canterbury Tales is a long poem by Geoffrey Chaucer, written in Middle English between 1387 and 1400 and left unfinished. Tri-County holds the audiobook: an unabridged Recorded Books production from 1992 (12 CDs, about 13 hours, various narrators) in which Professor Michael Murphy updated the spelling and pronunciation of Chaucer's English while leaving its grammar and words as written; it includes twelve of the tales. About thirty travelers meet at the Tabard Inn in Southwark and ride to Canterbury to visit the shrine of Saint Thomas Becket. Their host, the innkeeper Harry Bailly, proposes a storytelling contest, and the tales that follow, from a knight's romance to a miller's comic story, show people of every rank and trade. Underneath, it is a portrait of medieval life, its faith and its failings. Some tales are bawdy or violent.

f72ffeab-63d3-4a98-85f0-a81bc91cc60b.title: Scandal
f72ffeab-63d3-4a98-85f0-a81bc91cc60b.summary: Scandal is an American political thriller television series starring Kerry Washington. Created by Shonda Rhimes, it aired on ABC from April 5, 2012, until April 19, 2018, for 124 episodes over seven seasons. Kerry Washington's character, Olivia Pope, is partially based on former George H. W. Bush administration press aide Judy Smith, who served as a co-executive producer.

f784074b-72ad-410c-b0fb-be047299c518.title: If You Give A Pig A Pancake
f784074b-72ad-410c-b0fb-be047299c518.summary: One thing leads to another when you give a pig a pancake

f7b52a71-4f6a-5845-97ac-2e4783da7160.title: Otherwise Known as Sheila the Great
f7b52a71-4f6a-5845-97ac-2e4783da7160.summary: Otherwise Known as Sheila the Great is a novel for young readers by Judy Blume, published by E. P. Dutton in 1972 with a cover by Roy Doty. It is the second Fudge book and the first to put Peter Hatcher's rival, Sheila Tubman, at the center. Ten-year-old Sheila spends a summer in Tarrytown, New York. She acts confident, but she secretly fears dogs, spiders and the water and does not want to admit it. At day camp she meets Merle 'Mouse' Ellis, takes swimming lessons and starts a camp newspaper. After a sleepover goes wrong, she learns that her friends see more than she thinks. Kirkus Reviews praised Blume's eye for childhood customs and found Sheila's worries about her image funny and easy to recognize. Blume says Sheila shares her own childhood fears. The Library of Congress files it under Self-acceptance and Friendship.

f7e7ab85-b3ea-40a5-8242-6fec07620175.title: Dawn of the Planet of the Apes
f7e7ab85-b3ea-40a5-8242-6fec07620175.summary: Taking place 10 years after the events of the first film (Rise of the Planet of the Apes), this move follows Caesar leads a colony of apes in an effort to co-exist with humans.

f8818dae-30dc-407a-85a9-1d5a24863427.title: Grumpy Cat
f8818dae-30dc-407a-85a9-1d5a24863427.summary: Cat eats, sleeps, and spends his days alone. The other cats think he is a grumpy cat, but really--he's just a lonely cat. But that is all about to change when he meets Kitten

f8f94fe9-7158-54cd-8175-93433467237e.title: Thirteen Reasons Why
f8f94fe9-7158-54cd-8175-93433467237e.summary: Thirteen Reasons Why is a young adult novel by Jay Asher, first published in 2007 by Razorbill, a Penguin imprint. Clay Jensen comes home to a box of seven cassette tapes recorded by Hannah Baker, a classmate who has died by suicide. On them she names the people and moments she says led to her death, and each listener must pass the tapes on. Following a map she left, Clay crosses their town in one night, hearing how rumors, betrayal, sexual assault and the silence of the people around her built up. Underneath, the book is about how small acts of cruelty and neglect add up, and how people treat one another. Kirkus called it an entrancing character study. It has been among the most challenged books in U.S. schools and libraries, and a Netflix series based on it (2017) drew public concern from suicide-prevention groups. It deals with suicide and sexual assault.

f99c9aa1-57be-421b-b93e-f3817b7fedc2.title: Starfinder
f99c9aa1-57be-421b-b93e-f3817b7fedc2.summary: A science fiction TTRPG set in the far reaches of space, where players can assume a variety of roles and go on spacefaring adventures.

f9a1c20f-aa72-45d0-b47e-39d91c7e7647.title: Just The Way You Are
f9a1c20f-aa72-45d0-b47e-39d91c7e7647.summary: The Animals are having a party, and tired of their normal appearances, they all want to look special for the big event. They come to realize that they are special just the way they are.

fb509023-500c-50fe-bc91-39d9d4aded82.title: Looking for Alaska
fb509023-500c-50fe-bc91-39d9d4aded82.summary: Looking for Alaska is a young adult novel by John Green, first published in 2005 by Dutton. Sixteen-year-old Miles Halter, who collects famous people's last words, leaves his safe life in Florida for Culver Creek, an Alabama boarding school, hoping to find what the writer Rabelais called the "Great Perhaps." His roommate nicknames him Pudge and brings him into a close group of friends, above all the clever, unpredictable Alaska Young, and the year fills with pranks, late-night talks and a first love. The book is split into "Before" and "After," with chapters counting the days to and from a sudden loss, and its second half follows the friends' grief and their search for answers the book never fully gives. Underneath, it is about friendship, grief, forgiveness and living with questions that have no answer. It won the 2006 Michael L. Printz Award and is also one of the most often challenged books in the United States.

fb7966b2-8b1d-45ab-9b41-429246a774d7.title: Turn of Mind
fb7966b2-8b1d-45ab-9b41-429246a774d7.summary: Implicated in the murder of her best friend, Jennifer White, a brilliant retired surgeon with dementia, struggles with fractured memories of their complex relationship and wonders if she actually committed the crime

fc7e1d6c-53d7-5d48-b19d-c5b071652111.title: Reached
fc7e1d6c-53d7-5d48-b19d-c5b071652111.summary: Reached is a young adult dystopian novel by Ally Condie, published by Dutton in 2012 as the third and last book of the Matched trilogy, after Matched and Crossed. Told in turn by Cassia, Ky and Xander, it follows the three as the Rising, a rebel movement, moves openly against the Society, which steers its citizens' work, matches and memories with tablets. A plague then spreads through the Provinces, and the three race to help find a cure while asking whether the Rising can be trusted any more than the Society. Underneath, it is about the freedom to choose and the cost of a world that decides for people. Kirkus Reviews and Publishers Weekly each gave it a starred review.

fc91d76d-e20c-5372-b8e6-92e762f65274.title: Margaret Garner
fc91d76d-e20c-5372-b8e6-92e762f65274.summary: Margaret Garner is an opera in two acts by composer Richard Danielpour, with an English libretto by Toni Morrison, her first. Co-commissioned by three companies, it premiered in Detroit in 2005 with Denyce Graves as Margaret, then was staged in Cincinnati, Philadelphia and by New York City Opera. It is loosely based on the real Margaret Garner, who fled slavery in Kentucky with her family in 1856, the same story that inspired Morrison's novel Beloved. In the opera, a new owner takes a hold of the Kentucky plantation, Margaret's husband Robert is sent away, the family tries to escape toward free Ohio, and Margaret kills her children rather than see them returned to slavery. At her trial the court debates whether to charge her with destroying property or with murder. The score draws on spirituals, gospel, jazz and folk. It shows slavery's violence, a hanging, and a mother's death, and the opera departs from history in several ways.

fe1c15ff-8af2-5980-b858-508a2efbd676.title: One of Us Is Lying
fe1c15ff-8af2-5980-b858-508a2efbd676.summary: One of Us Is Lying is a young adult mystery by Karen M. McManus, her debut novel, first published in 2017 by Delacorte Press. Five students at Bayview High School, in suburban San Diego, are sent to detention, and only four walk out. Simon, who runs a gossip app that exposes his classmates' secrets, dies during detention, and the secrets he was about to post make the other four suspects: a brain, a criminal, a jock and a princess. They take turns narrating as they try to clear their names, and learn that the labels the school gave them cover little of the truth. Underneath, it is about gossip, secrets, reputation and how fast people judge. It won several state reader awards and was made into a TV series in 2021.

fe36f28d-8945-44f7-b89e-549c43325226.title: We Like to Party! (The Vengabus)
fe36f28d-8945-44f7-b89e-549c43325226.summary: "We Like to Party! (The Vengabus)" is a dance-pop song by the Vengaboys, released in 1998. The song is characterized by its infectious and upbeat tempo, making it a popular anthem for parties and celebrations. The lyrics convey a carefree and fun-loving attitude, celebrating the enjoyment of life and the excitement of being on the Vengabus, which is portrayed as a party vehicle.

fe5ed17b-0856-413f-a160-4bcf6ab8b75b.title: The Imitation Game
fe5ed17b-0856-413f-a160-4bcf6ab8b75b.summary: The Imitation Game is a 2014 American biographical thriller film directed by Morten Tyldum and written by Graham Moore, based on the 1983 biography Alan Turing: The Enigma by Andrew Hodges. The film's title quotes the name of the game cryptanalyst Alan Turing proposed for answering the question "Can machines think?", in his 1950 seminal paper "Computing Machinery and Intelligence". The film stars Benedict Cumberbatch as Turing, who decrypted German intelligence messages for the British government during World War II. Keira Knightley, Matthew Goode, Rory Kinnear, Charles Dance, and Mark Strong appear in supporting roles.
